kept.why: The additional cost to cast is sacrifice a creature or discard a card, and neither was recorded. That cost is exactly why the card is played in aristocrats and graveyard decks rather than as plain removal.

kept.name: Aerial Extortionist
kept.why: 'Whenever this creature enters or deals combat damage' had only the damage half. The second ability triggers on another player casting a spell, which trig:cast alone does not distinguish from your own casts.

kept.name: Quietus Spike
kept.why: The trigger halves a player's life total and no life loss was recorded. It read as a plain deathtouch stick.

kept.name: Ultimate Magic: Holy
kept.why: The foretold half prevents all damage dealt to you and was not recorded at all. Mass indestructible is a save for your board, which nothing said.

kept.name: Transpose
kept.why: It creates a 0/1 Wizard token and no token effect was listed, although the token's damage ability was read.

kept.name: Boseiju, Who Shelters All
kept.why: The clause that makes the card worth playing, 'that spell can't be countered', was not recorded. Without it Boseiju reads as an ordinary colourless land.

kept.name: Zombie Master
kept.why: Granting your other Zombies '{B}: Regenerate' keeps them alive through removal and combat. Only the swampwalk half was described as an effect.

kept.name: Expel the Interlopers
kept.why: You choose a number and it destroys by power. Both the choice and the power reference were missing. Not marked scope:wipe: it is power-filtered, matching the standing treatment of Elspeth, Sun's Champion and Dusk // Dawn.

kept.name: Witch-king of Angmar
kept.why: The trigger fires when creatures deal combat damage to YOU and no trigger word covered it, so the sacrifice effect had nothing causing it. 'Each opponent sacrifices' is a mass effect.

kept.name: Troll of Khazad-dûm
kept.why: Swampcycling searches the library for a land. eff:search-library was recorded but nothing said the search is for a land, which is the whole reason this creature is run as a ramp and fixing card.

kept.name: Cyberman Patrol
kept.why: Afflict triggers when the creature BECOMES BLOCKED, which trig:becomes-blocked already records. trig:blocks means this creature blocks something, which afflict never does.

kept.name: Uncharted Haven
kept.why: A land whose only ability taps for one mana of a chosen colour, carrying no mana word, no tap cost and no choice. Nothing about what it does was recorded at all.

kept.name: Sundial of the Infinite
kept.why: The ability costs {T}, unrecorded, and 'End the turn' ends the remaining phases, which is what eff:skip-phase names. eff:counter alone described the stack clean-up and not the turn ending.

kept.name: Cemetery Tampering
kept.why: The entire hideaway half was unread: it triggers on entering, looks at the top five of your library, exiles one, and the upkeep ability later plays that exiled card without paying its mana cost. Only the mill clause had been recorded.

kept.name: Welding Jar
kept.why: Regenerating a target artifact keeps a permanent alive; the list had the sacrifice cost and the keyword but no word saying what the card DOES for you.

kept.name: Ultima, Origin of Oblivion
kept.why: Two whole clauses were unread. Stripping a land of all types and abilities and leaving it with '{T}: Add {C}' is exactly the Imprisoned in the Moon shape, so eff:neutralise. The second ability is a mana doubler triggered on tapping a land for {C}, which needs both the trigger and eff:add-mana.

kept.name: Eaten Alive
kept.why: The additional cost to cast (sacrifice a creature) was not recorded at all, and it is the reason this is a one-mana exile spell rather than a four-mana one.

kept.name: Mjölnir, Storm Hammer
kept.why: The attack trigger puts a stun counter on the tapped creature; the tap was recorded and the counter was not.

kept.name: Thraben Charm
kept.why: The third mode exiles any number of players' graveyards, which is graveyard hate and had no word. Deliberately not eff:exile, which the convention keeps separate.

kept.name: One Ring to Rule Them All
kept.why: Chapter III counts creature cards in each opponent's graveyard and chapter I mills into it, so the card genuinely reads the graveyard zone. Did NOT add scope:wipe: 'all nonlegendary creatures' is a restricted selector, the same shape as Hour of Reckoning, which is a payoff rather than a symmetric wipe.

kept.name: Lost Monarch of Ifnir
kept.why: Afflict triggers when the creature becomes blocked, and the card both has afflict and grants it to other Zombies. The life loss was recorded, the event that causes it was not.

kept.name: Keen Duelist
kept.why: 'You each put the card you revealed into your hand' is the card-advantage half of this card, and the list only recorded the life loss. It is a symmetric draw engine and nothing said it drew.

kept.name: Ajani, Strength of the Pride
kept.why: The 0 ability exiles Ajani himself along with the opponents' board, and only the opponents' half was recorded. cares:lifegain because the token he makes is a lifegain payoff and the +1 gains life, so the card wants a lifegain deck rather than merely triggering once.

kept.name: Mishra's Factory
kept.why: The whole point of the card - '{1}: this land becomes a 2/2 Assembly-Worker artifact creature' - had no word. Only the mana and the pump ability were recorded.

kept.name: Collective Effort
kept.why: The third mode puts a +1/+1 counter on each creature target player controls and was entirely unread. Escalate's cost is tapping untapped creatures you control, which is an additional cost to cast.

kept.name: Nautiloid Ship
kept.why: The enters trigger exiles a player's graveyard - graveyard hate with no word for it. The combat trigger then reads the cards exiled with the Vehicle, so it looks at the exile zone as well as the graveyard.

kept.name: Archpriest of Shadows
kept.why: Backup 1 is an enters trigger. The counter it places was recorded but nothing said when it happens, so the card read as though the counter came from nowhere.

kept.name: Skyhunter Strike Force
kept.why: Lieutenant gives other creatures you control melee. The keyword on itself was recorded; the grant to the rest of the board was not, and that is the reason the card is played.

kept.name: Soulless Jailer
kept.why: 'Players can't cast noncreature spells from graveyards or exile' is a prohibition and had no word. Both named zones are what the card is entirely about. Left eff:exile-graveyard alone: it exiles nothing, but that word is the engine's graveyard-hate marker and this card is graveyard hate, so removing it would drop a real anti-synergy signal.

kept.name: Chain of Smog
kept.why: Half the card - 'that player may copy this spell and may choose a new target' - was unread; only the discard was recorded.

kept.name: Iron Spider, Stark Upgrade
kept.why: The second activated ability was completely unread: it draws a card, and it does so by removing two +1/+1 counters from among your artifacts, which makes the first ability a resource for the second.

kept.name: Grim Guardian
kept.why: Constellation reads 'whenever this creature OR another enchantment you control enters', so it triggers on itself. Only the other-permanent half was recorded.

kept.name: Spectacular Spider-Man
kept.why: The sacrifice ability gives your whole team hexproof and indestructible, which is a protection spell, and nothing said so. eff:pump is wrong: there is no power or toughness change anywhere on the card, and it made a protection card read as an anthem.

kept.name: Tenuous Truce
kept.why: The draw happens at the beginning of the enchanted opponent's end step and the timing was unrecorded, so the card read as an attack-triggered aura that also drew at some unspecified point.

kept.name: Grievous Wound
kept.why: The life loss was recorded but not the event that causes it - 'whenever enchanted player is dealt damage'. Without it the aura reads as a static drain.

kept.name: Fain, the Broker
kept.why: The second ability's cost is removing a counter from a creature you control, which is what turns his first ability into a Treasure engine. The counters going on were recorded and the counters coming off were not.

kept.name: Angel of Indemnity
kept.why: Encore's cost is exiling this card from your graveyard, and it was unrecorded, so the card's second use looked free.

kept.name: Lembas
kept.why: The third line shuffles the card from the graveyard into its owner's library. Nothing recorded the shuffle or the zone move; Golgari Thug in this same batch already carries eff:move-zone for the equivalent graveyard-to-library wording.

kept.name: Aether Hub
kept.why: "Pay {E}" is an activation cost paid by removing energy counters. Aetherworks Marvel in this same batch already carries cost:remove-counters for "Pay six {E}", so the convention is established and this card is missing it.

kept.name: Transmutation Font
kept.why: Almost the whole card was unread. It creates a token of your choice (eff:create-token, eff:choose), both abilities tap (cost:tap), the second sacrifices three artifact tokens as a cost (cost:sacrifice) and searches out an artifact straight onto the battlefield, then shuffles. Only eff:search-library had been recorded, so a Clue/Food/Blood token engine looked like a bare tutor.

kept.name: Ulamog's Dreadsire
kept.why: Ward—Sacrifice a permanent counters the opposing spell or ability unless its controller pays that cost, which is exactly the tax eff:unless-pays names. eff:sacrifice alone reads as though this card sacrifices things on its own.

kept.name: Rule of Law
kept.why: The entire card is "each player can't cast more than one spell each turn" and the only judgement word on it was scope:all, so the engine knew it affected everyone and had no idea what it did. eff:cant-cast is the stax word for exactly this.

kept.name: Golgari Thug
kept.why: Dredge 4 returns this card from your graveyard to your hand, which is the definition of eff:recur-self. Without it the card reads as a one-shot death trigger rather than the repeatable fodder a graveyard deck plays it for.

kept.name: Leyline of Hope
kept.why: It replaces every life gain event with one more life and its anthem is switched on by being 7 life above your starting total. Nothing recorded that it cares about gaining life at all, so a lifegain deck could not find it.

kept.name: Peter Parker's Camera
kept.why: Only ctr:film and a generic eff:add-counters had been recorded. It enters with counters on itself, the ability taps and removes a film counter as costs, and the effect copies a target activated or triggered ability you control — that copy is both eff:copy and, when aimed at a trigger, eff:multiply-triggers, which is the Lithoform Engine shape.

kept.name: Species Specialist
kept.why: "Whenever a creature of the chosen type dies, you may draw a card" — neither the death trigger nor the draw was recorded, so a repeatable draw engine carried only eff:choose.

kept.name: Leyline of the Void
kept.why: eff:exile-graveyard was correctly present but nothing said the card is about graveyards, which is the whole of its text.

kept.name: Eidolon of Rhetoric
kept.why: Same text as Rule of Law: the only judgement word was scope:all and the card's entire effect went unrecorded.

kept.name: Soul of New Phyrexia
kept.why: Giving your whole board indestructible is protection, which is the role this card is played for. Its second ability is activated from the graveyard, so it also cares about that zone; neither was recorded.

kept.name: Coalition Relic
kept.why: The main-phase trigger removes all charge counters to convert them into mana. Only the putting of counters was recorded, so the half that actually makes the mana was missing.

kept.name: The Gold Saucer
kept.why: Nothing on this land affects everything — it is three self-contained activated abilities (add mana, coin-flip a Treasure, sacrifice two artifacts to draw). scope:all reads as a global effect that is not there.

kept.name: Serra Paragon
kept.why: It lets you cast a permanent spell with mana value 3 or less from your graveyard, which eff:play-from-graveyard (lands) does not cover. Deliberately NOT adding eff:exile: the exile is on the granted death trigger cleaning up the recurred card, and adding it would file a value engine as removal.

kept.name: Pit of Offerings
kept.why: The enters trigger exiles up to three cards from graveyards and the second mana ability reads the colours of those exiled cards. None of that was recorded, so a piece of graveyard hate looked like a plain colourless land.

kept.name: Emeritus of Woe // Demonic Tutor
kept.why: The Demonic Tutor half searches your library and then shuffles. eff:search-library was there but the shuffle and the fact that the card is about your library were not. Not adding trig:dies: the death count is an intervening-if on an end step trigger, not a dies trigger.

kept.name: Karumonix, the Rat King
kept.why: Both are false. The card looks at the top five and puts the revealed Rats into your HAND — nothing is exiled and nothing is played from exile. eff:impulse would advertise it to an impulse-draw deck it does nothing for, and cares:zone:exile is a word scan with no clause behind it.

kept.name: Vincent Valentine // Galian Beast
kept.why: "Whenever Vincent attacks, you may transform it" is an actual transform effect, not merely the kw:transform that was recorded. And "When Galian Beast dies, return it to the battlefield tapped" brings the card back from the graveyard by itself, which is eff:recur-self.

kept.name: Gods Willing
kept.why: Granting protection from a colour to your own creature at instant speed is the protection trick this card exists to be. grants:protection records the keyword; eff:protect records the job.

kept.name: Dalkovan Encampment
kept.why: The activated ability sets up "Whenever you attack this turn, create two 1/1 Warrior tokens tapped and attacking". The attack trigger was unrecorded, so a go-wide combat land read as a mana rock with an incidental token.

kept.name: Nim Deathmantle
kept.why: Only eff:attach had been recorded on one of the most-played recursion engines in the format. It pumps +2/+2, grants intimidate, and its whole reason for existing is the death trigger: whenever a nontoken creature is put into your graveyard from the battlefield you MAY PAY {4} to return that card to the battlefield. That is trig:dies, eff:return-from, eff:do-if-cost-paid and cares:zone:graveyard, none of which were present.

kept.name: Firdoch Core
kept.why: "{4}: This artifact becomes a 4/4 artifact creature until end of turn" turns a permanent into a creature and was entirely unrecorded.

kept.name: Knight Exemplar
kept.why: Granting indestructible to your other Knights keeps them alive through wraths, which is the role the card is played for. Consistent with Frontline Medic in this same batch, which already carries eff:protect for the same grant.

kept.name: Patron of the Vein
kept.why: The second trigger exiles the opponent's dead creature before the counters go on your Vampires, and the exile went unrecorded. Not adding eff:exile-graveyard: this only ever hits creatures an opponent controls as they die, and the broad graveyard-hate word would make a Vampire deck's own graveyard plan read this as hostile.

kept.name: Shadowheart, Dark Justiciar
kept.why: The ability is "{1}{B}, {T}, Sacrifice another creature" and the tap half of the cost was missing, so a card that can only be used once a turn looked like a repeatable free outlet.

kept.name: Aetherworks Marvel
kept.why: The activated ability taps as part of its cost, and its energy is fed by permanents you control being put into a GRAVEYARD — the sacrifice-payoff half of the card that makes it worth building around. Neither was recorded.

kept.name: Council's Judgment
kept.why: Will of the council is the mechanic the card is built on and nothing recorded it, so a voting deck could not find one of the format's best voting cards.

kept.name: Stone of Erech
kept.why: Both halves of this card are graveyard hate — a replacement exiling opponents' dying creatures, and an activated ability that exiles a target player's graveyard entirely. The list carried only eff:draw, so the card's whole purpose was unrecorded.

kept.name: Doubling Cube
kept.why: The tap in the activation cost was missing, and doubling each type of unspent mana is precisely eff:multiply. eff:add-mana alone understates a card whose output scales with the mana you already have.

kept.name: Reveillark
kept.why: It only returns creature cards with power 2 or less — the power restriction is the whole reason this card is a combo piece rather than a general reanimator, and it went unrecorded.

kept.name: Take Up the Shield
kept.why: Indestructible until end of turn at instant speed is a protection trick, and the role word was missing while the keyword grant was present.

kept.name: God-Eternal Bontu
kept.why: The death or exile trigger puts the card into its owner's library third from the top, which is a zone move nothing recorded. Deliberately not eff:recur-self: it goes to the library rather than back to the battlefield.

kept.name: MacCready, Lamplight Mayor
kept.why: The first ability literally grants skulk until end of turn, and both abilities key off power thresholds (power 2 or less, power 4 or greater), which is cares:power.

kept.name: Dread Summons
kept.why: The whole payoff clause was unread: it creates a tapped 2/2 Zombie for each creature card milled. The mill is to graveyards and it hits each player.

kept.name: Haunting Voyage
kept.why: The foretold mode returns ALL creature cards of the chosen type from the graveyard, a mass reanimation rather than a targeted one (same shape as Replenish, which carries scope:all).

kept.name: Astarion, the Decadent
kept.why: The Friends mode gains life and was missing entirely; it is a modal 'choose one' trigger; and both modes read how much life was lost or gained this turn.

kept.name: Reckoner Bankbuster
kept.why: The activated ability's cost is {2}, {T}, remove a charge counter - none of that was recorded - and the ability makes a Treasure and a Pilot token. It also enters with three charge counters on itself.

kept.name: Lux Artillery
kept.why: Sunburst counts the colours of mana spent to cast the spell, which is exactly cares:mana-spent.

kept.name: Gravebreaker Lamia
kept.why: It searches the library and puts the card into the GRAVEYARD, a library-to-graveyard move; eff:search-library alone reads as a tutor to hand.

kept.name: Speaker of the Heavens
kept.why: The token ability can only be activated if you have at least 7 life more than your starting total, so the card cares about how much life you have gained.

kept.name: Alisaie Leveilleur
kept.why: Partner with is an enters trigger that fetches a named card from a library, and none of that was recorded. Dualcast keys on the second spell YOU cast each turn.

kept.name: Darksteel Reactor
kept.why: The entire point of the card - twenty charge counters and you win the game - was missing.

kept.name: Infiltration Lens
kept.why: Only the equip half was read. It draws two cards, and it triggers when the equipped creature becomes blocked.

kept.name: Phyresis Outbreak
kept.why: The second sentence was unread: each creature your opponents control gets -1/-1 for each poison counter. The poison counters go on players, and both halves are mass effects.

kept.name: Divine Reckoning
kept.why: It destroys every creature except one per player, including your own board, so it is a symmetric wrath and not a one-sided removal spell.

kept.name: Kor Haven
kept.why: Only the mana ability was read. Preventing all combat damage from an attacking creature is the card's whole purpose.

kept.name: Hour of Revelation
kept.why: Destroy all nonland permanents destroys yours too; scope:all alone does not warn a go-wide deck away from it.

kept.name: Sanctum of Eternity
kept.why: Returning your own commander from the battlefield to your hand is a bounce of your own permanent.

kept.name: Final Act
kept.why: It is modal - 'Choose one or more' - and nothing recorded that the player picks the modes.

kept.name: Angel of Serenity
kept.why: Its removal clause was entirely unread: it exiles up to three creatures from the battlefield and/or creature cards from graveyards, and the leave trigger returns those exiled cards.

kept.name: Brave the Elements
kept.why: Protection from a chosen colour keeps your creatures alive, which is eff:protect. It gives no +X/+X at all, so eff:pump is false and makes it look like a combat trick that grows creatures. It also specifically cares about white creatures.

kept.name: The Masamune
kept.why: Two granted abilities were unread: first strike while attacking, and 'must be blocked if able'. The granted trigger doubler keys on a creature dying.

kept.name: Victory Chimes
kept.why: The mana ability costs {T} and the tap cost was not recorded.

kept.name: Martial Impetus
kept.why: Almost nothing was read. It is an Aura that attaches to a creature, gives +1/+1, goads it, and pumps every other creature attacking an opponent.

kept.name: Legion's Landing // Adanto, the First Fort
kept.why: The land face was unread - it taps for {W} and taps to make Vampires - and the front face transforms when you attack with three or more creatures.

kept.name: Yes Man, Personal Securitron
kept.why: The ability costs {T}, puts a quest counter on itself, and the leaves trigger creates a Soldier token per quest counter - the token half was missing.

kept.name: Lossarnach Captain
kept.why: The trigger reads 'whenever THIS creature or another Human you control enters', so it fires on its own arrival as well as on others'.

kept.name: Stonehewer Giant
kept.why: The activated ability includes {T} and searches your library, neither of which was recorded.

kept.name: Planetarium of Wan Shi Tong
kept.why: The payoff clause was unread: it looks at the top card of your library and lets you cast it without paying its mana cost.

kept.name: Arahbo, the First Fang
kept.why: The trigger reads 'whenever Arahbo or another nontoken Cat you control enters', so it fires on its own arrival too.

kept.name: Rite of Oblivion
kept.why: Flashback lets it be cast from the graveyard; every other flashback and foretell card in this batch records that.

kept.name: Extinguish All Hope
kept.why: It destroys every nonenchantment creature including your own, so a go-wide deck must be warned off it.

kept.name: Putrid Goblin
kept.why: Persist is precisely 'brings itself back from the graveyard'; eff:return-from alone reads as generic recursion of other cards.

kept.name: Indulging Patrician
kept.why: "if you gained 3 or more life this turn" is a lifegain condition and the list had nothing recording it.

kept.name: Dancer's Chakrams
kept.why: Job select is an enters trigger that creates a Hero token; the equip grants +2/+2 and lifelink. Only eff:attach was recorded.

kept.name: Ao, the Dawn Sky
kept.why: "Choose one —" is a modal choice, and mode one looks at the top seven of your library.

kept.name: Angel of Finality
kept.why: The whole reason to play this card is exiling a graveyard and the list recorded only flying and the enters trigger.

kept.name: Crush Contraband
kept.why: "Choose one or both" is a modal spell.

kept.name: Demonic Junker
kept.why: "for each player, destroy up to one target creature that player controls" includes you, and the card rewards it with "If a creature you controlled was destroyed this way".

kept.name: Sword of Body and Mind
kept.why: +2/+2, protection from green and blue, and the damage trigger mills ten. None of the three were recorded.

kept.name: Airbender's Reversal
kept.why: Modal, and the second mode exiles a creature YOU control and lets it be recast from exile.

kept.name: Coiling Rebirth
kept.why: "create a token that's a copy of that creature" - the reanimation was recorded but the token copy was not.

kept.name: Nighthowler
kept.why: It gives +X/+X, and bestow makes it an Aura attached to a creature.

kept.name: The Restoration of Eiganjo // Architect of Restoration
kept.why: Chapter III exiles the Saga and returns it transformed; chapter I searches the library. The back face triggers on attacking or blocking, which is trig:attacks and trig:blocks - it never triggers on BECOMING blocked.

kept.name: Cauldron of Souls
kept.why: The list was three words and none described the card: a tap ability granting persist to any number of your creatures, which is how it keeps them alive.

kept.name: Baron Bertram Graywater
kept.why: "Whenever one or more tokens you control enter" - the list carried no trigger word at all.

kept.name: Teysa, Orzhov Scion
kept.why: The activated ability costs three WHITE creatures; only cares:color:b (the dies trigger) was recorded.

kept.name: Phial of Galadriel
kept.why: Two of its three lines were unread: it draws an extra card on an empty hand, and it doubles lifegain at low life.

kept.name: Desecrated Tomb
kept.why: "Whenever one or more creature cards leave your graveyard" - the token creation was recorded with no trigger.

kept.name: Animation Module
kept.why: The second ability is {3},{T} and copies a counter onto a permanent OR A PLAYER; the first is "you may pay {1}. If you do".

kept.name: Necrodominance
kept.why: Nothing the card does was recorded. It skips your draw step, pays life for that many cards, caps your hand at five, and replaces your graveyard.

kept.name: Rammas Echor, Ancient Shield
kept.why: "creatures you control with defender gain exalted until end of turn" was unrecorded.

kept.name: Scheming Silvertongue // Sign in Blood
kept.why: The sorcery half draws two cards, and the front face checks "if you gained 2 or more life this turn".

kept.name: Shadowgrange Archfiend
kept.why: Madness—{2}{B}, Pay 8 life: the alternate casting cost includes eight life.

kept.name: Mage-Ring Network
kept.why: The mana ability's cost is removing any number of storage counters; only the counter-adding half was recorded.

kept.name: Undying Evil
kept.why: It changes no power or toughness - eff:pump appears to come from the +1/+1 counter in undying's reminder text. What it actually does is save a creature that is about to die.

kept.name: The Golden Throne
kept.why: The mana ability costs {T} as well as a creature, and the life-support replacement exiles The Golden Throne itself.

kept.name: Crypt Incursion
kept.why: There is no exile cost on this card. Its only cost is {2}{B}; the exiling is the effect, already recorded as eff:exile-graveyard.

kept.name: Wall of Reverence
kept.why: The end step trigger gains life equal to a creature's power, and the list recorded the trigger and cares:power but not the gain.

kept.name: Shelter
kept.why: Grants protection from a colour at instant speed to save a creature, so eff:protect. It changes no power or toughness, so eff:pump is wrong.

kept.name: Orzhov Advokist
kept.why: The second half of the trigger stops that player's creatures attacking you or your planeswalkers, and nothing recorded it. The trigger touches each player, which is a mass selector.

kept.name: Rapacious Guest
kept.why: It creates a Food token on combat damage and neither the token creation nor the combat damage trigger was written down.

kept.name: Shielded by Faith
kept.why: The whole point of the card is re-attaching itself to each creature that enters, and eff:attach was missing.

kept.name: Tiller Engine
kept.why: It is a modal 'choose one' trigger, and the trigger watches a land you control entering, which is another permanent entering.

kept.name: Mech Hangar
kept.why: The third ability turns a Vehicle into an artifact creature until end of turn, which is exactly eff:animate and was unrecorded.

kept.name: Chittering Witch
kept.why: The enter trigger makes a Rat token per opponent and the token creation itself was missing.

kept.name: Test of Endurance
kept.why: The card does nothing except check a large life total, so it belongs to lifegain decks and nothing said so.

kept.name: The Warring Triad
kept.why: Its mana ability costs {T}, and the tap cost was not recorded.

kept.name: Eclipsed Realms
kept.why: You choose a creature type as it enters, the same clause shape that already earns eff:choose on Gathering Stone.

kept.name: Celestial Armor
kept.why: The enter trigger gives hexproof as well as indestructible, and giving both at flash speed is a save.

kept.name: Make a Stand
kept.why: A mass indestructible trick whose only job is keeping your board alive through a wrath.

kept.name: Increasing Devotion
kept.why: Flashback lets it be cast again from the graveyard, the same self-recursion Disturb already earns elsewhere in this batch.

kept.name: Archenemy's Charm
kept.why: It is a 'Choose one' modal spell and the modality itself was unrecorded.

kept.name: Gemstone Mine
kept.why: The mining counters go on the land itself. The generic word reads as a card that puts counters on other things, which would file a land into a counters deck.

kept.name: Flagstones of Trokair
kept.why: It fetches one Plains card. Nothing about it affects everything, and the word came from the compound 'Plains card' filter.

kept.name: The Endstone
kept.why: Both halves of the card were unread: it draws off every land drop and spell you cast, and it sets your life total to half your starting total each end step.

kept.name: Out of the Tombs
kept.why: The upkeep trigger puts two eon counters on the enchantment itself before milling, and only the mill was recorded.

kept.name: Eiganjo Castle
kept.why: Its second ability prevents 2 damage to a legendary creature and the card carried no effect word at all beyond making mana.

kept.name: Ghost Vacuum
kept.why: The second ability sacrifices the artifact as a cost, and the payoff reads the cards exiled with it, so it genuinely cares about the exile zone.

kept.name: Ichor Rats
kept.why: The enter trigger hits each player, not a target.

kept.name: Court of Locthwain
kept.why: Only the monarch clause was read. It exiles the top of an opponent's library to play, and while you are the monarch it casts one of those exiled cards without paying its mana cost.

kept.name: Skittering Cicada
kept.why: The cast trigger gives it +X/+X and trample, and neither the pump nor the trample grant was written down.

kept.name: Lunarch Veteran // Luminous Phantom
kept.why: The back face's whole trigger is another creature you control leaving the battlefield, and it replaces its own trip to the graveyard with exile.

kept.name: Songbirds' Blessing
kept.why: The attack trigger digs through the top of your library for an Aura and takes it. The card carried no effect word at all.

kept.name: Lord of the Void
kept.why: The combat damage trigger exiles seven cards off a player's library and puts a creature from among them onto the battlefield under your control. Only the trigger was recorded, none of the effect.

kept.name: Gathering Stone
kept.why: Only the cost reduction was read. It has a real enter trigger and an upkeep trigger that looks at the top of your library, takes the card of the chosen type, and can otherwise put it into your graveyard.

kept.name: Stinging Study
kept.why: You lose X life alongside drawing X, the same shape Blood Pact already records.

kept.name: Norn's Choirmaster
kept.why: The trigger fires on a commander you control entering as well as attacking, and only the attack half was recorded.

kept.name: Rocky Tar Pit
kept.why: It searches the library for a land, which is what cares:zone:library-land says and what Flagstones already carries. It fetches one land, so nothing about it affects everything.

kept.name: White Sun's Zenith
kept.why: It shuffles itself back into your library, which is half the card and was unrecorded.

kept.name: Rabble Rousing
kept.why: Hideaway 5 is a real enter trigger that looks at the top five cards of your library and squirrels one away. Only the later payoff was read.

kept.name: Cosmogrand Zenith
kept.why: The trigger is a 'choose one' mode and the modality was not recorded.

kept.name: General's Enforcer
kept.why: Its activated ability exiles a card from a graveyard, so it reads the graveyard zone, exactly as Ghost Vacuum does.

kept.name: Tormented Soul
kept.why: Half its text is that it cannot block, and only the unblockable half was recorded.

kept.name: Costly Plunder
kept.why: It sacrifices one artifact or creature as a cast cost. The word came from the 'artifact or creature' filter and wrongly says the card affects everything.

kept.name: Necromantic Selection
kept.why: It destroys all creatures including your own, which is the definition of a board wipe, and nothing marked it as one. That matters because the engine uses scope:wipe to keep symmetric wipes out of go-wide decks.

kept.name: Gollum, Patient Plotter
kept.why: "{B}, Sacrifice a creature: Return this card from your graveyard to your hand" is the definition of a card bringing itself back. eff:return-from was present but the self-recursion, which is the whole reason the card is played in sacrifice decks, was not.

kept.name: Starfield Shepherd
kept.why: The ETB searches your library, so cares:zone:library. The printed warp reminder says "Exile this creature at the beginning of the next end step, then you may cast it from exile on a later turn" - the card exiles itself and is later cast from exile, neither of which was recorded.

kept.name: Light of Promise
kept.why: The granted ability is "Whenever you gain life, put that many +1/+1 counters on this creature." The counters were recorded and the lifegain trigger that drives them was not, so a lifegain deck could not find this card at all.

kept.name: Phyrexian Censor
kept.why: "Each player can't cast more than one non-Phyrexian spell each turn" is a hard restriction on casting spells and produced no word. Only the enters-tapped half was read.

kept.name: Price of Fame
kept.why: "This spell costs {2} less to cast if it targets a legendary creature" is a cost reduction and nothing recorded it.

kept.name: Luxior, Giada's Gift
kept.why: Two of the three lines were unread. "Equipped creature gets +1/+1 for each counter on it" is eff:pump. "Equipped permanent isn't a planeswalker and is a creature in addition to its other types" turns a permanent into a creature, which is exactly eff:animate - and it is the entire point of the card.

kept.name: The Ooze
kept.why: Both halves make Mutagen tokens and eff:create-token was absent. The first ability triggers on a creature leaving the battlefield. It also exiles a card from a graveyard, so cares:zone:graveyard belongs beside the eff:exile-graveyard that was already there.

kept.name: Beacon of Unrest
kept.why: "Shuffle Beacon of Unrest into its owner's library" is why the Beacon cycle is played - it is reusable. Nothing recorded the shuffle.

kept.name: Naya Panorama
kept.why: It searches for a basic Mountain, Forest, or Plains and puts it onto the battlefield. That is a land fetch, and only the generic cares:zone:library was recorded, so it did not read as a mana source.

kept.name: Securitron Squadron
kept.why: Both triggers were missing. Squad's "When this creature enters, create that many tokens that are copies of it" is trig:enters-self, and "Whenever a creature token you control enters, put a +1/+1 counter on it" is trig:enters-other.

kept.name: Walking Bulwark
kept.why: The card's only activated ability produced no effect word at all. It plainly grants haste. The rest of that ability - letting a creature with defender attack and assign damage by toughness - has no word available, so I have proposed one.

kept.name: Lost Jitte
kept.why: The whole modal ability was unread apart from the untap. It is a "Choose one" (eff:choose), paid by removing a charge counter (cost:remove-counters), and two of its three modes produced nothing: "Target creature can't block this turn" and "Put a +1/+1 counter on equipped creature" (a counter on another creature, so eff:add-counters as well as the eff:add-counters-self already there for the charge counter).

kept.name: Luck Bobblehead
kept.why: "Roll X six-sided dice" is eff:random and "If you rolled 6 exactly seven times, you win the game" is eff:win-game. An alternate win condition going unrecorded is the most serious kind of omission a deck builder can have.

kept.name: Boon of the Spirit Realm
kept.why: Constellation reads "Whenever this enchantment or another enchantment you control enters". Only the -other half was recorded; it triggers off its own arrival too.

kept.name: Vizkopa Guildmage
kept.why: The second ability is "Whenever you gain life this turn, each opponent loses that much life." The drain was recorded and the lifegain trigger that causes it was not, which is the half that makes this a lifegain payoff.

kept.name: Noxious Ghoul
kept.why: "Whenever this creature or another Zombie enters" - it triggers on its own arrival as well as on other Zombies, and only the -other half was recorded.

kept.name: Darien, King of Kjeldor
kept.why: "Whenever you're dealt damage" is the card's only trigger and it was absent. The token creation was recorded with nothing to say when it happens.

kept.name: Mechtitan Core
kept.why: The activation cost is "Exile this Vehicle and four other artifact creatures and/or Vehicles you control" - exiling itself and exiling other permanents, neither recorded as a cost. "When that token leaves the battlefield, return all cards exiled with this Vehicle ... to the battlefield" is a leaves trigger and a return, both missing.

kept.name: Burning-Rune Demon
kept.why: The ETB searches your library for two cards. eff:search-library was there without the zone.

kept.name: Moogles' Valor
kept.why: "For each creature you control, create a 1/2 white Moogle creature token with lifelink" is half the card and eff:create-token was completely absent - a mass token maker that no token deck could find. Giving your whole board indestructible is also eff:protect.

kept.name: Angelic Field Marshal
kept.why: Lieutenant gives "this creature gets +2/+2". Only the vigilance half of the ability was recorded.

kept.name: Akroma, Angel of Wrath
kept.why: "protection from black and from red" - cares:color:r was recorded from that clause and cares:color:b, from the same clause, was not. One word of a pair was dropped.

kept.name: Ifnir Deadlands
kept.why: "{T}, Pay 1 life: Add {B}" is a life-payment cost and it was not recorded. The pain-land half of a land that also makes colourless was invisible.

kept.name: Liliana, Heretical Healer // Liliana, Defiant Necromancer
kept.why: Large gaps on both faces. The front's trigger ends "If you do, create a 2/2 black Zombie creature token" and exiles Liliana herself to flip her - no token word, no self-exile, no transform. The back's "+2: Each player discards a card" produced nothing at all.

kept.name: Senu, Keen-Eyed Protector
kept.why: The cost is "Exile Senu" - the card exiles ITSELF, which by the -self/-own convention is eff:exile-self, and it is a cost so cost:exile-self too. eff:exile-own means flickering your other permanents and would wrongly file a two-mana legend as a blink enabler.

kept.name: The Legend of Yangchen // Avatar Yangchen
kept.why: Chapter III is "Exile this Saga, then return it to the battlefield transformed" - the Saga exiles itself and comes back, so eff:exile-self plus the return and the transform, not eff:exile-own, which claims it flickers your other permanents. The back face triggers on "whenever you cast your second spell each turn", which is your own casting, so trig:cast-own.

kept.name: Kaya, Geist Hunter
kept.why: Only the +1 was read. The −2 doubles every token you would create, which is eff:multiply and is the card's headline ability. The −6 exiles all cards from all graveyards and creates a Spirit token for each - graveyard hate and mass token creation, neither recorded.

kept.name: Flickering Ward
kept.why: "Enchanted creature has protection from the chosen color" is the entire function of the card and produced no word. Only the colour choice and the bounce were recorded, so a one-mana repeatable protection aura read as a card that does nothing.

kept.name: Throne of Geth
kept.why: The ability's cost is "{T}, Sacrifice an artifact". cost:sacrifice is recorded and the tap half is not.

kept.name: Heirloom Blade
kept.why: The death trigger reveals from the top of your library until it finds a creature card sharing a type and puts it into your hand. That is looking through library cards and taking one, and neither the library nor the selection is recorded.

kept.name: Bucknard's Everfull Purse
kept.why: The activation cost is "{1}, {T}" and the effect opens with "Roll a d4". The tap cost and the die roll are both unrecorded.

kept.name: Orochi Soul-Reaver
kept.why: "Whenever one or more creatures you control deal combat damage to a player" is a damage trigger and nothing records it. Manifest takes the top card of that player's library to the battlefield, which is a library zone it touches and a card moved between zones. Ninjutsu's cost is returning an unblocked attacker to hand.

kept.name: Champions from Beyond
kept.why: Two of the three clauses are unread: Light Party is "whenever you attack ... scry 2, then draw a card" and Full Party is "whenever you attack ... those creatures get +4/+4". Only the enters trigger and the scry were recorded.

kept.name: Vona's Hunger
kept.why: "Each opponent sacrifices a creature", and with the city's blessing half the creatures they control. This is a mass edict hitting every opponent's board, not a single sacrifice.

kept.name: White Auracite
kept.why: "Exile ... until this artifact leaves the battlefield" carries a linked return trigger on this permanent leaving. Fiend Hunter, the same shape spelled out longhand, carries both words.

kept.name: Eviscerator's Insight
kept.why: Flashback {4}{B} means the card casts itself out of the graveyard, which is the self-recursion shape (unearth, escape, disturb) and makes it a graveyard card. Neither is recorded.

kept.name: Hidden Hideout
kept.why: The second ability gives a creature lifelink until end of turn and nothing records it. The mana ability reads your commander's colour identity, which is a real commander dependency.

kept.name: Cactus Preserve
kept.why: "This land becomes an X/X green Plant creature" turns a permanent into a creature and is entirely unread; only the mana ability was recorded.

kept.name: Soaring Lightbringer
kept.why: "Whenever you attack a player, create a ... token" is an attack trigger and only the token creation was recorded.

kept.name: Blight Mound
kept.why: The Pest token it makes reads "When this token dies, you gain 1 life", so the card is a life-gain engine and nothing records the life.

kept.name: Unlicensed Hearse
kept.why: This is one of the format's main pieces of graveyard hate and carries NO graveyard word at all. "{T}: Exile up to two target cards from a single graveyard" is a tap cost plus graveyard exile, and none of the three was recorded.

kept.name: Baldin, Century Herdmaster
kept.why: The attack trigger gives up to one hundred target creatures +0/+X, which is a pump and nothing records it. "Each creature assigns combat damage equal to its toughness" is a rule change over every creature in the game.

kept.name: Folk Hero
kept.why: The granted ability is "whenever YOU cast a spell that shares a creature type", so it listens to your own casts rather than any cast. Only the undirected trig:cast was recorded.

kept.name: The Irencrag
kept.why: It becomes an Equipment with equip {3} and a +3/+3 buff, so it attaches to a creature. The pump was recorded and the attach was not.

kept.name: Heartstone
kept.why: "Activated abilities of creatures cost {1} less" applies to every creature in the game, including opponents'. The card is a symmetric static and nothing records its breadth.

kept.name: Elder Brain
kept.why: "Exile all cards from that player's hand" is a mass exile of an entire hand, and neither the exile nor the scope was recorded; only the replacement draw was.

kept.name: Tevesh Szat, Doom of Fools
kept.why: Two whole abilities are unread. The +1 draws two or three cards. The −10 gains control of all commanders and puts them from the command zone onto the battlefield, which is a steal plus a zone move, and the minus loyalty is a counter-removal cost where only the plus cost was recorded.

kept.name: Noble Heritage
kept.why: The granted ability triggers "when this creature enters and at the beginning of your upkeep", and no trigger word of any kind was recorded. "Each player may put two +1/+1 counters" reaches every player.

kept.name: Decorum Dissertation
kept.why: Paradigm is the whole reason to play the card and none of it is read: it exiles itself, then lets you cast a copy of it from exile without paying its mana cost, every main phase.

kept.name: Bovine Intervention
kept.why: "Its controller creates a 2/2 white Ox creature token" is a second clause and the card makes a token. Only the destroy was recorded.

kept.name: Scavenger's Talent
kept.why: Level 1 is the entire early game of this card: "whenever one or more creatures you control die, create a Food token". Neither the death trigger nor the token was recorded.

kept.name: Preston, the Vanisher
kept.why: "Create a token that's a copy of that creature" is a copy effect; only the generic token creation was recorded.

kept.name: Karlov of the Ghost Council
kept.why: The exile ability costs "Remove six +1/+1 counters from Karlov", which is unrecorded, and the card is the archetypal lifegain-matters commander since its only trigger is on gaining life.

kept.name: Fiend Hunter
kept.why: The second half returns the exiled card to the battlefield, so the card both exiles and returns and the return was unrecorded, as was the exile zone it reads from.

kept.name: Indulgent Tormentor
kept.why: The upkeep trigger draws a card unless the opponent sacrifices a creature or pays 3 life. The draw is the main reason to play it and was unrecorded, as was the tax structure and the opponent's sacrifice; only the life loss was.

kept.name: Eriette of the Charmed Apple
kept.why: The first ability stops every creature enchanted by your Auras from attacking you or your planeswalkers, and nothing recorded it. The drain hits each opponent.

kept.name: Ob Nixilis, Unshackled
kept.why: "Whenever an opponent searches their library" is a library-hate condition and no zone word records what the trigger watches.

kept.name: Tymna the Weaver
kept.why: The trigger is a postcombat main phase trigger and nothing recorded the step. "You may pay X life. If you do, draw X cards" is a paid-for effect, so cost:life and eff:do-if-cost-paid are both missing. Left trig:deals-damage alone: it is loose as a trigger word but it is the only thing recording that this cares about combat damage connecting.

kept.name: Eumidian Hatchery
kept.why: The death trigger creates an Insect token per hatchling counter and no effect word said the card makes tokens at all.

kept.name: Gixian Puppeteer
kept.why: "Whenever you draw your second card each turn" is the card's main trigger and nothing recorded it, so the drain and lifegain looked like they came from nowhere.

kept.name: Afterlife from the Loam
kept.why: "For each player, choose up to one target creature card in that player's graveyard" reaches every graveyard, and the cards come back UNDER YOUR CONTROL, so it steals from opponents rather than only reanimating your own. Did not add a cost word for delve: neither cost:exile nor cost:cast-exile is clearly the right shape for an alternative cost.

kept.name: Realmbreaker, the Invasion Tree
kept.why: It mills the opponent (only the printed kw:mill was there, not the effect), the Praetor ability shuffles, and the land is put onto the battlefield under your control from THEIR graveyard, which is theft.

kept.name: Rolling Hamsphere
kept.why: Crew 3 taps other creatures you control as the cost to animate it; only the printed kw:crew was recorded.

kept.name: Secret Arcade // Dusty Parlor
kept.why: "Whenever you cast an enchantment spell" is a cast trigger with both a whose and a what, and only the bare trig:cast was there.

kept.name: Veinwitch Coven
kept.why: It triggers on YOU GAINING LIFE, which is a lifegain payoff and was unrecorded. eff:bounce-own is wrong: it means returning your own creatures from the battlefield to hand, and this returns a creature CARD from the graveyard, which eff:return-from already says.

kept.name: Screeching Scorchbeast
kept.why: "Each player gets two rad counters" is counters on players, affecting everybody, and neither was recorded. The mill trigger makes it a graveyard-filling payoff.

kept.name: Sword of Sinew and Steel
kept.why: The +2/+2 was unrecorded, and so was the protection it grants. cares:color:r was there for protection from red but cares:color:b was missing for the black half of the same clause.

kept.name: Dion, Bahamut's Dominant // Bahamut, Warden of Light
kept.why: The activated ability returns it TRANSFORMED and chapters I-II hit EACH OTHER CREATURE you control with a counter and flying, so it is a board-wide pump the list did not scope.

kept.name: Lolth, Spider Queen
kept.why: The -8 emblem is a combat damage trigger ("whenever an opponent is dealt combat damage by one or more creatures you control") and the ultimate produced no facet at all.

kept.name: Extinguisher Battleship
kept.why: "When this Spacecraft enters, destroy..." is an ETB and no trigger word was present, so the destroy and the 4 damage looked like static effects. Station puts charge counters on ITSELF equal to a creature's power, so both the self-counters and the power-scaling were unread. eff:set-pt is wrong: nothing here sets any power or toughness, the 5+ line is the card's own printed statline.

kept.name: Angel of Invention
kept.why: Fabricate 2 is an enters trigger and no trigger word was recorded, so the counters and Servos read as static. It also has lifelink itself, which gains life (same treatment Tymna's list already gets).

kept.name: Bandit's Talent
kept.why: Level 3 draws an additional card per opponent and eff:draw was missing outright. Levels 2 and 3 both check how many cards opponents hold, which is the whole point of the card and nothing said it looks at hands.

kept.name: Resurrection Orb
kept.why: The entire second ability returns the equipped creature from the graveyard to the battlefield when it dies, and the list recorded the trigger but not the recursion, so a reanimation Equipment read as a plain lifelink stick.

kept.name: Throat Slitter
kept.why: Ninjutsu's cost is returning an unblocked attacker you control to hand; only the printed kw:ninjutsu was recorded.

kept.name: Umbra Mystic
kept.why: Umbra armor keeps your enchanted permanents alive by destroying the Aura instead, which is exactly what eff:protect names, and the card carried no effect word at all.

kept.name: Nightmare Shepherd
kept.why: The token is a COPY of the dead creature, which nothing recorded, and it is made by exiling the card from your graveyard as an optional cost. Deliberately not eff:exile-graveyard: that is graveyard hate and this exiles your own card as fuel.

kept.name: Dismantling Wave
kept.why: The cycling trigger destroys ALL artifacts and enchantments, and the main half hits one per opponent; nothing recorded that this is a mass effect.

kept.name: Firemind Vessel
kept.why: The mana ability costs {T} and the tap cost was missing.

kept.name: Navigation Orb
kept.why: The ability costs {T} as well as the sacrifice, and it ends with a shuffle; neither was recorded.

kept.name: Mirage Mesa
kept.why: A land whose only ability is "{T}: Add one mana of the chosen color" carried neither the mana nor the tap cost. Nothing recorded that it produces mana at all.

kept.name: Protection Magic
kept.why: Shield counters are the game's plainest "keeps your creatures alive" effect and only the mechanical counter placement was recorded, so a protection spell read as a counters card.

kept.name: Chaos Wand
kept.why: The card carried no effect facet at all. It taps, it exiles off the top of an opponent's library, and it CASTS THE SPELL WITHOUT PAYING ITS MANA COST, which is the whole reason to play it.

kept.name: Gothmog, Morgul Lieutenant
kept.why: "Creature tokens you control have deathtouch" is half the card and no grant word was recorded, so a token-deck anthem read as a one-shot amass trigger.

kept.name: Phyrexian Rebirth
kept.why: "Destroy all creatures" with no restriction kills your own board too, which is the exact case scope:wipe is for; it had only the generic scope:all.

kept.name: Horn of the Mark
kept.why: It digs five cards deep and puts one into your hand, and neither zone was recorded next to the look-and-pick.

kept.name: Ossification
kept.why: "...until this Aura leaves the battlefield" is a real leaves-the-battlefield trigger that hands the exiled permanent back, and nothing recorded it. Did not add eff:return-from, which would misread a removal Aura as recursion.

kept.name: Idyllic Grange
kept.why: The mana ability's tap cost was missing, and "When this land enters untapped, put a +1/+1 counter on target creature" is an enters trigger that had no trigger word, leaving the counter unattached to anything.

kept.name: Virus Beetle
kept.why: "each opponent discards a card" hits every opponent, not a single target.

kept.name: Nazgûl Battle-Mace
kept.why: Two granted keywords were never recorded. The granted triggered ability watches for an opponent sacrificing (trig:sacrificed), taxes them 3 life (eff:unless-pays), and takes the card out of the graveyard onto the battlefield. Annihilator 1 is an attack trigger that makes the defender sacrifice.

kept.name: Bronzebeak Foragers
kept.why: "until this creature leaves the battlefield" is a leaves-self trigger that returns the exiled cards, so the exile is temporary rather than permanent removal. The activated ability moves a card from exile to the graveyard. It exiles once per opponent.

kept.name: Marketback Walker
kept.why: Cost is {X}{X}, so mana value is 0 off the stack and the card reads as free. It is not a cheap card at any point a player casts it.

kept.name: Pariah's Shield
kept.why: The whole card is "all damage that would be dealt to you is dealt to equipped creature instead" and the list held only eff:attach. Nothing said what the Equipment does.

kept.name: Cosmic Intervention
kept.why: Exiling your own dying permanents and returning them at end of turn is a blink of your own board. It applies to every permanent you control, not one target.

kept.name: Big Game Hunter
kept.why: "destroy target creature with power 4 or greater" reads a creature's power to choose a legal target.

kept.name: The Cruelty of Gix
kept.why: "You lose 3 life" sits inside chapter II's effect after the tutor resolves. It is not a cost being paid, so the card was filed as a life-payment card when it is a life-loss one.

kept.name: Sword of the Squeak
kept.why: The +1/+1 for each small creature was missing entirely, so the Equipment appeared to grant nothing. The auto-attach is a triggered ability on another creature entering, and "base power or toughness 1" reads power.

kept.name: Coppercoat Vanguard
kept.why: Granting ward {1} to every other Human is a real effect and the list recorded only the +1/+0. Ward resolves as "counter it unless that player pays", which is eff:unless-pays.

kept.name: Kor Cartographer
kept.why: It fetches one Plains for itself when it enters. Nothing about the card affects everything, and scope:all makes it look like a mass effect.

kept.name: Papalymo Totolymo
kept.why: The activated ability costs {4}, {T} and sacrificing itself, and neither cost was recorded. It also reads power to pick which creature each opponent gives up.

kept.name: Crucible of the Spirit Dragon
kept.why: The mana ability pays by removing X storage counters. Only the counter-adding half was recorded, so the payoff half of a storage land was invisible.

kept.name: Honor-Worn Shaku
kept.why: It taps one legendary permanent to untap itself. There is no mass effect on the card.

kept.name: Barrowgoyf
kept.why: The combat damage trigger mills and then lets you take a creature card from among the milled cards into your hand. Neither the mill nor the recursion was recorded, so the card read as a vanilla graveyard-sized body.

kept.name: Norn's Decree
kept.why: The card gives opponents poison counters when their creatures connect with you, and nothing recorded either the poison or the damage trigger. eff:unless-pays is wrong: no clause on this card offers anyone a payment.

kept.name: Erebos, Bleak-Hearted
kept.why: "you may pay 2 life. If you do, draw a card" is the entire reason to play this card and none of it was recorded. It is an optional life payment for a card, which is exactly the do-if-cost-paid shape.

kept.name: Sorin Markov
kept.why: The minus 3 sets an opponent's life total to 10, which is not damage or life loss and had no word. Both minus abilities pay loyalty, so cost:remove-counters was missing while cost:add-counters was present for the plus.

kept.name: Amalia Benavides Aguirre
kept.why: The trigger fires on gaining life, which is the whole build around her and was unrecorded. "destroy all other creatures" affects the whole board. I deliberately did NOT add scope:wipe: it fires only at power exactly 20, so treating her as a board wipe would keep her out of the go-wide lifegain decks she belongs in. cares:power is arguable for the power 20 check but reads as a power-matters card, so I left it off.

kept.name: Feral Ghoul
kept.why: "each opponent gets a number of rad counters equal to its power" puts counters on players, and only the +1/+1 counter on itself was recorded.

kept.name: Elesh Norn // The Argent Etchings
kept.why: The front face's only real ability is a tax on opponents dealing damage to you, and neither the trigger nor the tax was recorded. Chapter II's team pump and double strike were missing, transforming is on both faces, and chapter III destroys all other permanents including your own, which is a genuine wipe.

kept.name: Assault Suit
kept.why: The list held only eff:attach and the upkeep trigger, so nothing said what the Equipment grants or does. It pumps, grants haste, hands the creature to an opponent for the turn, and untaps it.

kept.name: Dawn of a New Age
kept.why: It enters with a hope counter for each creature you control. Only the removal half of the counter engine was recorded.

kept.name: Stargaze
kept.why: It looks at twice X cards and picks X, which is selection rather than a draw, and the rest go to your graveyard, which is self-mill. Both were missing. eff:draw is loose but is the card-advantage signal, so I left it.

kept.name: Séance Board
kept.why: The mana ability is "{T}: Add X mana" and the tap cost was not recorded, so it did not read as a tap-for-mana artifact.

kept.name: The Millennium Calendar
kept.why: Almost nothing about this card was recorded. It triggers on untapping permanents, puts that many counters on itself, has a {2}, {T} ability that doubles them, and the payoff drains every opponent.

kept.name: Desecrate Reality
kept.why: "For each opponent, exile up to one target permanent" hits every opponent at once, the same multiplayer-wide shape as Exhume and Innocent Blood, both of which carry scope:all.

kept.name: Clown Car
kept.why: "Roll X six-sided dice" is a die roll and nothing recorded it. mv:cheap comes from the {X}-only cost collapsing to mana value 0, which reads a card you would never cast for under 4 mana as a two-drop.

kept.name: Sorin of House Markov // Sorin, Ravenous Neonate
kept.why: Extort drains each opponent (eff:lose-life) off your own casts (trig:cast-own). The flip clause exiles him and returns him transformed at your postcombat main phase, gated on how much life you gained this turn - none of exile-self, transform, the step trigger or cares:lifegain was recorded, and the -1 also keys on life gained. The -6 puts a lifelink counter on a creature.

kept.name: Nils, Discipline Enforcer
kept.why: "For each player, put a +1/+1 counter on up to one target creature that player controls" is a mass effect across every player. The second ability is a Ghostly Prison: creatures can't attack you unless their controller pays {X}, and neither the tax nor the attack restriction was recorded.

kept.name: Traxos, Scourge of Kroog
kept.why: "Whenever YOU cast a historic spell" is your own cast, not any cast. The bare trig:cast does not distinguish an untapper that rewards your artifact spells from a stax piece watching opponents.

kept.name: Metalworker
kept.why: The ability costs {T} and nothing recorded it, unlike every other tapper in the batch. It also reads artifact cards in your hand, which is where its whole payoff lives.

kept.name: Phyrexian Delver
kept.why: "You lose life equal to that card's mana value" is a whole sentence with no word for it. The drawback is the card's defining cost and a lifeloss deck genuinely cares.

kept.name: Sunfall
kept.why: "Exile all creatures" wipes the board including yours. scope:all says it is a mass effect but not that it is symmetric destruction, which is the word the anti-synergy check reads to keep a wipe out of a go-wide deck.

kept.name: Scion of Draco
kept.why: No clause on the card gains life. It grants lifelink to your black creatures, which grants:lifelink already records. Left as it stands it files a 12-mana domain artifact as a lifegain card.

kept.name: Scavenged Brawler
kept.why: The ability puts a flying counter, a vigilance counter, a trample counter and a lifelink counter on a creature. Only grants:vigilance was recorded - the other three grants are the same clause. It is also activated from the graveyard, which nothing noted.

kept.name: Avenger of the Fallen
kept.why: Mobilize's reminder text ends "Sacrifice them at the beginning of the next end step". The tokens are made and then sacrificed every combat, which is the card's whole aristocrats value, and neither the sacrifice nor the delayed end-step trigger was recorded.

kept.name: Swift Reconfiguration
kept.why: This carried no effect word at all. It is an Aura (eff:attach, as Hero's Heirloom and Unfinished Business have) and turning a creature into a non-creature Vehicle it loses all other card types is exactly eff:neutralise - the Darksteel Mutation shape. Without it a one-mana removal spell is invisible as removal.

kept.name: Gleaming Splendor
kept.why: "Whenever an opponent draws their second card each turn" is a draw trigger, and "{2}{W}: Two target players each draw a card" is the card's own draw. Only the Treasure half was recorded.

kept.name: Tarrian's Journal // The Tomb of Aclazotz
kept.why: "Discard your hand" is a cost, and it transforms. The back face is a land that taps for {B} - eff:add-mana was missing entirely - and lets you cast a creature spell FROM your graveyard, which is eff:cast-from-graveyard. Nothing on either face returns a card to a zone, so eff:return-from is wrong.

kept.name: Scroll of Fate
kept.why: Manifest puts a card from your hand straight onto the battlefield, which is precisely eff:put-onto-battlefield, and the ability costs {T}. Only the token half was read.

kept.name: Canoptek Scarab Swarm
kept.why: "Exile target player's graveyard" is graveyard hate and "create a 1/1 Insect token" for each hit is its payoff. Neither effect was recorded, so a dedicated hate creature reads as a vanilla flier.

kept.name: Ajani's Chosen
kept.why: "If that enchantment is an Aura, you may attach it to the token" - the attach half of the trigger was not recorded.

kept.name: Hare Apparent
kept.why: The card's only ability creates Rabbit tokens and it carries no effect word whatsoever. A go-wide token payoff currently reads as a vanilla 1/1.

kept.name: Elementalist's Palette
kept.why: "Whenever you cast a spell with {X} in its mana cost, put two charge counters on this artifact" is a whole ability with nothing recorded: it is a cast trigger on your own spells and it grows itself with counters.

kept.name: Palace Jailer
kept.why: "Exile target creature an opponent controls" had no word for it, so one of the format's best white removal creatures was filed as a monarch enabler only.

kept.name: Conformer Shuriken
kept.why: The granted ability is "Whenever this creature attacks, tap target creature defending player controls". The tap and the counters were read but not the attack trigger they hang off.

kept.name: Shay Cormac
kept.why: "Whenever a creature with a bounty counter on it dies" is a death trigger with nothing recorded, and the first ability is a mass effect on opponents' permanents. Two of his three abilities need words that do not exist.

kept.name: Desolation Twin
kept.why: "Create a 10/10 colorless Eldrazi creature token" had no word at all. The trigger is "When you cast this spell", which trig:cast already records - there is no enters trigger on the card, so trig:enters is wrong.

kept.name: Season of the Burrow
kept.why: Three of the four things this modal sorcery does were missing: the Rabbit token, the card its controller draws off the exile mode, and the fact that it is modal at all ("Choose up to five {P} worth of modes").

kept.name: Obelisk of Urd
kept.why: "Creatures you control of the chosen type get +2/+2" is the card, and neither the pump nor its mass scope was recorded - so the format's standard tribal anthem cannot be found as one. King of the Pride, the same effect, carries both.

kept.name: Solitary Confinement
kept.why: Only the shroud line was read. It prevents all damage dealt to you, skips your draw step, and sacrifices itself each upkeep unless you discard a card - four clauses, one recorded.

kept.name: Bag of Holding
kept.why: Two of its three abilities were unread: it exiles your discarded cards out of your graveyard - which is worth knowing, since it works AGAINST a graveyard deck - and the last ability sacrifices it to return everything it exiled to hand.

kept.name: White Lotus Tile
kept.why: The mana ability costs {T} and it was not recorded, unlike Alloy Myr and Hedron Crawler in the same batch.

kept.name: Pestilence
kept.why: "Deals 1 damage to each creature and each player" is a symmetric board-wide effect. eff:damage alone reads as a ping.

kept.name: Essence Channeler
kept.why: "As long as you've lost life this turn, this creature has flying and vigilance" is a conditional self-grant with no word for it, and the death trigger moves its counters onto another creature you control, which is a counter placement on a different permanent than eff:add-counters-self covers.

kept.name: Innocent Blood
kept.why: Nothing is sacrificed as a cost here - the edict IS the effect, already recorded as eff:sacrifice. cost:sacrifice means an on-demand outlet (Ashnod's Altar, Viscera Seer), so a one-sided-ish edict currently reads as a sacrifice outlet an aristocrats deck can build around.

kept.name: Syr Vondam, Sunstar Exemplar
kept.why: The second ability triggers on Syr Vondam HIMSELF dying or being exiled, so it needs trig:leaves-self alongside the trig:leaves-other already carried for the first ability. It also gates on "while its power is 4 or greater", which is cares:power.

kept.name: Moseo, Vein's New Dean
kept.why: The Pest token it creates carries "Whenever this token attacks, you gain 1 life", so the card does produce life gain - which is also the trigger condition for its own Infusion ability, and cares:lifegain is already present with no producer beside it.

kept.name: Cartographer's Hawk
kept.why: "return it to its owner's hand" returns this creature, one of your own, to hand. That is a self-bounce and eff:move-zone alone does not say whose permanent moved or where.

kept.name: Peacewalker Colossus
kept.why: "Another target Vehicle you control becomes an artifact creature until end of turn" is exactly eff:animate, and it is the whole reason this card is played. The list carried no effect word at all.

kept.name: Angelic Skirmisher
kept.why: At each combat you CHOOSE first strike, vigilance or lifelink and your creatures gain it. Only grants:vigilance was recorded, so two of the three granted keywords and the modal choice were missing.

kept.name: Haunted One
kept.why: The granted ability explicitly gives creatures undying until end of turn. The counter and pump halves are recorded; the keyword grant is not.

kept.name: Felisa, Fang of Silverquill
kept.why: Mentor is "Whenever this creature attacks, put a +1/+1 counter on target attacking creature". The counter effect is recorded but the attack trigger that causes it is not.

kept.name: Of Herbs and Stewed Rabbit
kept.why: Every one of the three chapters creates tokens - a Food on I, a Food on II, and a Halfling for each Food on III - and the list carried no token word at all despite tok/cares:sub entries for Food and Halfling.

kept.name: Paladin Class
kept.why: Three separate clauses were unread: the level 1 static taxes opponents' spells {1} more (eff:increase-cost), level 3 triggers "Whenever you attack" (trig:attacks), and that same ability grants double strike.

kept.name: Apprentice Necromancer
kept.why: The reanimated creature "gains haste", and the ability then sacrifices it at the next end step. Only the return-from half of the ability was read.

kept.name: Midnight Banshee
kept.why: Putting a -1/-1 counter on each nonblack creature makes creatures smaller, which is what eff:shrink names. Wither does the same to anything it damages. eff:add-counters alone reads as a counters payoff rather than as a mass shrink.

kept.name: Far Traveler
kept.why: The granted ability is a blink - exile a tapped creature you control, then return it - and it happens at the beginning of your end step. The card carried no effect or trigger word whatsoever, only cares: words.

kept.name: Solar Array
kept.why: "When you next cast an artifact spell this turn" is a delayed trigger on your own artifact cast. The sunburst counters and the mana ability were read; the trigger that delivers them was not.

kept.name: Filth
kept.why: The entire point of an Incarnation is the second ability, which functions only "as long as this card is in your graveyard". Nothing recorded that the card works from the graveyard.

kept.name: Star Compass
kept.why: The mana ability is "{T}: Add one mana..." and the tap cost was not recorded, unlike every other tap-for-mana rock.

kept.name: Anti-Venom, Horrifying Healer
kept.why: "If damage would be dealt to Anti-Venom, prevent that damage" is a damage prevention replacement; only the +1/+1 counters half of that clause was read.

kept.name: Divine Resilience
kept.why: Granting indestructible is a protection spell, which eff:protect names. It gives no power or toughness boost at all, so eff:pump is wrong - it would tell the engine this is a combat trick.

kept.name: Warren Warleader
kept.why: "Whenever you attack, choose one -" is a modal ability (eff:choose). Offspring's token copy triggers when this creature itself enters, so trig:enters-self belongs beside the bare trig:enters already carried.

kept.name: Danitha, Benalia's Hope
kept.why: The entire enters ability was unread: it puts an Aura or Equipment from your HAND (put-onto-battlefield) or your GRAVEYARD (return-from) onto the battlefield ATTACHED to her. Lifelink also means she gains life, the same way Gifted Aetherborn carries eff:gain-life for the bare keyword.

kept.name: Outrageous Robbery
kept.why: The cards go to EXILE face down and you may play them for as long as they remain there, which is precisely eff:impulse. Nothing is put into a graveyard, so eff:mill is wrong and would offer this to a mill deck as a mill payoff.

kept.name: Guardian Scalelord
kept.why: Backup triggers when this creature enters, and when it targets another creature that creature gains this card's abilities, which here is flying and the attack trigger. Only the attack trigger and the counter were recorded.

kept.name: Excalibur II
kept.why: "Whenever you gain life, put a charge counter" makes this a lifegain payoff. trig:gains-life records the trigger shape but nothing records that the deck must be gaining life for the card to do anything.

kept.name: Triskelion
kept.why: The damage ability's cost is "Remove a +1/+1 counter from this creature". The damage is recorded and the cost that pays for it is not, which matters because it makes Triskelion a counters-matter card.

kept.name: Metropolis Reformer
kept.why: Both non-keyword lines were unread: "You have hexproof" grants hexproof to you, and "Whenever this creature is dealt damage, you gain that much life" gains life. Only the damage trigger was recorded, with nothing saying what it does.

kept.name: Tithing Blade // Consuming Sepulcher
kept.why: The back face's drain happens at the beginning of your upkeep and no trigger word recorded that. Craft's cost exiles this artifact itself plus a creature you control or from your graveyard, and it returns the card transformed.

kept.name: Grave Betrayal
kept.why: It returns creatures you DON'T control to the battlefield "under your control" - it steals them. eff:return-from alone reads as self-recursion and misses that this is a theft engine.

kept.name: Component Pouch
kept.why: Both abilities cost {T}, the mana ability additionally removes a component counter, and the d20 ability puts one or two counters back on the Pouch itself. Only the mana and the die roll were read.

kept.name: Dream Devourer
kept.why: Almost nothing was read. It grants foretell to every nonland card in your HAND at a cost reduced by {2}, and it gets +2/+0 whenever you foretell.

kept.name: The Mind Stone
kept.why: The whole harnessed ability was unread: at the beginning of your end step it exiles a nonland permanent you control and returns it, which is a repeatable blink. Only the mana ability was recorded.

kept.name: Mirrormind Crown
kept.why: It replaces your token creation with tokens that are COPIES of the equipped creature. The card carried eff:attach and cares: words but nothing saying it makes tokens or copies anything.

kept.name: Orcish Medicine
kept.why: "your choice of lifelink or indestructible" is a modal choice and grants lifelink as well as indestructible; only the indestructible branch was recorded. Granting indestructible to a creature is also protection.

kept.name: Wojek Investigator
kept.why: Investigating makes Clue tokens, whose only purpose is "{2}, Sacrifice this token: Draw a card". Recording only eff:create-token hides that this is a card-draw engine, the same way Food makers carry eff:gain-life.

kept.name: War of the Last Alliance
kept.why: Chapter III pumps the whole team ("Creatures you control gain double strike"), which every other mass-buff card here marks with scope:all. Chapters I and II search your library, and Vexing Puzzlebox shows a library search carries cares:zone:library.

kept.name: Titan's Presence
kept.why: The additional cost is revealing a colorless creature card from your hand. cost:reveal is exactly that cost, and the card reaches into your hand as a zone, which cares:zone:hand records.

kept.name: Ardyn, the Usurper
kept.why: It creates a token that is a COPY of the exiled card, so eff:copy is missing. Nothing is returned to any zone - the card is exiled and a new token is made - so eff:return-from is wrong and would read Ardyn as a recursion commander.

kept.name: Blitzball
kept.why: The second ability's cost is "{T}, Sacrifice this artifact". The sacrifice cost was not recorded at all.

kept.name: Sower of Discord
kept.why: "As this creature enters, choose two players" is an entry ability and a genuine choice; neither the entry trigger nor the choice was recorded. rec:partial confirms the compiler gave up on this card.

kept.name: Come Back Wrong
kept.why: It returns the destroyed creature under YOUR control, which is stealing a permanent, and that is the whole point of the card. The delayed "sacrifice it at the beginning of your next end step" is an end-step trigger.

kept.name: Sifter of Skulls
kept.why: The Eldrazi Scion tokens it makes carry "Sacrifice this token: Add {C}", so this card genuinely produces mana. Same reasoning the project already applies to Treasure makers, whose ramp role was right while the mana facet was missing.

kept.name: Redemption Arc
kept.why: It goads the enchanted creature and eff:goad was never recorded. eff:exile-own means a blink of your own permanent; "{1}{W}: Exile enchanted creature" is permanent removal of a creature that is usually an opponent's, not a flicker.

kept.name: Edgar, Charmed Groom // Edgar Markov's Coffin
kept.why: Almost the whole card was unread. It brings ITSELF back from the graveyard when it dies (eff:recur-self, cares:zone:graveyard) and transforms. The back face has an upkeep trigger that puts a bloodline counter on itself and later removes those counters. Only the token and the anthem had been recorded.

kept.name: Lord of the Undead
kept.why: The activated ability returns a Zombie from the graveyard TO YOUR HAND; the hand half of that zone move was not recorded, matching how Eye of Nidhogg records the same wording.

kept.name: Auriok Champion
kept.why: Protection from black AND from red. cares:color:r was recorded and cares:color:b was dropped.

kept.name: Jeweled Amulet
kept.why: The mana ability's cost is "Remove a charge counter from this artifact". It also explicitly notes the TYPE OF MANA SPENT to pay the first ability, which is exactly cares:mana-spent.

kept.name: Thunderhawk Gunship
kept.why: Nothing here changes power or toughness. "Attacking creatures you control gain flying" is already covered by grants:flying, and every other keyword-granter in this batch (War of the Last Alliance, Crossway Troublemakers, Abzan Battle Priest) correctly carries no eff:pump.

kept.name: Selective Obliteration
kept.why: "Exile each permanent unless..." is a symmetric board wipe that hits your own permanents too, which is what scope:wipe means and is what an anti-synergy check needs to see. "Each player chooses a color" is a choice.

kept.name: Detection Tower
kept.why: The whole second ability is about hexproof and produced no word at all - the card's facet list currently describes a plain colorless mana land.

kept.name: Seizan, Perverter of Truth
kept.why: Half the card was missing: "that player ... draws two cards" at EACH player's upkeep. This is a symmetric group draw engine and only the life loss had been recorded.

kept.name: Gonti's Aether Heart
kept.why: Taking an extra turn is the entire reason the card exists and was not recorded. Its cost is exiling itself. It also triggers on ITSELF entering ("Gonti's Aether Heart or another artifact"), not only on other artifacts.

kept.name: Oltec Matterweaver
kept.why: "Choose one —" is a modal choice, and the second mode creates a token that is a COPY of an artifact token. Only the generic token-making was recorded.

kept.name: Vexing Puzzlebox
kept.why: The dice trigger puts charge counters ON THIS ARTIFACT, which is the engine that powers the search ability; only the removal of those counters as a cost had been recorded.

kept.name: Crossway Troublemakers
kept.why: "you may pay 2 life" is a life payment. eff:do-if-cost-paid records that there IS a cost but never says what it is.

kept.name: The Book of Exalted Deeds
kept.why: The end-step trigger is conditional on having GAINED 3 OR MORE LIFE this turn, which is the card's whole deck-building requirement and was missing. The activated ability's costs ({T}, exile itself) and its counter placement were also unrecorded.

kept.name: Pack Rat
kept.why: "Discard a card" is part of the activation cost and was not recorded. cost:discard rather than cost:discard-self, since the -self convention (cost:sacrifice-self, cost:exile-self) means the card itself, not you.
