kept.why: The whole card is an upkeep trigger on the enchanted player and neither timing word was present.

kept.name: Hot Soup
kept.why: 'Whenever equipped creature is dealt damage, destroy it' was entirely unread. It destroys your own creature, so the -own form is the correct one and plain eff:destroy would file this as removal.

kept.name: Hulkbuster Armor
kept.why: 'Equipped creature has base power and toughness 9/9' sets P/T; only the flying grant was recorded.

kept.name: Extinction Event
kept.why: 'Choose odd or even' is a real choice on resolution. It exiles roughly half of every creature on the board including yours, so it is a symmetric sweeper.

kept.name: Three Dreams
kept.why: It searches and shuffles your library; only the search was recorded.

kept.name: Resolute Archangel
kept.why: The entire non-keyword text sets your life total back to your starting total and nothing recorded it. It is not a life gain, so eff:set-life is the right word.

kept.name: Syphon Flesh
kept.why: Half the card makes a 2/2 Zombie for each creature sacrificed and eff:create-token was missing. It hits each other player, so the scope is mass.

kept.name: Perilous Vault
kept.why: The activation costs tapping and exiling the artifact itself, neither recorded. It exiles every nonland permanent including yours, which is a full board wipe.

kept.name: Angelic Intervention
kept.why: Granting protection until end of turn to save a creature or planeswalker is the protection-trick job and only the grants: word was present.

kept.name: Szarekh, the Silent King
kept.why: Putting an artifact creature or Vehicle from among the milled cards into your hand is a return out of the graveyard; only the mill half was read.

kept.name: Kaervek, the Spiteful
kept.why: 'Other creatures get -1/-1' makes creatures smaller. Recorded as a pump, this reads as an anthem when it is a static sweeper that kills x/1s.

kept.name: Ral Zarek, Guest Lecturer
kept.why: The -1 makes any number of target players discard, which was entirely unrecorded, and the -7 makes an opponent skip turns.

kept.name: Field of Souls
kept.why: It triggers on a nontoken creature being put into your graveyard from the battlefield and the graveyard zone was not recorded.

kept.name: Deceiver of Form
kept.why: It reveals the top card of your library and may put it on the bottom, and the copy effect applies to every other creature you control.

kept.name: Frogmite
kept.why: Affinity for artifacts is a cost reduction and it was the only real thing the card does; the list held the keyword but no effect at all.

kept.name: Team Avatar
kept.why: The damage ability costs discarding this card, which was unrecorded.

kept.name: Darkblast
kept.why: Dredge returns this card from your graveyard to your hand. eff:return-from was there but the fact that it brings ITSELF back, which is the whole reason Darkblast is played, was not.

kept.name: Zof Consumption // Zof Bloodbog
kept.why: The land half was not read at all: it taps for mana. Mana value is 6 on the sorcery face ({4}{B}{B}), and the empty cost field left it with no mv word.

kept.name: Hand of Vecna
kept.why: The whole point of the card is missing: it pumps. The begin-combat trigger gives +X/+X, and equip is paid with life.

kept.name: Elbrus, the Binding Blade // Withengar Unbound
kept.why: 'unattach Elbrus, then transform it' is an explicit transform and nothing said so. The back face is a 13/13.

kept.name: Thran Temporal Gateway
kept.why: Nothing but the type line was read. It is a tap ability that cheats a permanent out of hand, which is exactly eff:put-onto-battlefield.

kept.name: Koh, the Face Stealer
kept.why: 'When Koh enters' is a real enters trigger and was absent entirely. 'Pay 1 life:' is an activation cost, and the whole card is built on the pile of creatures exiled with it.

kept.name: Myr Propagator
kept.why: The activated ability costs {3} and a tap; the tap was not recorded.

kept.name: Leonardo, Cutting Edge
kept.why: Lifelink gains life (the convention every other lifelinker in this batch follows), and 'Whenever you gain life' is a lifegain payoff. Sneak is an alternative cast cost that returns your own unblocked attacker to hand.

kept.name: Weatherlight Compleated
kept.why: The dies trigger draws a card at seven counters and only the scry half was recorded.

kept.name: Arcbound Condor
kept.why: Modular has a death trigger ('When it dies, you may put its +1/+1 counters on target artifact creature') and no trig:dies was present, though the counter effect from that same clause was.

kept.name: Enduring Angel // Angelic Enforcer
kept.why: The replacement effect transforms the card, and the back face doubles your life total, which is life gain. Neither was recorded.

kept.name: Wave of Rats
kept.why: It returns ITSELF from the graveyard to the battlefield, which is the card's entire reason to exist, and blitz draws a card when it dies.

kept.name: Clattering Augur
kept.why: 'This creature can't block' and the graveyard-to-hand self-recursion were both unread.

kept.name: Exterminate!
kept.why: Replicate here is paid by tapping an untapped Dalek you control, which is a cast cost tapping other creatures.

kept.name: Sorin, Grim Nemesis
kept.why: The ultimate makes a pile of Vampire Knight tokens and nothing recorded that it makes tokens at all. The minus abilities are loyalty costs removing counters; only the plus was recorded.

kept.name: Fateful Handoff
kept.why: Nothing is sacrificed anywhere on this card. You give the permanent away, which eff:give-control already says. cost:sacrifice would file it as a sacrifice outlet, which it is not.

kept.name: Planar Atlas
kept.why: It exiles nothing and touches no exile zone: it looks at four, puts a land on top and the rest on the bottom. eff:impulse (exile off the top to play them) and cares:zone:exile are both wrong. It does hunt for a land in your library, which is the one thing not recorded.

kept.name: Invasion of New Capenna // Holy Frazzle-Cannon
kept.why: The whole back face was unread: it is an Equipment with Equip {1} and an attack trigger.

kept.name: Wight of Precinct Six
kept.why: It gets +1/+1 for each creature card in opponents' graveyards, so it pumps itself, the same reading Fleshtaker's '+2/+2' gets.

kept.name: Shard of the Void Dragon
kept.why: The second trigger is about artifacts hitting a graveyard or exile from the battlefield, and neither zone was recorded; the graveyard half is literally an artifact dying.

kept.name: Edgewall Inn
kept.why: Only 'choose a color' was read. It is a land that taps for mana and sacrifices itself to return an Adventure card from your graveyard, and none of that was recorded.

kept.name: Gruesome Slaughter
kept.why: The damage is 'equal to its power', and the grant is a mass one over every colourless creature you control.

kept.name: Pox
kept.why: Nothing is sacrificed as a cost; the sacrifices are the spell's effect, which eff:sacrifice already covers. cost:sacrifice would make Pox read as a sacrifice outlet.

kept.name: Timothar, Baron of Bats
kept.why: The exile half of the trigger and the return of the exiled card to the battlefield were both unread, which is the entire engine of the card.

kept.name: The Grim Captain's Locker
kept.why: The second ability grants escape to your graveyard's creatures, so the deck casts them from there. That is a different claim from returning a card and neither the grant nor the graveyard casting was recorded.

kept.name: Momentum Breaker
kept.why: The last ability is '{2}, Sacrifice this enchantment', and the self-sacrifice cost was not recorded.

kept.name: The Sibsig Ceremony
kept.why: 'destroy that creature' destroys YOUR own creature, which is the card's whole mechanism and was unread. Recording it as plain eff:destroy would wrongly file this as removal.

kept.name: Invasion of Tolvada // The Broken Sky
kept.why: The back face's static anthem and lifelink grant and its end-step token trigger were all unread; only the token creation itself survived.

kept.name: Fell Beast of Mordor
kept.why: Devour eats your own creatures and the counters it enters with were never recorded as being put on it; ctr:+1/+1 alone says nothing about where they came from.

kept.name: Holy Avenger
kept.why: The combat damage trigger puts an Aura from your hand straight onto the battlefield, which is exactly eff:put-onto-battlefield, and nothing said the card cares about your hand.

kept.name: Blight Rot
kept.why: Four -1/-1 counters make the creature smaller and usually kill it. With only eff:add-counters the card reads as a +1/+1-counters card instead of the removal spell it is.

kept.name: Binding Mummy
kept.why: It taps ONE target artifact or creature. Nothing here affects everything.

kept.name: Gollum, Scheming Guide
kept.why: The attack trigger draws a card and makes Gollum unblockable when the guess is wrong, and it looks at the top of the library. The list carried the trigger and none of the effects.

kept.name: Scion of Halaster
kept.why: The granted ability replaces your first draw each turn (a draw trigger) and ends with 'Then draw a card', while looking at the top two of your library. Only eff:surveil was recorded.

kept.name: Gorbag of Minas Morgul
kept.why: The reflexive trigger is modal (choose one) and one mode draws a card; neither was recorded. Sacrificing your own Goblin/Orc is the same cost shape Scourge of Nel Toth carries as cost:sacrifice, and it is what makes this an aristocrats card.

kept.name: Scorn-Blade Berserker
kept.why: Backup 1 is an enters trigger ('When this creature enters, put a +1/+1 counter on target creature'). eff:add-counters was recorded but the trigger that causes it was not.

kept.name: Zuko's Conviction
kept.why: Kicker: pay {4} more and the card goes to the battlefield instead of your hand. That is exactly 'gives more if you pay'.

kept.name: Optimistic Scavenger
kept.why: The trigger is another permanent (an enchantment you control) entering, not this creature. trig:enters was recorded without the direction.

kept.name: Eater of Virtue
kept.why: The card names thirteen keywords it can grant the equipped creature and only two were recorded. It also cares about what is in its own exile pile, which is where every one of those grants comes from.

kept.name: Celestial Unicorn
kept.why: Its whole card is a lifegain payoff. trig:gains-life was there but nothing said the card cares about lifegain, so a lifegain deck could not find it.

kept.name: Defacing Duskmage // Vandal's Edit
kept.why: The back half is 'Each player loses 2 life', a symmetric effect hitting everyone.

kept.name: Geth's Summons
kept.why: The corrupted half puts a creature card from an OPPONENT'S graveyard onto the battlefield under your control. Taking their card was not recorded anywhere.

kept.name: Triarch Praetorian
kept.why: 'When this creature enters from a graveyard' is an enters trigger and neither trig word was present. It also loses you 2 life, the same shape Audacious Thief records as eff:lose-life.

kept.name: Grafted Wargear
kept.why: 'Whenever this Equipment becomes unattached, sacrifice that permanent.' The sacrifice is half the card and nothing in the list said it happens.

kept.name: Assault Intercessor
kept.why: A trigger on one opponent's creature dying, draining 2 from that one player. Nothing mass about it.

kept.name: Lothlórien Blade
kept.why: It deals damage equal to the equipped creature's power, so the card genuinely reads power.

kept.name: Wrath of the Skies
kept.why: It destroys EACH artifact, creature and enchantment at or under the energy paid, your own included. That is a symmetric board wipe and only scope:all was recorded.

kept.name: Chalice of the Void
kept.why: Add: 'Whenever a player casts a spell...' is a cast trigger and no trig word was present. Remove: the cost is {X}{X}, so the mana value collapses to 0 and the card reads as a cheap two-drop. It is never cast for nothing, and a deck asking for cheap cards should not be offered it.

kept.name: Balthor the Defiled
kept.why: It returns all black AND all red creature cards; only black was recorded. Exiling Balthor is the activation cost and no cost word said so.

kept.name: Conclave Tribunal
kept.why: The entire card is 'exile target nonland permanent an opponent controls'. The list had the enters trigger and no effect at all, so this removal spell could not be chosen as removal. Seal from Existence, the same effect in this batch, carries eff:exile.

kept.name: Curse of Misfortunes
kept.why: It searches your library, puts the Curse onto the battlefield and shuffles. The search was recorded, the shuffle and the library interest were not.

kept.name: Let's Play a Game
kept.why: 'Choose one' (or one or more with delirium). Every mode was recorded and the modality itself was not.

kept.name: Cecil, Dark Knight // Cecil, Redeemed Paladin
kept.why: The front face untaps AND transforms, and you lose life equal to the damage dealt. The back face has an attack trigger granting indestructible; grants:indestructible was recorded without the trigger that causes it.

kept.name: Uba Mask
kept.why: Drawn cards are exiled face up and playable only that turn, which is the impulse pattern, and the whole card is a draw replacement. The list had no effect or trigger at all. Deliberately NOT adding eff:exile: the exile is not removal and would wrongly make this card an answer.

kept.name: Sarah Jane Smith
kept.why: 'Whenever you cast a historic spell' is a cast trigger you own, and no trig word was present. The Clue it makes draws a card, the same way Shelob's Ambush records eff:gain-life off its Food token.

kept.name: Magnifying Glass
kept.why: The Clue token it makes is a card draw. eff:create-token alone does not say the card draws.

kept.name: Healer of the Pride
kept.why: You gain 2 life off one creature entering. Nothing affects everything.

kept.name: Awaken the Erstwhile
kept.why: The card had NO effect words at all. It makes every player discard their whole hand (you included) and then makes that many Zombie tokens for each of them.

kept.name: Prosthetic Injector
kept.why: +0/+2 is a pump, and toxic 1 gives a poison counter on combat damage. The list recorded only that it is an Equipment.

kept.name: Keening Stone
kept.why: The ability costs {5}, {T}. The tap cost was missing.

kept.name: Necrosynthesis
kept.why: On death it looks at the top X cards of your library and takes one, so the card reads the library top.

kept.name: Network Terminal
kept.why: It taps one other artifact you control to draw and discard one card. Nothing mass.

kept.name: Death in Heaven
kept.why: Chapter III puts creature cards exiled from OTHER players' graveyards onto the battlefield under your control, which is theft and was not recorded, and the card tracks its own exile pile.

kept.name: Glasses of Urza
kept.why: '{T}: Look at target player's hand.' The tap cost was missing.

kept.name: March of Wretched Sorrow
kept.why: The additional cost is exiling black cards from your hand, which is both a cast-time exile cost and a genuine interest in your hand. Neither was recorded.

kept.name: ED-E, Lonesome Eyebot
kept.why: The attack trigger puts a quest counter on ED-E itself, which is the whole engine behind the draw. No counter effect was recorded.

kept.name: Nezumi Linkbreaker
kept.why: The Mercenary token it leaves behind pumps a creature you control each turn, which is the only ongoing thing the card does.

kept.name: Saradoc, Master of Buckland
kept.why: The trigger fires on Saradoc himself OR another creature entering, and it reads power ('power 2 or less'); bare trig:enters lost both. grants:lifelink is deliberately not added here as kw:lifelink is already carried.

kept.name: Sentry Bot
kept.why: Costs {1} less for each creature attacking you is a cost reduction; "you get {E} for each creature attacking you" puts energy counters on a player; "you may pay {E}{E}{E}. If you do" is the pay-for-more shape; the payoff hits each creature you control.

kept.name: Panoptic Mirror
kept.why: The imprint ability's cost includes {T}. "You may copy a card exiled with this artifact" is a copy effect and nothing recorded it. It cares about its own exile pile and about instants/sorceries in your hand. Deliberately NOT adding eff:exile: exiling your own card from hand would make this read as removal.

kept.name: Yathan Tombguard
kept.why: "you draw a card and you lose 1 life" - only the draw was recorded. Same shape as Gruesome Realization, which carries eff:lose-life for its own self-life-loss clause.

kept.name: Mad Auntie
kept.why: The regenerate ability costs {T} and nothing recorded it. Regenerating another target Goblin keeps your creature alive, which is what eff:protect names.

kept.name: Heirloom Epic
kept.why: "you may tap an untapped creature you control rather than pay that mana" is a convoke-shaped cost paid by tapping other creatures, which is exactly cost:tap-others and is the whole reason to play the card.

kept.name: Shadow of the Enemy
kept.why: No exile is paid as a cost here - the exile is the effect, so cost:exile is wrong. Nothing is returned to hand or battlefield either, so eff:return-from is wrong; the cards stay in exile and you cast them there. It exiles ALL creature cards from that graveyard, and the payoff is casting cards that were in a graveyard.

kept.name: Maralen of the Mornsong
kept.why: Each player searches their library, and the whole card is symmetric across every player. Its most important line, "Players can't draw cards", has no word at all.

kept.name: Madame Null, Power Broker
kept.why: "you may pay life equal to its power. If you do" is a life payment, the pay-for-more shape, and a check on the creature's power - all three unrecorded.

kept.name: General Kudro of Drannith
kept.why: "exile target card from an opponent's graveyard" is graveyard hate and no facet recorded it at all. The activated ability only kills a creature with power 4 or greater. The trigger reads "General Kudro OR another Human", so it fires on itself too.

kept.name: Show of Confidence
kept.why: "When you cast this spell" is a genuine cast trigger, and the copy count is the number of other instant and sorcery spells you have cast this turn, which is a spells-cast-matters signal.

kept.name: Smuggler's Buggy
kept.why: Hideaway 4 is an enters trigger that looks at the top four of your library and exiles one to cast later - the exile-from-top-to-play shape - and none of it was recorded. Only the combat damage trigger and the free cast were.

kept.name: Estinien Varlineau
kept.why: "you draw X cards and lose X life" - the draw was recorded and the life loss was not.

kept.name: Dusk Mangler
kept.why: The additional cost to cast is sacrifice a creature, discard a card, OR pay 4 life, so all three cast-cost words apply and none was recorded. The enters trigger hits each opponent.

kept.name: Planar Outburst
kept.why: "Destroy all nonland creatures" is a symmetric board wipe that kills your own board and only eff:destroy was recorded. Awaken puts four +1/+1 counters on a land you control and turns it into a 0/0 Elemental creature with haste.

kept.name: Star Charter
kept.why: Nothing is exiled and nothing is played from exile - the cards go to your hand or the bottom of your library, so eff:impulse and cares:zone:exile are both false and would make this read as an impulse-draw card. It only takes a creature with power 3 or less.

kept.name: Sandbenders' Storm
kept.why: Earthbend 3 puts three +1/+1 counters on the land and the animated land has haste; the destroy mode only hits a creature with power 4 or greater. The animate half was read and the counters, haste and power check were not.

kept.name: Illicit Shipment
kept.why: Casualty 3 is an additional cost paid by sacrificing a creature as you cast the spell. The copy it produces was recorded but the sacrifice that pays for it was not.

kept.name: Sengir Autocrat
kept.why: It creates three 0/1 Serf tokens on entry and the list has no effect word at all - only the two triggers. The leave clause hits all Serf tokens. Deliberately NOT adding eff:exile: the tokens exiled are its own, and the word would make a token maker read as removal.

kept.name: Leader's Talent
kept.why: Only the level 3 cast trigger was read. Level 1 is "whenever you attack" and level 2 is "whenever a creature you control leaves the battlefield ... you gain 2 life", so an attack trigger, a leave trigger and a lifegain effect are all missing.

kept.name: Gate Colossus
kept.why: Affinity for Gates makes the spell cost less and nothing recorded it. It can't be blocked by creatures with power 2 or less, which is a power check. The graveyard-to-library clause is a trigger on another permanent entering, and neither trigger word was present.

kept.name: Aethergeode Miner
kept.why: "Exile this creature, then return it to the battlefield" is a self-blink and the list recorded only the energy half of the card.

kept.name: Gutterbones
kept.why: "Return this card from your graveyard to your hand" is the definition of a creature that brings itself back, and the generic eff:return-from does not say that it is itself.

kept.name: Mukotai Ambusher
kept.why: Ninjutsu puts this card onto the battlefield from your hand, which is exactly what the word names; only the return-to-hand cost was recorded.

kept.name: Courageous Resolve
kept.why: The card grants protection from each of your opponents and nothing recorded the grant. Granting protection to keep a creature alive is what eff:protect names.

kept.name: Bronze Bombshell
kept.why: "that player sacrifices it" is a sacrifice effect and only the damage was recorded.

kept.name: Phyrexian Negator
kept.why: "sacrifice that many permanents" is a sacrifice effect. The list had the trigger and no effect at all.

kept.name: Divinity of Pride
kept.why: Lifelink gains life, which is how the other lifelink card in this batch is recorded, and the +4/+4 is conditional on your life total, which is the lifegain payoff the card exists for.

kept.name: Argentum Masticore
kept.why: "sacrifice this creature unless you discard a card" makes you discard, and that clause is what real decks use it for (madness, reanimation, Masticore-style rummaging). Nothing recorded it. Deliberately NOT adding eff:sacrifice: the sacrifice is a drawback on itself, not an outlet that eats other creatures, and filing it as one would put it in aristocrats decks.

kept.name: Tower of the Magistrate
kept.why: "Target creature gains protection from artifacts until end of turn" is a grant and the whole reason this land is played (it unattaches Equipment and answers artifact removal). Only the mana ability was read.

kept.name: Yosei, the Morning Star
kept.why: "target player skips their next untap step" is the famous half of this card and was unread; eff:skip-phase is exactly that word. Yosei is a 4/4, and pt:big means power 5 or more.

kept.name: Leather Armor
kept.why: +0/+1 is a pump and was not recorded. Ward {1} counters a targeting spell unless the opponent pays, which is precisely what eff:unless-pays describes, and it is the only thing this Equipment is played for.

kept.name: Knight of Dusk's Shadow
kept.why: "Your opponents can't gain life" is a global static affecting every opponent, matching how scope:all is used on the other team-wide statics in this batch (Kwende, Corrosive Mentor). The effect itself has no word at all, hence the proposal.

kept.name: Draco
kept.why: Domain reduces this spell's own cost by {2} per basic land type, which is the entire reason the card is castable. Same shape as Ghalta: the card's defining clause is a cost reduction and nothing recorded it.

kept.name: Kemba's Banner
kept.why: For Mirrodin! is "When this Equipment enters, create a 2/2 Rebel token, then attach this to it". The token and the attach were both read; the entry trigger that causes them was not.

kept.name: Blade of the Oni
kept.why: "Equipped creature has base power and toughness 5/5" is a set-pt, not a pump, and "has menace" is a grant. The card had kw:menace for its own printed menace but nothing for the menace it hands out.

kept.name: Order of Midnight // Alter Fate
kept.why: "This creature can't block" was unread. eff:cant-block-self is the -self word for a creature that cannot block, as distinct from eff:cant-block which stops someone else's creature.

kept.name: Mindleecher
kept.why: It exiles the top card of each opponent's library and lets you look at and play those cards. That is exile plus impulse draw, not milling: mill means library to graveyard and nothing here reaches a graveyard, so eff:mill would offer this card to a self-mill or graveyard deck it does nothing for. Mindleecher is a 4/5, and pt:big means power 5 or more.

kept.name: Deluge of Doom
kept.why: "All creatures get -X/-X" with no restriction is a symmetric board wipe that kills your own creatures too, which is exactly what scope:wipe exists to say. Without it the anti-synergy check cannot keep this out of a go-wide or tokens deck. Same shape as Toxic Deluge and Bane of the Living.

kept.name: Agent of Erebos
kept.why: "Exile target player's graveyard" is the whole card and it carried no effect word at all. eff:exile-graveyard is the graveyard-hate word kept apart from eff:exile, which matters because this must not read as creature removal. Constellation triggers on this creature entering as well as other enchantments, so trig:enters-self belongs beside trig:enters-other.

kept.name: Arbiter of Woe
kept.why: "As an additional cost to cast this spell, sacrifice a creature" was unread. cost:cast-sacrifice is the word for an additional cast cost, distinct from cost:sacrifice (an activated outlet), and it is why this card belongs in a deck with fodder.

kept.name: Grand Entryway // Elegant Rotunda
kept.why: The front half creates a 1/1 Glimmer token and nothing recorded it. The +1/+1 counters on up to two creatures make them bigger, matching how eff:add-counters and eff:pump are paired on the fully-read cards in this batch (Lightfoot Technique, The Destined White Mage).

kept.name: Nightblade Brigade
kept.why: Mobilize 1 is "Whenever this creature attacks, create a tapped and attacking token". The token creation was read, the attack trigger that produces it was not, so nothing tells an attack-matters deck this card is one of theirs.

kept.name: Krav, the Unredeemed
kept.why: Partner with is "When this creature enters, target player may put Regna into their hand from their library, then shuffle". eff:search-library was recorded but the entry trigger that causes it, the shuffle, and the library zone were all missing.

kept.name: Fabrication Foundry
kept.why: "Exile one or more other artifacts you control with total mana value X" is an activation cost that eats your own artifacts. That is the card's whole engine and it was unread, so nothing marks it as an artifact sacrifice outlet.

kept.name: Pestilence Demon
kept.why: "1 damage to each creature and each player" hits everything, which is what scope:all says, and it hits you too, which is what eff:damage-self says. Recorded as a bare eff:damage it reads as targeted removal rather than a repeatable symmetric sweeper.

kept.name: Wizard's Rockets
kept.why: This is a mana rock and carried no mana word at all. "{X}, {T}, Sacrifice this artifact: Add X mana in any combination of colors" gives all three: it adds mana, it taps, and it eats itself. Only the replacement-draw was read, so the engine could not offer it as ramp or fixing.

kept.name: Fishing Gear
kept.why: "Exile the top card of that player's library" was unread; only the downstream put-onto-battlefield and token were. The exile and both zones are what make this a library-attack Equipment rather than a plain pump.

kept.name: The Dominion Bracelet
kept.why: "+1/+1" is a pump and was unread. "Exile The Dominion Bracelet" is the activation cost of the granted ability, which cost:exile-self names. The player-control effect itself has no word, hence the proposal.

kept.name: Path to Redemption
kept.why: This is a Pacifism-style removal Aura you put on an opponent's creature, and eff:exile-own says the opposite: it means blinking your own permanent, which would offer this to a blink deck as an enabler it can never be. "Enchanted creature can't attack or block" is the main clause and was unread, and the 1/1 Ally token was unread too.

kept.name: Rat Out
kept.why: "You create a 1/1 black Rat creature token" was unread. Half of a two-line instant, and the half a tokens or sacrifice deck plays it for.

kept.name: Leyline Binding
kept.why: The card carried no effect word at all. "Exile target nonland permanent an opponent controls" is the whole card and Domain reducing its own cost by {1} per basic land type is why it is played at one mana. Without eff:exile it cannot be offered as removal to any deck.

kept.name: Rocket-Powered Goblin Glider
kept.why: Mayhem lets you cast this card from your graveyard after discarding it, and the entry trigger reads "if it was cast from your graveyard". eff:recur-self is the word for a permanent that brings itself back, and it is what makes this Equipment attractive to a discard or graveyard deck.

kept.name: Razaketh's Rite
kept.why: "then shuffle" was unread. Small, but the shuffle is a real clause and matters to decks that stack their library.

kept.name: Soul of Eternity
kept.why: Encore was read only as eff:copy. It also creates token copies, gives them haste, costs you exiling this card from your graveyard, and operates from the graveyard at all, which is the reason a reanimator deck wants it.

kept.name: Sanguine Evangelist
kept.why: Battle cry is "Whenever this creature attacks, each other attacking creature gets +1/+0". Neither the attack trigger nor the team pump was recorded, so a go-wide aggro deck cannot see the card's anthem half at all.

kept.name: Chancellor of the Annex
kept.why: Both abilities counter a spell "unless that player pays {1}", which is a tax rather than a hard counter. eff:counter alone overstates it, and eff:unless-pays is the word for the tax that is actually what this card does.

kept.name: Skyclave Cleric // Skyclave Basilica
kept.why: The land half, "{T}: Add {W}", was entirely unread, so a modal double-faced land reads as a creature that cannot produce mana. Skyclave Cleric costs {1}{W}, so its mana value is 2 and mv:cheap applies.

kept.name: Valiant Changeling
kept.why: Its entire first line is a cost reduction on itself ("costs {1} less to cast for each creature type among creatures you control") and no facet recorded it. Same shape as Ghalta.

kept.name: Accursed Witch // Infectious Curse
kept.why: "When this creature dies, return it to the battlefield transformed" is a self-recursion from the graveyard and nothing recorded it. The back face's "At the beginning of enchanted player's upkeep" is an upkeep trigger with no trigger word at all; the drain effects were recorded but the timing was not.

kept.name: Spawn of Mayhem
kept.why: "deals 1 damage to each player" includes you, which is what -self records. Only the outgoing eff:damage was written down.

kept.name: Koskun Falls
kept.why: The card had a trigger timing and nothing else. Upkeep asks you to tap an untapped creature you control (eff:tap-own). The second line is a Ghostly Prison: all creatures cannot attack you unless their controller pays {2}.

kept.name: Tetzimoc, Primal Death
kept.why: The activated ability puts a prey counter on target creature and no counter effect was recorded. The enters trigger destroys EACH creature your opponents control with a prey counter, which is mass removal rather than a single destroy.

kept.name: Zhentarim Bandit
kept.why: "you may pay 1 life" is a life cost and was not recorded.

kept.name: Fated Return
kept.why: It reanimates from ANY graveyard "under your control", so it steals from opponents. Dredge the Mire carries eff:gain-control for the same wording.

kept.name: Atraxa's Skitterfang
kept.why: It grants your choice of flying, vigilance, deathtouch OR lifelink and only vigilance was written down, so three of the four grants were lost. The choice itself is unrecorded, and "enters with three oil counters on it" puts counters on itself.

kept.name: Martyr's Bond
kept.why: Every opponent sacrifices on every nonland permanent of yours dying; the effect hits the whole table, not one player.

kept.name: Ominous Harvest
kept.why: Gravestorm counts permanents put into a graveyard from the battlefield this turn, so the card is keyed on the graveyard and nothing said so.

kept.name: Safana, Calimport Cutthroat
kept.why: Treasure tokens are mana. The corpus records eff:add-mana on Zhentarim Bandit for the same Treasure trigger; Safana's reminder text is simply absent from the printed line.

kept.name: Insatiable Frugivore
kept.why: It creates Food tokens and no token effect was recorded at all (only the incidental eff:gain-life). The pump ability costs Sacrifice X Foods, grants menace, and pumps every creature you control. The enters trigger exiles three cards from your graveyard, so it is keyed on the graveyard.

kept.name: Technodrome
kept.why: "This creature can't attack or block unless its power is 6 or greater" is half the card and neither restriction was recorded.

kept.name: Flicker
kept.why: It exiles a permanent and returns it immediately: this is the archetypal blink, and the blink word was missing while only the generic exile and return were present.

kept.name: Arcbound Javelineer
kept.why: The ability costs {T} plus removing counters; the tap half of the cost was not recorded.

kept.name: Alacrian Armory
kept.why: "that permanent ... becomes an artifact creature if it's a Vehicle" turns a noncreature permanent into a creature and nothing recorded it.

kept.name: Commune with Evil
kept.why: Nothing is exiled by this card, so both the exile-zone word and impulse (which means exiling off the top to play the cards) are wrong. Three of the four cards go to your own graveyard, which is self-mill and fills the yard.

kept.name: Gideon of the Trials
kept.why: The 0 ability turns him into a 4/4 creature with indestructible; the animation and the indestructible grant were both missing, only the static P/T setting was recorded.

kept.name: Tivash, Gloom Summoner
kept.why: "you may pay X life" is a life cost and was not recorded.

kept.name: Karai, Future of the Foot
kept.why: Sneak's alternative cost is returning an unblocked attacker you control to hand. Spider-Man, Web-Slinger carries cost:return-to-hand for the identical mechanic.

kept.name: Oathkeeper, Takeno's Daisho
kept.why: "return that card to the battlefield under your control if it's a Samurai" reanimates the dead equipped creature and no return effect was recorded, nor the graveyard it comes from.

kept.name: Intrepid Adversary
kept.why: It puts valor counters on itself and that is the whole engine of the card; only the resulting pump was recorded. The repeatable "you may pay {1}{W} any number of times" is exactly a pay-for-more effect.

kept.name: Azula Always Lies
kept.why: "Choose one or both" is a modal spell and the choice was not recorded.

kept.name: Live or Die
kept.why: "Choose one" is a modal spell and the choice was not recorded.

kept.name: Dredge the Mire
kept.why: Every opponent is made to give up a creature card, so the effect hits the whole table rather than one target.

kept.name: Deadly Cover-Up
kept.why: Only the board wipe was read. The whole second half - exile a card from an opponent's graveyard, then exile every copy of it from their graveyard, hand and library - produced nothing. eff:search-library deliberately not added: it searches an OPPONENT's library, and that word means tutoring for yourself.

kept.name: Cryptic Spires
kept.why: A mana land carrying no mana word at all. '{T}: Add one mana of either of the circled colors' is a tap cost and an add-mana effect; the engine read only acost:1.

kept.name: Raven Eagle
kept.why: Two clauses lost. It creates a Clue token when a creature card is exiled, and the drain is on 'whenever you draw your second card each turn', which is a draw trigger and the reason this card is played. Graveyard is the zone it exiles from.

kept.name: Splendor Mare
kept.why: The cycling trigger was never read. 'Put a lifelink counter on target creature you control' both puts a counter and grants lifelink to another creature; kw:lifelink only records the printed keyword on this body.

kept.name: Silverquill Lecturer
kept.why: Demonstrate's copies each become a token, so this genuinely makes token copies of every creature spell you cast. eff:copy alone understates it.

kept.name: Sanwell, Avenger Ace
kept.why: The whole first ability - 'prevent all damage that would be dealt to Sanwell' - produced nothing. The tap trigger exiles the top six and lets you cast from among them, which is exactly eff:impulse's gloss; eff:look-and-pick alone misses that the cards go to exile.

kept.name: Bogslither's Embrace
kept.why: Blight 1 puts a -1/-1 counter on a creature you control as an additional cost to cast. kw:blight records the keyword; nothing recorded that paying it costs a counter, which is the whole reason this card sits in a -1/-1 deck.

kept.name: Dungeoneer's Pack
kept.why: It creates a Treasure token and nothing said so - eff:add-mana came from the reminder text, not from the token being made. The activation cost also includes {T}, which was dropped.

kept.name: Nightmare Unmaking
kept.why: It is a modal card ('Choose one'), and both modes compare creature POWER against your hand size. Neither the mode choice nor the power comparison was recorded. scope:wipe deliberately withheld: the filter is dynamic and a deck can build around it, and that word is reserved for symmetric destruction.

kept.name: Costume Closet
kept.why: Two of three abilities half-read. Moving a counter OFF this artifact is a removal of counters as well as an addition, the activation costs {T}, and the third ability triggers when another creature you control leaves the battlefield - no leave trigger was recorded.

kept.name: Overencumbered
kept.why: The entire second ability was unread: at the beginning of combat the enchanted opponent must pay {1} per artifact or their creatures cannot attack. That is a combat-step trigger, a tax, and an attack restriction - this is a stax card and carried no effect word at all. eff:create-token deliberately withheld: the tokens go to the OPPONENT, so recording it would file this as a tokens payoff.

kept.name: Lay Down Arms
kept.why: The life goes to the exiled creature's CONTROLLER, which is the opponent almost every time. This is a one-mana white removal spell with a drawback, not a lifegain card, and the word would put it in lifegain decks.

kept.name: Reality Smasher
kept.why: Its famous ability produced only eff:discard. It triggers on becoming the target of an opponent's spell, counters that spell, and the discard is the tax that avoids the counter. Three of the four words describing that were missing.

kept.name: Doom's Time Platform
kept.why: It puts two time counters on the exiled card and grants suspend, which ends in casting it without paying its mana cost. eff:return-from is the only word present and the card never returns anything - the payoff is a free cast out of exile. eff:exile-graveyard deliberately withheld: this exiles YOUR OWN graveyard as a payoff and that word means graveyard hate.

kept.name: Obzedat, Ghost Council
kept.why: Only half the blink was read. It exiles itself at end step and returns to the battlefield at the beginning of your NEXT UPKEEP - the return and its upkeep trigger were both missing, so the card read as a one-way self-exile.

kept.name: Deathrender
kept.why: The reason this card is played - putting a creature card from your HAND straight onto the battlefield when the equipped creature dies - produced nothing. That is eff:put-onto-battlefield's exact gloss.

kept.name: Thief of Blood
kept.why: 'Remove all counters from all permanents' is a symmetric, global effect and nothing recorded its scope. eff:remove-counters alone reads as a targeted counter removal.

kept.name: Eldrazi Mimic
kept.why: Changing its base power and toughness to match another creature is eff:set-pt and was missing entirely. scope:all is wrong: the ability touches only this creature, and the word came from the 'another colorless creature you control' selector rather than from anything global.

kept.name: Orochi Hatchery
kept.why: Its cost is {X}{X}, so mana value is 0 anywhere but the stack and it reads as a two-mana card. Nobody ever casts this for zero; calling it cheap is a rules artefact, not a fact about the card.

kept.name: Sun Droplet
kept.why: The first ability was unread. 'Whenever you're dealt damage, put that many charge counters on this artifact' is a damage trigger and a counter-adding effect; only the upkeep half was recorded.

kept.name: Spectral Steel
kept.why: The graveyard ability returns an Aura or Equipment CARD from your graveyard to your hand. eff:bounce-own means returning your own creatures from the battlefield to hand, which this never does - it is recursion, not a bounce, and the graveyard zone was not recorded at all.

kept.name: Clot Sliver
kept.why: 'All Slivers have...' grants the regenerate ability to every Sliver on the battlefield, including opponents'. eff:protect is there but nothing records that the grant is global rather than to itself.

kept.name: Carrion Grub
kept.why: 'This creature gets +X/+0, where X is the greatest power among creature cards in your graveyard' is a pump and produced nothing - the card read as a four-mana mill-four with no body-growing clause.

kept.name: Rhoda, Geist Avenger
kept.why: Partner with fetches Timin from a library to hand on entry and shuffles, and no entry trigger or zone was recorded although eff:search-library was. scope:all is wrong: the counter ability watches one opponent's creature becoming tapped, which is not a global effect.

kept.name: Ring of Three Wishes
kept.why: The tutored card goes to your hand and you then shuffle; neither was recorded. scope:all is wrong - this is an unrestricted tutor for ONE card, and 'search your library for a card' is breadth of choice, not a global effect.

kept.name: Reiver Demon
kept.why: 'Destroy all nonartifact, nonblack creatures' is a mass destroy and no scope word was recorded. scope:wipe deliberately withheld: black and artifact creatures survive, so a black deck's own board largely lives and this is a payoff rather than a symmetric wipe.

kept.name: Death-Priest of Myrkul
kept.why: 'You may pay {1}. If you do, create a token' is an optional-payment effect and nothing recorded it, so the token looked unconditional.

kept.name: Eye of Duskmantle
kept.why: This card never returns anything to any zone. It lets you PLAY LANDS and CAST SPELLS from your graveyard, which are two distinct existing words, and eff:return-from would file it as recursion when it is a graveyard-as-second-hand card.

kept.name: Kusari-Gama
kept.why: The trigger and its scope were both lost. It fires when the equipped creature deals damage to a blocker and then deals that much to EACH OTHER CREATURE the defending player controls, which is the whole card and reads as a one-sided sweeper.

kept.name: Curse of Thirst
kept.why: The damage happens at the beginning of enchanted player's upkeep and no timing trigger was recorded, so the damage read as a one-shot.

kept.name: Born to Drive
kept.why: Carried no effect word of any kind. It is an Aura (attaches), it gives +1/+1 per creature and Vehicle (pump), and its channel ability discards it to create two Pilot tokens - all four clauses were unread.

kept.name: Marshland Bloodcaster
kept.why: The activated ability costs {T} and that was dropped along with everything else on the card - it carries no eff: word at all today.

kept.name: Mishra's Self-Replicator
kept.why: The trigger is on spells YOU cast, not any player's, and the copy only happens if you pay {1}. Bare trig:cast loses both the ownership and the optional payment.

kept.name: Quest for the Nihil Stone
kept.why: It puts a quest counter on ITSELF whenever an opponent discards, and nothing recorded that it accumulates counters at all. The discard trigger has no word in the vocabulary.

kept.name: Extract a Confession
kept.why: With evidence collected it takes the creature with the GREATEST POWER, which is a power comparison nothing recorded. The evidence exile is specifically an additional cost to CAST. It edicts every opponent, the same mass shape Relic Vial carries scope:all for.

kept.name: Protector of the Wastes
kept.why: Its exile ability triggers on entering and no enter trigger was recorded at all. Monstrosity 3 puts three +1/+1 counters on it, so it grows itself and nothing said so.

kept.name: Mage's Attendant
kept.why: The token it makes is a counterspell on a stick (counter target noncreature spell unless its controller pays {1}). The list recorded that a token is made and nothing about what the token does, so the card is invisible to anything looking for interaction.

kept.name: Thran Spider
kept.why: It creates two Powerstone tokens and eff:create-token was missing. eff:impulse is wrong: looking at the top four and putting one in HAND exiles nothing and plays nothing off the top. Nothing on this card touches exile, so cares:zone:exile is a phantom.

kept.name: Petty Larceny
kept.why: It exiles the top two cards of an opponent's library face down and lets you play them, which is exactly impulse (from their library rather than yours). None of the exile-and-play half was recorded, only the Treasure.

kept.name: Cyan, Vengeful Samurai
kept.why: His only ability triggers on creature cards LEAVING your graveyard, and no trigger word was recorded. trig:leaves and trig:leaves-self both mean leaving the battlefield, which would misfile him as a blink payoff; trig:zone-change is the word for an odd-zone trigger. Deliberately NOT adding eff:reduce-cost: his first line reduces only his own cost, and PLAN_RULES turns that word into "wants big expensive spells", which is the opposite of a graveyard-creature deck.

kept.name: Troop of Ponies
kept.why: The ability costs {2}, {T} and a sacrifice; the tap half of the cost was missing. It shuffles at the end, which nothing recorded.

kept.name: Amaranthine Wall
kept.why: {2}: gains indestructible changes no power or toughness, so eff:pump is wrong. Keeping a creature alive through a removal spell is exactly eff:protect.

kept.name: Skirsdag High Priest
kept.why: Nothing here affects everything. It makes one Demon token, gated on a creature having died. The morbid condition is a check, not a mass effect, and scope:all tells the engine this is a board-wide card.

kept.name: Lucky Clover
kept.why: It triggers on YOU casting an Adventure INSTANT OR SORCERY. Only the bare trig:cast was recorded, so no spellslinger plan keyed on casting instants or sorceries can see it.

kept.name: Night of Souls' Betrayal
kept.why: "All creatures get -1/-1" makes creatures smaller. eff:pump reads it as an anthem, which is the opposite card. Withering Curse in this same batch carries eff:shrink for -2/-2.

kept.name: Cheeky House-Mouse // Squeak By
kept.why: The Adventure gives +1/+1 until end of turn and only the unblockable half was recorded.

kept.name: Splinter, Hamato Yoshi
kept.why: Sneak is a ninjutsu-shaped alternative cost: you return an unblocked attacker you control to hand to cast him. Nothing recorded that casting him costs you a permanent back to hand.

kept.name: Dead of Winter
kept.why: -X/-X on all nonsnow creatures is a sweeper, not an anthem. Same correction as Night of Souls' Betrayal.

kept.name: Feed the Infection
kept.why: The corrupted clause drains EVERY opponent with three or more poison counters, and the list only recorded the self-draw half's life loss. There is no word for caring about poison counters.

kept.name: Lord Jyscal Guado
kept.why: Investigate makes a Clue, and a Clue is "{2}, Sacrifice: Draw a card". Foreboding Fruit in this same batch correctly carries eff:gain-life for the Food token it makes, so a token's own ability does count; this card's draw was missing.

kept.name: Foreboding Fruit
kept.why: Adamant creates a Food token and eff:create-token was missing entirely, even though the downstream eff:gain-life from that Food was recorded. The adamant condition is literally about how much black mana was spent.

kept.name: Relic Vial
kept.why: The granted Cleric ability is "whenever a creature you control DIES, each opponent loses 1 life and YOU GAIN 1 LIFE". Both the death trigger and the lifegain were missing, which is the half that makes it an aristocrats card.

kept.name: Ajani Goldmane
kept.why: The -6 creates a white Avatar creature token and nothing recorded that this card makes tokens.

kept.name: Ozox, the Clattering King
kept.why: Dying creates Jumblebones, which was not recorded at all. He can't block, and the loop returns Ozox himself from the graveyard, which is what makes him repeatable sacrifice fodder rather than a one-shot.

kept.name: Basilica Shepherd
kept.why: It creates two Phyrexian Mite tokens. The downstream eff:poison from their toxic was recorded and the token creation itself was not.

kept.name: Overseer of Vault 76
kept.why: First Contact triggers on himself OR another small creature you control entering, and no enter trigger of any kind was recorded. The combat ability is paid for by removing three quest counters, and it pumps EVERY creature you control.

kept.name: Pox Plague
kept.why: Losing half your life is the spell's EFFECT, not a cost paid to cast it; there is no cost on this card at all. It empties every board including your own, so a go-wide or token deck must be warned off it the way it is warned off a destroy-all.

kept.name: Inversion Behemoth
kept.why: The card had NO effect word at all. Switching power and toughness of any number of target creatures is a power/toughness rewrite, and eff:set-pt is the closest true word; without it the engine reads this as a 5-mana creature that does nothing.

kept.name: Isolated Watchtower
kept.why: It reveals the top card of your library and puts a basic land from there onto the battlefield. That is land ramp out of the library, and only the scry half was recorded.

kept.name: Saving Grace
kept.why: The whole point of the card is unrecorded. "All damage that would be dealt this turn to you and permanents you control is dealt to enchanted creature instead" is a damage redirection and eff:redirect-damage (44 cards) is exactly that word. Only eff:pump (+0/+3) was read.

kept.name: Boneyard Scourge
kept.why: It returns a card from graveyard to battlefield, so eff:return-from belongs beside eff:recur-self (Royal Warden and Platoon Dispenser both carry the pair for the same shape). "You may pay {1}{B}. If you do, return this card" is the do-if-cost-paid shape.

kept.name: Relic Seeker
kept.why: Renown 1 puts a +1/+1 counter on THIS creature, which is eff:add-counters-self and not only the generic eff:add-counters. It also searches your library for the Equipment.

kept.name: Citizen's Crowbar
kept.why: "Equipped creature gets +1/+1" was never read - Captain's Claws carries eff:pump for +1/+0. The granted ability's cost includes "Sacrifice Citizen's Crowbar", and the engine already read that quoted ability (eff:destroy is present), so its self-sacrifice cost should be there too.

kept.name: Oblivion's Hunger
kept.why: The card changes no power or toughness at all - it grants indestructible and draws. eff:pump is wrong and would make it read as a combat trick. Granting indestructible to keep a creature alive is eff:protect, which Cauldron Haze already carries for the same job.

kept.name: Mavinda, Students' Advocate
kept.why: Her entire ability produced no verb. "You may cast target instant or sorcery card from your graveyard" is eff:cast-from-graveyard, and "it costs {8} more to cast this way" is eff:increase-cost.

kept.name: Iron Man Armor
kept.why: "{2}: If this Equipment isn't a creature, it becomes a 0/0 Construct Hero artifact creature" turns a permanent into a creature, which is eff:animate.

kept.name: Frostwalk Bastion
kept.why: Two of its three abilities produced no verb. "{1}{S}: this land becomes a 2/3 Construct artifact creature" is eff:animate, and "tap that creature and it doesn't untap during its controller's next untap step" is eff:tap.

kept.name: Eye Collector
kept.why: "Each player mills a card" hits every player, which is what scope:all says. Ebon Drake carries it for the same "whenever a player" breadth.

kept.name: Bebop, Skull & Crossbones
kept.why: Its combat trigger was read for nothing: "you may draw X cards ... you lose X life" is eff:draw and eff:lose-life and neither is present. Partner with is a genuine enters-the-battlefield trigger (the engine already pulled eff:search-library out of it) so trig:enters and trig:enters-self follow, along with the library it searches.

kept.name: Horobi, Death's Wail
kept.why: "Whenever a creature becomes the target" is any creature under any player's control, so scope:all applies as it does on Priest of the Crossing and Ebon Drake.

kept.name: Cemetery Protector
kept.why: Two whole clauses were unread. "Exile a card from a graveyard" is eff:exile-graveyard, and "whenever you play a land or cast a spell" is a cast trigger of your own spells - Diary of Dreams carries trig:cast, trig:cast-own and cares:zone:stack for the same wording.

kept.name: Tymaret, Chosen from Death
kept.why: The card carried no effect word at all. "Exile up to two target cards from graveyards" is graveyard hate, "you gain 1 life for each creature card exiled this way" is eff:gain-life, and "Tymaret's toughness is equal to your devotion to black" is a characteristic-defining toughness, which is eff:set-pt.

kept.name: Tale of Momo
kept.why: It searches your library, and the engine recorded only the graveyard half of "search your library and/or graveyard".

kept.name: Depopulate
kept.why: "Each player who controls a multicolored creature draws a card" makes every qualifying player draw, not just you, which is what eff:draw-each says. Plain eff:draw reads as card advantage for the caster.

kept.name: Fight as One
kept.why: Both modes grant indestructible to save a creature, which is eff:protect - the same reason Cauldron Haze carries it. The pump is only incidental to that.

kept.name: Mirror of the Forebears
kept.why: An artifact that becomes a copy of a creature becomes a creature, which is eff:animate. eff:copy alone does not say that the artifact itself starts attacking.

kept.name: Feat of Resistance
kept.why: "It gains protection from the color of your choice" is unrecorded - grants:protection is the printed-style word for it and eff:protect is what the card is FOR. Only the counter was read.

kept.name: Hildibrand Manderville // Gentleman's Rise
kept.why: "Creature tokens you control get +1/+1" is an anthem and produced nothing - History of Benalia carries eff:pump and scope:all for the same shape. "You may cast it from your graveyard as an Adventure" is eff:cast-from-graveyard, and it is how the card brings itself back, so eff:recur-self and the graveyard it cares about belong too.

kept.name: Druidic Satchel
kept.why: Only the Saproling branch was read. "If it's a land card, put that card onto the battlefield under your control" is a land off the top of the library, which is cares:zone:library-land and eff:put-onto-battlefield, and "you gain 2 life" is eff:gain-life.

kept.name: Darkness Descends
kept.why: Two -1/-1 counters on EACH creature makes every creature smaller, which is eff:shrink, and it is a symmetric sweeper that kills your own board as readily as theirs. That is the honest reading of scope:wipe and is why it must never be put in a go-wide deck; the counter word alone cannot say either thing.

kept.name: Pegasus Guardian // Rescue the Foal
kept.why: The whole Adventure half was unread. "Exile target creature you control, then return that card to the battlefield" is a blink, and eff:exile-own plus eff:return-from plus cares:zone:exile is exactly what a blink card carries.

kept.name: Hostile Hostel // Creeping Inn
kept.why: "Remove those counters, transform it" is eff:transform (kw:transform is only the printed keyword). The back face's whole ability hangs off "whenever this creature attacks" and there is no trig:attacks, and it exiles creature cards from YOUR graveyard, so cares:zone:graveyard belongs. Deliberately NOT eff:exile-graveyard: it feeds on its own graveyard and that word is graveyard hate, which would make the anti-synergy check refuse it in exactly the deck that wants it.

kept.name: Lulu, Loyal Hollyphant
kept.why: "Put a +1/+1 counter on each tapped creature you control, then untap them" is a mass effect, which is how Priest of the Crossing and History of Benalia are marked.

kept.name: Cauldron Haze
kept.why: The card grants persist by name and nothing records which keyword it hands out - eff:protect alone cannot tell it apart from a fog or an indestructible trick.

kept.name: Shadowborn Apostle
kept.why: "Sacrifice six creatures named Shadowborn Apostle" is a sacrifice cost paid with other creatures and produced no word at all, and the Demon is put onto the battlefield from the library rather than drawn, which eff:search-library alone does not say.

kept.name: Investigator's Journal
kept.why: "This artifact enters with a number of suspect counters on it" puts counters on itself - Bone Devourer carries eff:add-counters-self for the identical "enters with counters" wording.

kept.name: History of Benalia
kept.why: Chapters I and II create a 2/2 Knight token each and the card carries no token verb whatsoever. The most played thing this card does was missing.

kept.name: Everglades
kept.why: "Sacrifice it unless you return an untapped Swamp you control to its owner's hand" is the karoo bounce-land cost, and cost:return-to-hand (41 cards, about the size of that cycle) is the word for it. Nothing recorded that the land costs you a land.

kept.name: Super-Soldier Serum
kept.why: "+2/+2" produced no eff:pump and first strike was not recorded as granted although vigilance was. The trigger is "whenever enchanted creature attacks or blocks" and only trig:blocks is present, so half the trigger is missing.

kept.name: Charnel Serenade
kept.why: "Exile Charnel Serenade with three time counters on it" exiles the card itself, which is eff:exile-self.

kept.name: Necron Monolith
kept.why: Crew 4 is literally "tap any number of creatures you control with total power 4 or more" as a cost, which is cost:tap-others. Nothing recorded that the card asks you to tap your board.

kept.name: Send in the Pest
kept.why: "Each opponent discards" is a multiplayer effect (scope:all, the same reading Thoughtrender Lamia in this batch already carries). The token it makes says "you gain 1 life", so the card does gain life.

kept.name: Apple of Eden, Isu Relic
kept.why: Only the costs were read. The ability taps ({T} in the cost), exiles an opponent's whole hand, makes the owner draw a card for each thing you play this way, and has a delayed end-step trigger returning the exiled cards to hand.

kept.name: Triskaidekaphobia
kept.why: Only the life loss was read. Both modes make players lose the game (eff:lose-game), one mode gains everyone life, the ability is modal ("choose one"), and every clause is "each player".

kept.name: Builder's Talent
kept.why: Level 3 returns a permanent card from your graveyard to the battlefield, which is unrecorded along with the graveyard it reads. Level 2 triggers on other permanents you control entering, not only on itself.

kept.name: Herald of Amity
kept.why: "Exile the top eight cards of your library. You may cast an Aura spell from among them without paying its mana cost" is exactly eff:impulse. Only the free cast was recorded, not the exile off the top or that it reads your library.

kept.name: Transmogrant's Crown
kept.why: It is an Equipment with Equip {2} or {B} and nothing said it attaches to a creature. Bonesplitter in this same batch carries eff:attach for the identical clause.

kept.name: Harvestrite Host
kept.why: "Then draw a card if this is the second time this ability has resolved this turn" was not read at all. The trigger is "this creature or another Rabbit", so it fires on itself entering too.

kept.name: Soul Enervation
kept.why: "Each opponent loses 1 life" is scope:all. The second ability triggers on creature cards leaving your graveyard and no trigger word was recorded for it at all.

kept.name: Banewhip Punisher
kept.why: The activated ability is "{B}, Sacrifice this creature: Destroy target creature that has a -1/-1 counter on it". Sacrificing itself as a cost was not recorded.

kept.name: Paradise Plume
kept.why: Two of its three lines were unread: "Whenever a player casts a spell of the chosen color, you may gain 1 life" is a cast trigger that gains life, and the mana ability costs {T}.

kept.name: Icingdeath, Frost Tyrant
kept.why: It creates an Equipment token on death and nothing said it makes a token. The token gives +2/+0 and has an attack trigger; the engine already took eff:tap from that same token text, so the rest of it belongs too.

kept.name: Ambitious Farmhand // Seasoned Cathar
kept.why: "then shuffle" and the Coven ability "Transform this creature" were both unread. kw:transform is the printed keyword; eff:transform is the card actually doing it.

kept.name: Rally the Ancestors
kept.why: "Exile those creatures at the beginning of your next upkeep" is a delayed upkeep trigger and no trigger word was recorded. Deliberately not adding eff:exile for that clause: it exiles your own returned creatures, so tagging it would read as removal, which this card is not.

kept.name: Bessie, the Doctor's Roadster
kept.why: Crew 2 taps creatures you control as a cost, which nothing recorded.

kept.name: Sanitarium Skeleton
kept.why: "{2}{B}: Return this card from your graveyard to your hand" is the definition of eff:recur-self, and it was carrying only the generic eff:return-from.

kept.name: Tomik, Distinguished Advokist
kept.why: Tomik exiles nothing from anywhere; eff:exile-graveyard would file a protective stax piece as graveyard hate. What he actually does is make lands and land cards in graveyards untargetable by opponents, which is granting hexproof.

kept.name: From Father to Son
kept.why: It searches your library and nothing recorded that it reads the library zone.

kept.name: Prowling Geistcatcher
kept.why: Only the counters were read. It triggers whenever you sacrifice another creature (trig:sacrificed), exiles that creature of yours, and returns every card exiled with it to the battlefield when it leaves.

kept.name: Elven Passage
kept.why: "then shuffle" and "If you do, untap that land" were both unread.

kept.name: Silumgar Assassin
kept.why: Both of its abilities are power comparisons: creatures with power greater than its own can't block it, and the megamorph trigger destroys a creature with power 3 or less. Nothing recorded that it reads power.

kept.name: Swift Demise
kept.why: "Destroy each creature you don't control that was dealt damage this turn" is a mass destroy, not a single target. Not scope:wipe, since your own creatures are spared.

kept.name: Abyssal Gatekeeper
kept.why: The whole effect was missing: "each player sacrifices a creature of their choice" is an edict on every player, and the card carried no effect word at all.

kept.name: Strategic Betrayal
kept.why: Nothing is sacrificed; the opponent EXILES a creature they control, and eff:exile already records that. Leaving eff:sacrifice on it would let a card that is pure removal be read as a sacrifice outlet for an aristocrats deck.

kept.name: Skybind
kept.why: Constellation reads "this enchantment or another enchantment you control enters", so it fires on itself as well. The exiled permanent comes back on a delayed end-step trigger, which had no trigger word.

kept.name: Desperate Plea
kept.why: "As an additional cost to cast this spell, sacrifice a creature" was unread, and "Choose one or both" makes it modal.

kept.name: Konda's Banner
kept.why: Both anthem lines were unread: creatures sharing a color, and creatures sharing a creature type, each get +1/+1. It is a mass pump, not just an Equipment that attaches.

kept.name: Call a Surprise Witness
kept.why: The second and third sentences were unread: it puts a flying counter on the returned creature, which both places a counter and gives that creature flying.

kept.name: Norika Yamazaki, the Poet
kept.why: The whole payoff clause produced nothing. Letting you cast an enchantment card from your graveyard is exactly eff:cast-from-graveyard; only the trigger half was recorded.

kept.name: Hall of Triumph
kept.why: It recorded the 'choose a color' clause and dropped the effect that clause exists for: a static +1/+1 to every creature you control of that colour.

kept.name: Egon, God of Death // Throne of Death
kept.why: The back face's activated ability was unread: it taps and exiles a creature card from your graveyard as costs. Both faces are built on the graveyard and no cares:zone:graveyard was recorded.

kept.name: Thornplate Intimidator
kept.why: Only the life-loss mode of the enters trigger was read. The opponent's two alternatives, sacrificing a nonland permanent or discarding a card, are real modes of the card.

kept.name: Starlight Spectacular
kept.why: The pump was recorded with no trigger at all. It happens at the beginning of combat on your turn.

kept.name: Alchemist's Vial
kept.why: Everything after the cantrip was unread: the ability taps and sacrifices the artifact as costs, and stops a creature attacking and blocking.

kept.name: Silver Sable, Mercenary Leader
kept.why: The attack trigger's actual effect, granting lifelink to a modified creature, was not recorded; only the enters trigger's counter was.

kept.name: Restless Bloodseeker // Bloodsoaked Reveler
kept.why: Sacrificing two Blood tokens is a sacrifice cost, and what it buys is a transform, neither of which was recorded. The back face's drain hits each opponent.

kept.name: Ransom Note
kept.why: The sacrifice ability is modal and its cost sacrifices the Clue, and goading a creature was left unrecorded although kw:goad is on the card.

kept.name: Heavenly Blademaster
kept.why: The third line, a static anthem giving every other creature you control +1/+1 for each Aura and Equipment on it, produced nothing.

kept.name: Lightmine Field
kept.why: There is no 'unless' clause anywhere on this card. It deals damage to attacking creatures unconditionally; nothing taxes an opponent or offers them a payment.

kept.name: Lokhust Heavy Destroyer
kept.why: The enters trigger is an edict on every player and was entirely unread; only the unearth half was recorded.

kept.name: Electrostatic Pummeler
kept.why: The pump is sized by the creature's own power, which is the whole point of the card and is what makes it a power-matters card.

kept.name: Eland Umbra
kept.why: Umbra armor is the reason to play this: the enchanted creature survives destruction and the Aura dies instead. Only the +0/+4 was recorded.

kept.name: Protector of the Crown
kept.why: The second line, which redirects all damage that would be dealt to you onto this creature, produced nothing.

kept.name: Scarblade's Malice
kept.why: The delayed trigger that makes the Elf token fires when the creature dies, and no death trigger was recorded.

kept.name: Tenacious Underdog
kept.why: The blitz cost is {2}{B}{B} plus 2 life, an additional life payment made as you cast it.

kept.name: Gate to the Afterlife
kept.why: The activated ability was read only as a library search. It taps and sacrifices the artifact as costs, puts the found card straight onto the battlefield, and shuffles.

kept.name: Verrak, Warped Sengir
kept.why: The trigger is entirely about life being paid to activate an ability and paying that much again; no life cost was recorded.

kept.name: Invasion of Innistrad // Deluge of the Dead
kept.why: The back face's activated ability exiles a target card from ANY graveyard, which is genuine graveyard hate and was completely unread.

kept.name: Myriad Construct
kept.why: The card's defining ability, triggering on becoming the target of a spell and making Construct tokens equal to its power, produced no verb and no trigger.

kept.name: All-Fates Stalker
kept.why: The card carried no effect at all. Its enters trigger is an O-Ring style exile of a creature, held in exile until this creature leaves the battlefield.

kept.name: Life's Finale
kept.why: 'Destroy all creatures' is a symmetric board wipe that kills your own board too, and only the generic scope:all was recorded.

kept.name: Spider-Man, Peter Parker
kept.why: His whole engine is triggered by gaining life; trig:gains-life records the trigger but nothing records that the deck should be built around lifegain.

kept.name: Foggy Swamp Visions
kept.why: It creates token COPIES of the exiled creature cards, then sacrifices those tokens - both unrecorded. It returns nothing: the cards are exiled permanently, so eff:return-from is wrong. The additional cost is waterbend (tapping artifacts and creatures, already recorded as cost:tap-others); the exile is the spell's effect, not a cost, so cost:exile is wrong.

kept.name: Vault 101: Birthday Party
kept.why: Chapter I creates two tokens and chapters II and III put an Aura or Equipment onto the battlefield from hand or graveyard. None of those three effects was recorded - the list only had eff:attach from the last clause.

kept.name: Ajani, Outland Chaperone
kept.why: The -8 looks at the top X cards of your library and takes cards from among them; nothing recorded that it reads the library at all. Deliberately not adding eff:put-onto-battlefield: its gloss is specifically from your hand, and it feeds a ramp signal that would be wrong for a nonland-permanent effect.

kept.name: Terrarion
kept.why: It is a mana rock and carried no eff:add-mana at all - only the cantrip on death was read. The activated ability taps and sacrifices itself, neither recorded.

kept.name: Goryo's Vengeance
kept.why: The returned creature gains haste, which is the whole point of the card. Not adding eff:exile for the end-step clause: it exiles the creature this spell itself returned, so recording it would read as removal.

kept.name: Stronghold Assassin
kept.why: It destroys ONE target nonblack creature. Nothing about it is a mass effect; scope:all appears to have come from the nonblack filter.

kept.name: Sorin, Solemn Visitor
kept.why: The +1 gives all your creatures +1/+0 and lifelink - a team-wide anthem that was entirely unrecorded, so only the -2 token was read. The loyalty-adding cost was missing while cost:remove-counters was present.

kept.name: Raven of Fell Omens
kept.why: Each opponent loses life, which is a multiplayer-wide drain rather than a single target.

kept.name: Arrest
kept.why: This is the archetypal Pacifism-style answer: it turns a creature into a harmless permanent without destroying it. Without the word it carries the three cant- restrictions but is invisible as removal.

kept.name: Alien Symbiosis
kept.why: The Aura gives +1/+1 (only the menace half was read), and the card can be cast from your graveyard by discarding a card as an additional cost - a whole recursion clause that was unrecorded.

kept.name: Sejiri Steppe
kept.why: Protection from a colour of your choice keeps the creature alive; it changes no power or toughness, so eff:pump is a mis-read of 'gains'.

kept.name: Massacre
kept.why: The first line lets you cast it without paying its mana cost when the land condition is met, which is the reason the card is played and was not recorded.

kept.name: Evil Eye of Orms-by-Gore
kept.why: Both of its abilities were unread. It stops every non-Eye creature you control from attacking - a board-wide restriction - and it has a can't-be-blocked-except clause, the same shape already recorded as eff:cant-be-blocked on Relentless X-ATM092 in this batch.

kept.name: Face of Divinity
kept.why: The conditional clause grants first strike and lifelink; only the +2/+2 was read.

kept.name: Diviner's Wand
kept.why: The granted abilities include '{4}: Draw a card' and a draw trigger that grants flying. The card is a Wizard draw engine and carried no eff:draw at all.

kept.name: Ceremonial Knife
kept.why: Equipped creature gets +1/+0 and has a combat-damage trigger that creates a Blood token. Only eff:attach was read - none of the three things the Equipment actually does.

kept.name: Starlit Sanctum
kept.why: The white ability gains life equal to toughness and was entirely unread while the black one was. Both abilities sacrifice a Cleric, and the drain is sized by the sacrificed creature's power.

kept.name: Tainted Adversary
kept.why: It creates twice X 2/2 Zombie tokens and carried no eff:create-token - the whole payoff of the card. The repeatable optional payment is the do-if-cost-paid shape.

kept.name: Dark Privilege
kept.why: Sacrificing a creature is an activation cost that was unrecorded, and regenerating the enchanted creature is exactly what eff:protect means.

kept.name: Flesh-Eater Imp
kept.why: The pump is on itself only and nothing else on the card affects more than one permanent.

kept.name: Vanguard of the Restless
kept.why: Spirits you control get +1/+1 for each commander cast - a team anthem that was not recorded. The recursion is gated on an optional payment.

kept.name: Jinxed Choker
kept.why: The activated ability puts a charge counter on it or removes one; neither direction was recorded, so the card that is built entirely on its own counter count reads as having no way to change it.

kept.name: Call the Gatewatch
kept.why: The search ends with a shuffle, which was not recorded.

kept.name: Doom Reigns Supreme
kept.why: The whole second half is unrecorded: an opponent exiles their top five and you may cast two of them without paying their mana costs. That is a free-cast off the top of a library, and the deck plays it for that payoff rather than for the one-life drain.

kept.name: Blood Curdle
kept.why: The second sentence puts a menace counter on one of your creatures, granting it menace. Only the destroy half was read.

kept.name: Nadier, Agent of the Duskenel
kept.why: His first ability triggers when a TOKEN YOU CONTROL leaves, which is the other-permanent split; only trig:leaves-self from his own leave trigger was recorded, so a token deck cannot see him.

kept.name: Shaile, Dean of Radiance // Embrose, Dean of Shadow
kept.why: Both faces tap to activate, unrecorded. The back face's draw engine - a card whenever a countered creature you control dies - was entirely unread, and Shaile's ability counters EVERY creature that entered this turn rather than one target.

kept.name: Noosegraf Mob
kept.why: Every counter it places goes on itself (enters with five, then removes them). eff:add-counters-self already says that; the generic word makes it read as a counters-deck enabler that puts counters on your other permanents, which it never does.

kept.name: Eliminate the Competition
kept.why: "As an additional cost to cast this spell, sacrifice X creatures" is a cast cost, not a repeatable outlet. cost:sacrifice marks it as a sacrifice outlet an aristocrats deck can use at will, which it is not.

kept.name: Silversmote Ghoul
kept.why: The recursion trigger reads "if you gained 3 or more life this turn". Nothing in the list records that this card is a lifegain payoff, which is the only reason it is played.

kept.name: Adventurer's Airship
kept.why: Crew 2 taps other creatures you control as a cost. That is exactly cost:tap-others and it is the card's only way to attack.

kept.name: Lantern Scout
kept.why: The rally trigger reads "whenever this creature OR another Ally you control enters". Only trig:enters-other was recorded, so its own arrival is unrecorded.

kept.name: Safe Passage
kept.why: It is a fog that keeps your whole board alive, not merely a damage-prevention footnote: eff:protect is the word for keeping your creatures alive, and it covers you and every creature you control, which is scope:all.

kept.name: Treasure Keeper
kept.why: It reveals cards from the top of the library until it hits a cheap nonland card and puts the rest on the bottom. The library is where the whole effect happens and no word said so.

kept.name: Dark Impostor
kept.why: "This creature has all activated abilities of all creature cards exiled with it" is a genuine exile-zone payoff, not just an exile effect.

kept.name: Deploy the Gatewatch
kept.why: Nothing is exiled and nothing is played from exile. It looks at the top seven and puts planeswalkers onto the battlefield, rest on the bottom. eff:look-and-pick and eff:put-onto-battlefield already say that correctly; impulse draw is a different mechanic and this card would be offered to Prosper-style decks on a false claim.

kept.name: Ever After
kept.why: "Put Ever After on the bottom of its owner's library" is a second, real clause that moves a card between zones and nothing recorded it.

kept.name: Black Vise
kept.why: The entire damage clause is an upkeep trigger and no trigger word was recorded at all, so the card reads as having no timing. "As this artifact enters, choose an opponent" is also an on-entry effect.

kept.name: Beyond the Quiet
kept.why: Exiling all creatures is a one-sided-in-no-way board wipe that kills your own board too. Without scope:wipe nothing can keep it out of a go-wide deck, which is the whole reason that word exists.

kept.name: Mask of Law and Grace
kept.why: It is an Aura that attaches to a creature, and eff:attach beside grants:protection is what identifies a protection piece. It names black as well as red and only red was recorded.

kept.name: Catapult Fodder // Catapult Captain
kept.why: The front face's whole job is transforming itself, and the back face is a repeatable sacrifice outlet costing {2}{B}, {T} and another creature. None of the three was recorded, so a sacrifice deck cannot see the outlet at all.

kept.name: Fix What's Broken
kept.why: "As an additional cost to cast this spell, pay X life" is a cast cost, matching the cost:cast-* family, rather than a life payment on an activated ability.

kept.name: Exterminatus
kept.why: "Destroy all nonland permanents", after stripping indestructible from opponents' side, is the archetypal symmetric board wipe. Only scope:all was recorded, which does not tell the engine it destroys your own board.

kept.name: Evra, Halcyon Witness
kept.why: "Exchange your life total with Evra's power" both sets a power/toughness and sets a life total. The card currently carries no effect word at all, so its only ability is invisible.

kept.name: Fume Spitter
kept.why: A -1/-1 counter on a target creature makes it smaller and is how this card kills things. eff:add-counters alone reads as a counters payoff rather than removal.

kept.name: Faramir, Field Commander
kept.why: "At the beginning of your end step, if a creature died under your control this turn, draw a card" is a death payoff. Only the end step trigger was recorded, so nothing says this belongs in an aristocrats deck.

kept.name: Pentavus
kept.why: Both abilities have real costs nothing recorded: removing a +1/+1 counter from itself, and sacrificing a Pentavite, which makes this a genuine sacrifice outlet. Every counter it adds goes on itself, so the generic add-counters word is unsupported.

kept.name: The Wedding of River Song
kept.why: Only "draw two" was recorded. The card also exiles a nonland card from your hand and from an opponent's hand with time counters on it, grants suspend, and time travel explicitly adds or removes time counters. Four whole clauses were unread.
