kept.why: Its only ability turns it into a 3/6 Golem creature and no effect word was recorded at all - the list held nothing but printed facts.

kept.name: Panacea
kept.why: The card's one ability prevents X damage and taps to do it; the list carried no effect and no cost beyond the mana.

kept.name: Personal Incarnation
kept.why: "Its owner loses half their life" on death was entirely unrecorded. The redirect also sends the damage to its OWNER, which is damage pointed at you.

kept.name: Opal Acrolith
kept.why: Like Opal Gargoyle, the trigger watches opponents but the effect is only on itself, so "affects everything" is wrong.

kept.name: Jade Idol
kept.why: Becoming a 4/4 Spirit artifact creature is an animation and only eff:set-pt was recorded, which describes the size and not the transformation. The trigger is on spells YOU cast, and only the bare trig:cast was present.

kept.name: Swooping Talon
kept.why: Provoke is a trigger on attacking, and it UNTAPS the defending creature before forcing the block. Only eff:force-block was recorded, so both halves of the mechanic were missing.

kept.name: Ivory Gargoyle
kept.why: It brings ITSELF back to the battlefield after dying and that, the card's defining ability, was not recorded at all - only the {4}{W} exile outlet was. It also makes you skip your next draw step, which nothing recorded.

kept.name: Necra Sanctuary
kept.why: The upkeep trigger checks the COLOURS of permanents you control, and doubles on white plus green. Nothing recorded that it cares about colour.

kept.name: Kagemaro's Clutch
kept.why: -X/-X makes a creature SMALLER; recording it as eff:pump says the opposite of what the card does. It is also an Aura that attaches to a creature, which was unrecorded.

kept.name: Elkin Bottle
kept.why: The list held no effect word whatsoever for a card that exiles the top of your library to play it - which is precisely eff:impulse. Deliberately NOT adding eff:exile: this is card advantage, not removal, and eff:exile would file it as an answer.

kept.name: Quagmire Lamprey
kept.why: It puts a -1/-1 counter on the blocker. eff:shrink records the outcome but not that a counter is placed, which is how Greater Werewolf in the same batch is recorded.

kept.name: Greater Werewolf
kept.why: "At end of combat" is a step trigger and no trigger word was recorded, so the ability reads as though it happens on its own.

kept.name: Bold Defense
kept.why: When kicked it gives your whole team first strike, and only the +N/+N was recorded.

kept.name: Starlight
kept.why: The life gained is counted off BLACK creatures an opponent controls; nothing recorded that the card reads colour.

kept.name: Agent of Shauku
kept.why: "Target creature gets +2/+0" hits one creature. Nothing here affects everything; the sacrifice-a-land cost is what the scan misread.

kept.name: Celestus Sanctifier
kept.why: Two clauses were unread. It looks at the top two of your library and picks which one stays, and it does something as it enters (turns it day).

kept.name: Jeweled Torque
kept.why: Only the colour choice was recorded. The card triggers whenever any player casts a spell, offers an optional {2} payment, and gains 2 life if paid - none of it was written down.

kept.name: Tainted Specter
kept.why: {T} is part of the activation cost. The ability reads the target's hand and can put a card on top of their library, and the damage hits each creature and each player, which is genuinely board-wide.

kept.name: Cagemail
kept.why: "Enchanted creature gets +2/+2 and can't attack" - only the can't-attack half was read. It is also a real pump, which matters because it can be put on your own blocker.

kept.name: Golden Wish
kept.why: The card's whole point is putting a card into your hand, and no word said it moved anything anywhere. Only the self-exile was recorded.

kept.name: Graven Dominator
kept.why: It sets base power and toughness 1/1 on EACH other creature - a one-sided board neutering - and none of set-pt, scope:all or the enters trigger was recorded. Haunt also exiles it when it dies.

kept.name: Samite Pilgrim
kept.why: The ability's cost is {T} and no cost word was recorded.

kept.name: Phyrexian Slayer
kept.why: It triggers only when it BECOMES BLOCKED, never when it blocks - it has no ability that fires on blocking. Compare Infinite Authority, which genuinely says "blocks or becomes blocked" and correctly carries both.

kept.name: Count Nefaria
kept.why: "This spell costs {3} less to cast" was entirely unread; the card had no effect word at all.

kept.name: Daru Stinger
kept.why: The damage ability costs {T} and no cost word was recorded.

kept.name: Nightsky Mimic
kept.why: It triggers on spells YOU cast, not on anyone's. Only the undirected trig:cast was recorded, which reads like a stax-style opponent trigger rather than the spellslinger payoff it is.

kept.name: Mercenary Knight
kept.why: The card carried a trigger and no effect at all. It sacrifices itself unless you discard a creature card, so both the sacrifice and the self-discard are real and unread.

kept.name: Guardian Angel
kept.why: The second sentence - pay {1} repeatedly for more prevention - was unread. That optional payment is most of the card.

kept.name: Infinite Authority
kept.why: It DESTROYS the other creature and no destroy word was recorded, so the engine could not see it as removal. The counter arrives on a delayed end-step trigger, which was also unread.

kept.name: Rebel Informer
kept.why: The card had no effect word at all. Putting a Rebel on the bottom of its owner's library is real removal, and the static clause makes it untargetable by white spells, which is the same white-hate signal Bog Elemental carries.

kept.name: Aegis of the Meek
kept.why: Nothing about what the card does was recorded - it had only a cost tier and a colour word. It taps to give +1/+2.

kept.name: Dread Wight
kept.why: The whole ability is an at-end-of-combat trigger and no trigger word was recorded.

kept.name: Bog Elemental
kept.why: The upkeep trigger sacrifices the creature or a land and no sacrifice word was recorded, so the engine saw an upkeep trigger doing nothing.

kept.name: Ashnod's Battle Gear
kept.why: The card had no effect word at all. +2/-2 is both a power pump and a toughness reduction, and the ability costs {T}.

kept.name: Wand of the Elements
kept.why: Each ability makes a single token from a single sacrificed land. Nothing is board-wide; the "sacrifice an Island" selector is what the scan misread.

kept.name: Raving Oni-Slave
kept.why: The card carried no trigger and no effect. It fires both when it enters and when it leaves the battlefield, which is the whole card.

kept.name: Grim Reminder
kept.why: The first line is "Search your library for a nonland card" and none of that clause is recorded. The graveyard ability returns THIS card to hand, which is eff:recur-self, not merely a generic return.

kept.name: Oracle's Attendants
kept.why: The whole card is unread: the {T} cost is missing, and "all damage that would be dealt to target creature is dealt to this creature instead" is exactly eff:redirect-damage. It keeps your creature alive, so eff:protect applies too.

kept.name: Chronosavant
kept.why: "You skip your next turn" is a real drawback the list does not mention; eff:skip-phase is the only word for skipping part of the game.

kept.name: Greel's Caress
kept.why: -3/-0 makes the creature smaller. eff:pump says the opposite and would offer this Aura to a deck looking to grow creatures.

kept.name: Femeref Healer
kept.why: Neither the tap cost nor the damage prevention is recorded; the card currently reads as doing nothing at all.

kept.name: Mindwarper
kept.why: The discard ability costs a +1/+1 counter off itself, which is unrecorded.

kept.name: Scavenging Ghoul
kept.why: Regeneration is paid by removing a corpse counter; the counters go on but nothing records them being spent.

kept.name: Dripping Dead
kept.why: It destroys the creature it damages, which is the whole card and is absent. "This creature can't block" is the drawback and has its own word.

kept.name: Spiritual Sanctuary
kept.why: The trigger is recorded but not what it does. The only effect on the card is gaining life.

kept.name: Mangara's Equity
kept.why: The choice is between black AND red and only red is recorded; it also keys on a white creature you control. Choosing a colour on resolution is eff:choose, and the damage clause is a trigger on a creature dealing damage.

kept.name: Kor Aeronaut
kept.why: The flying grant happens only "if it was kicked", which is precisely a pay-more-get-more clause.

kept.name: Skitterskin
kept.why: "This creature can't block" is unrecorded. Not col:none: devoid removes colour, but its colour identity is still black from {3}{B}.

kept.name: Nine-Ringed Bo
kept.why: The second sentence exiles the creature instead of letting it die, and only the damage half is recorded.

kept.name: Recuperate
kept.why: It is a modal "choose one" and the second mode, preventing 6 damage, is entirely missing.

kept.name: Sparring Golem
kept.why: The trigger is recorded but not the effect: it gets +1/+1 for each creature blocking it.

kept.name: Sacred Boon
kept.why: The counters arrive on a delayed trigger at the beginning of the next end step, which nothing records.

kept.name: Kor Castigator
kept.why: Its only line is conditional evasion, and the list carries no effect word. The other conditional-evasion cards in this batch (Marsh Threader, Moor Fiend) carry eff:cant-be-blocked.

kept.name: Midvast Protector
kept.why: Granting protection from a chosen colour to your own creature is a save; the protection role should be able to see it.

kept.name: Chimeric Sphere
kept.why: Both abilities turn this artifact into a creature, and the first gives it flying. Nothing on the card is currently recorded.

kept.name: Pale Wayfarer
kept.why: Nothing about this ability is recorded. {Q} is the untap symbol and is part of the cost, and the effect grants protection from a chosen colour to a creature.

kept.name: Rakalite
kept.why: Its entire activated ability prevents damage and no facet said so.

kept.name: Combat Medic
kept.why: The card's only ability is a damage prevention shield; the list held nothing but printed facts.

kept.name: Armed Assailant
kept.why: It gives itself +2/+0 while equipped, which is a pump the list never recorded.

kept.name: Shinen of Stars' Light
kept.why: Channel discards this card from hand as part of the activation cost.

kept.name: Chill Haunting
kept.why: It targets one creature for -X/-X. Nothing about it is mass or symmetric, and scope:all would read it as a sweeper.

kept.name: Maggot Therapy
kept.why: It is an Aura, so it attaches; and +2/-2 is how it is actually cast, as a two-mana kill on a small creature. The toughness reduction was unrecorded.

kept.name: Chariot of the Sun
kept.why: The ability taps to activate, grants flying, and sets base toughness to 1. All three clauses produced nothing.

kept.name: Withering Hex
kept.why: The enchanted creature gets -1/-1 per counter and never gets bigger, so eff:pump is backwards. It is an Aura, and it puts plague counters on itself.

kept.name: Lowland Tracker
kept.why: Provoke untaps the blocker as well as forcing the block; only the forced block was recorded.

kept.name: Mangara's Blessing
kept.why: It returns this very card from your graveyard to your hand, which is exactly what eff:recur-self names.

kept.name: Floodwater Dam
kept.why: It taps to activate and taps X lands. The list carried only costs and colour.

kept.name: Derelor
kept.why: The tax applies specifically to black spells you cast, so the card is about black.

kept.name: Tresserhorn Skyknight
kept.why: The prevention clause keys on creatures with first strike.

kept.name: Soldevi Steam Beast
kept.why: The life goes to a target OPPONENT. Counting that as lifegain would put the card in a lifegain deck, where it is actively bad.

kept.name: Dwarven Lightsmith
kept.why: Its enter trigger pumps every creature your team controls; neither the pump nor its breadth was recorded.

kept.name: Daggerclaw Imp
kept.why: "This creature can't block" is a real restriction on itself and produced no facet.

kept.name: Martyr of Bones
kept.why: Revealing X black cards from hand is part of the activation cost.

kept.name: Thran Weaponry
kept.why: The activated ability taps and gives ALL creatures +2/+2. The entire ability was unread.

kept.name: Patriarch's Desire
kept.why: +2/-2, doubled at threshold, is toughness reduction used as removal. Only the pump half was recorded.

kept.name: Pilgrim of Virtue
kept.why: Both halves of the card name black: protection from black, and prevention from a black source.

kept.name: El-Hajjâj
kept.why: The trigger gains you life equal to the damage dealt and the list recorded only the trigger, not the effect.

kept.name: Servant of Volrath
kept.why: It sacrifices A creature, one, not the board. scope:all makes a single edict read as a mass effect.

kept.name: Foul Familiar
kept.why: The first line, "This creature can't block", produced nothing. That is exactly eff:cant-block-self. The activated bounce half was already read.

kept.name: Jasmine Seer
kept.why: The whole ability was unread - the list is nothing but printed type facts. {2}{W}, {T} is cost:tap; "You gain 2 life for each card revealed" is eff:gain-life; the cards revealed come from your hand (cares:zone:hand) and must be white (cares:color:w).

kept.name: Kami of Tattered Shoji
kept.why: It gains flying, which grants:flying already says - no power or toughness changes anywhere on the card, so eff:pump is false. scope:all is false too: the trigger affects only this creature, nothing else on the board.

kept.name: Balm of Restoration
kept.why: {T} is part of the activation cost and was not recorded. "Choose one -" with two bullets is a modal ability, which is eff:choose; both modes were already read.

kept.name: Life Burst
kept.why: "for each card named Life Burst in each graveyard" counts cards in graveyards and was not recorded at all.

kept.name: Soul Shepherd
kept.why: Nothing on this card affects everything - it exiles one creature card from your own graveyard and gains you one life. scope:all is a false breadth claim.

kept.name: Putrid Raptor
kept.why: "Morph-Discard a Zombie card" is an alternative cost paid by discarding, and the discard comes from your hand. Neither was recorded, so the card reads as having no cost mechanic at all.

kept.name: Miracle Worker
kept.why: The ability is "{T}: Destroy target Aura" and the tap cost was not recorded. Deliberately NOT adding eff:destroy-own: the Aura sits on your creature but is usually an opponent's Pacifism, which is the whole point of the card.

kept.name: Skyshroud Vampire
kept.why: The pump is on this creature alone and the discard is a single card from your own hand. Nothing here affects everything.

kept.name: Wojek Apothecary
kept.why: The Radiance ability is "{T}: Prevent..." and the tap cost was not recorded. Left scope:all off deliberately - radiance reaches only creatures sharing a colour with the target, not the whole board.

kept.name: Legion Conquistador
kept.why: Only eff:search-library survived. The trigger searches your library (cares:zone:library), puts the cards into your hand (cares:zone:hand), and then shuffles (eff:shuffle) - three of the four clauses were dropped.

kept.name: Shimian Night Stalker
kept.why: The list held nothing but printed type facts. "{B}, {T}" is cost:tap, and "All damage that would be dealt to you... is dealt to this creature instead" is precisely eff:redirect-damage - the card's entire function was unrecorded.

kept.name: Melancholy
kept.why: It is an Aura that enchants a creature, so eff:attach. Tapping the enchanted creature and stopping it untapping is a permanent lockdown, which is eff:neutralise - the card is removal and read as none. eff:tap-own is wrong: "enchant creature" is any creature and this is aimed at an opponent's, so it must not be recorded as tapping your own board.

kept.name: Aven Trooper
kept.why: cost:discard was recorded but the hand it is paid from was not, unlike Skyshroud Vampire in this same batch which carries both.

kept.name: Reborn Hero
kept.why: The granted ability returns THIS card to the battlefield from the graveyard, which is eff:recur-self; the generic eff:return-from does not say the card brings itself back. "you may pay {W}{W}. If you do..." is eff:do-if-cost-paid, and neither was recorded.

kept.name: Warden of the Beyond
kept.why: 'Gets +2/+2 as long as an opponent owns a card in exile' is a static self-pump and produced no effect word; the same shape on Nim Grotesque in this batch carries eff:pump.

kept.name: Barbed-Back Wurm
kept.why: The whole card is '-1/-1 until end of turn' on a blocking creature and it carried no effect word at all.

kept.name: Righteous Indignation
kept.why: The trigger's payload, '+1/+1 until end of turn', was missing entirely. The trigger reads 'a black or red creature' and only the red half was recorded.

kept.name: Ignoble Soldier
kept.why: 'Prevent all combat damage that would be dealt by it' is the card's only effect and it was unrecorded.

kept.name: Argivian Blacksmith
kept.why: Prevention is the entire ability and was missing, and the ability costs {T}.

kept.name: Mercenaries
kept.why: 'Prevent that damage' is the only effect on the card and nothing recorded it.

kept.name: Defender en-Vec
kept.why: The prevention ability is paid for by removing a fade counter, which was not recorded as a cost.

kept.name: Samite Alchemist
kept.why: Prevention was missing and the ability costs {T}. The tap is on 'target creature you control', so it is eff:tap-own; eff:tap reads as tapping an opponent's board down, which this never does.

kept.name: Sacred Knight
kept.why: Conditional evasion was unrecorded (Righteous Avengers' plainswalk in this batch carries eff:cant-be-blocked), and the text names black as well as red.

kept.name: Golgothian Sylex
kept.why: The ability's cost is '{1}, {T}' and the tap was not recorded.

kept.name: Scour
kept.why: It exiles matching cards out of the controller's graveyard, hand and library; only the hand zone and the plain exile were recorded. I did not add eff:search-library or eff:shuffle: both search and shuffle happen to the OPPONENT's library, and those words would make it read as a tutor for you.

kept.name: Lim-Dûl's Cohort
kept.why: The card destroys nothing. It only says the creature it blocks or is blocked by 'can't be regenerated', which is a restriction; recording it as destruction files a vanilla body as removal.

kept.name: Ravenous Vampire
kept.why: It eats another creature ('you may sacrifice a nonartifact creature') every upkeep, and that sacrifice of something other than itself was unrecorded.

kept.name: Elvish Healer
kept.why: Damage prevention is the whole card and it carried no effect word; the ability costs {T}.

kept.name: Famished Ghoul
kept.why: It targets cards in a graveyard; it has eff:exile-graveyard but no record that it looks at the graveyard zone.

kept.name: Bloodied Ghost
kept.why: The counter goes on this creature itself, as a drawback. The generic word says it puts counters on things, which reads as counters support; -self is the documented word for a counter a card puts on itself.

kept.name: Tawnos's Weaponry
kept.why: 'Target creature gets +1/+1' is the only effect and nothing recorded it; the ability costs {2}, {T}.

kept.name: Orim's Touch
kept.why: Kicker: 'If this spell was kicked, prevent the next 4 damage instead' is exactly the pay-more-get-more shape and was unrecorded.

kept.name: Noble Vestige
kept.why: Its only ability prevents damage and costs {T}; neither was recorded.

kept.name: Trap Digger
kept.why: The damage ability is paid for by sacrificing a land with a trap counter on it, a sacrifice of something other than itself, and that cost was unrecorded.

kept.name: North Star
kept.why: The ability costs {4}, {T} and the tap was not recorded. I propose no word for 'spend mana as though it were any type': it is close to conditional mana and I would rather not coin a near-synonym.

kept.name: Murk Dwellers
kept.why: The attack trigger's payload, '+2/+0 until end of combat', was missing, leaving a trigger with no effect.

kept.name: Moratorium Stone
kept.why: Both abilities exile out of graveyards and nothing recorded that it looks at that zone; the second ability's cost includes sacrificing itself.

kept.name: Conservator
kept.why: Preventing damage to you is the entire card and carried no effect word; the ability costs {3}, {T}.

kept.name: Surging Dementia
kept.why: Ripple reveals the top four cards of your library and casts matching spells without paying their mana costs; only the discard half was recorded.

kept.name: Daru Healer
kept.why: The whole activated ability was dropped. "{T}: Prevent the next 1 damage" is a tap cost and a damage-prevention effect; the list had neither, leaving a Fog-on-a-stick reading as a vanilla Cleric.

kept.name: Kjeldoran Elite Guard
kept.why: Only the pump half of the ability was read. "When that creature leaves the battlefield this turn, sacrifice this creature" is a leaves trigger and a sacrifice effect, and it is the drawback that defines the card.

kept.name: Treacherous Werewolf
kept.why: Threshold grants +2/+2 (eff:pump) and a death trigger costing you 4 life (eff:lose-life, the same word Serpent Warrior carries for "you lose 3 life"). trig:dies was recorded but neither thing the trigger does was.

kept.name: Cold Snap
kept.why: It triggers on EACH player's upkeep and damages that player, so the damage is symmetric and hits the whole table including you. eff:damage alone reads as a one-sided burn effect.

kept.name: Nightshade Seer
kept.why: Everything the ability does was lost. It taps as a cost, gives -X/-X (a shrink, not a pump), and X is the number of black cards revealed from your HAND, which is a genuine hand-matters payoff.

kept.name: Grave Robbers
kept.why: It exiles an artifact card from a graveyard. eff:exile-graveyard was recorded but the zone it operates on was not, so it does not read as a card that interacts with graveyards at all.

kept.name: Battalion Foot Soldier
kept.why: It searches your library, which the list records as eff:search-library without the zone word every other library-interacting card in this batch carries (Harsh Deceiver has it for merely looking at the top card).

kept.name: Pearl Shard
kept.why: Both halves of the activation cost tap the artifact ("{3}, {T} or {W}, {T}"). The list has only eff:prevent-damage and the type line.

kept.name: Prowling Nightstalker
kept.why: "Can't be blocked except by black creatures" is conditional evasion, the same reading Raiding Nightstalker's swampwalk gets. The card currently carries no effect word at all.

kept.name: Harsh Deceiver
kept.why: The second ability untaps it AND gives +1/+1 until end of turn. eff:untap was recorded, the pump was dropped.

kept.name: Staff of the Ages
kept.why: A global static touching every creature with landwalk on the battlefield. The card currently produces no behaviour word whatsoever - only col:none and its type line.

kept.name: Spirit Shield
kept.why: The entire activated ability is missing. "{2}, {T}: Target creature gets +0/+2" is a tap cost and a pump; the list held only acost:3, col:none and the type line.

kept.name: Torment
kept.why: Enchanted creature gets -3/-0. That makes a creature SMALLER, so eff:pump is wrong and would file a removal-style aura as a creature enhancement; eff:shrink is the correct word.

kept.name: Krovikan Rot
kept.why: Recover returns THIS card from your graveyard to your hand when a creature you control dies. eff:return-from was already read from that clause, so the reading is not being extended - it is being made specific: the card it returns is itself, and the event it watches is a creature dying.

kept.name: Quagmire
kept.why: A global static affecting every creature with swampwalk. The card presently carries ONLY type:enchantment - no cost, no effect, nothing the engine could ever match.

kept.name: Serra Inquisitors
kept.why: The block/becomes-blocked triggers were read but what they do - "this creature gets +2/+0 until end of turn" - was not.

kept.name: Gangrenous Goliath
kept.why: It returns ITSELF from the graveyard to your hand, which is exactly eff:recur-self and is the whole point of the card. scope:all is wrong: tapping three Clerics you control is a targeted cost on three permanents, not an effect on everything.

kept.name: Pearlspear Courier
kept.why: "{2}{W}, {T}: Target Soldier gets +2/+2 and has vigilance" - the grant was recorded but the tap cost and the +2/+2 were both dropped.

kept.name: Hell Swarm
kept.why: All creatures get -1/-0. That destroys nothing - it cannot kill even a 1/1, since toughness is untouched. scope:wipe marks a card as a board wipe, which would make the engine treat this as anti-synergy in every go-wide deck. scope:all and eff:shrink already describe it correctly.

kept.name: Mold Demon
kept.why: "Sacrifice it unless you sacrifice two Swamps" is the entire body of the enters trigger and no effect word was recorded for it.

kept.name: Paranoid Parish-Blade
kept.why: Delirium gives +1/+0 as well as first strike. The keyword grant was read and the stat boost was not.

kept.name: Pit Raptor
kept.why: The upkeep trigger sacrifices the creature unless you pay {2}{B}{B}. trig:step:upkeep was recorded with no effect attached to it.

kept.name: Opal Guardian
kept.why: It animates into a 3/4 Gargoyle WITH FLYING AND PROTECTION FROM RED and only eff:animate was recorded. The keywords the animated body carries are as real as the animation, and self-grants are already recorded with the general word elsewhere in this batch (Zodiac Pig gets eff:cant-be-blocked off its own swampwalk).

kept.name: Opal Champion
kept.why: Same shape as Opal Guardian: becomes a 3/3 Knight WITH FIRST STRIKE and the keyword half of the clause was dropped. Opal Caryatid, whose animated body has no keyword, is correctly complete, which is what shows the omission here is the keyword rather than the animation.

kept.name: Shield of the Ages
kept.why: Its entire text is a damage prevention ability and it carried NO effect word at all, only type, cost and colour. Sphere of Purity in this same batch carries eff:prevent-damage for the identical wording.

kept.name: Zelyon Sword
kept.why: The whole second line was unread. '{3}, {T}: Target creature gets +2/+0' is a tap cost and a pump and the card had neither, only acost:3, col:none and type:artifact.

kept.name: Kjeldoran Javelineer
kept.why: '{T}: This creature deals damage equal to the number of age counters on it' had eff:damage recorded and the tap in its own activation cost dropped. I left the cumulative-upkeep age counters unwritten deliberately: eff:add-counters-self reads as 'grows itself with counters' and would file a card whose counters are a liability as a counters card.

kept.name: Minion of Tevesh Szat
kept.why: '{T}: Target creature gets +3/-2' was recorded as a pump only. The minus two toughness is the half players actually use it for, as repeatable removal on a small creature, and eff:shrink is how the same negative modifier is recorded on Veldrane and Foul Presence.

kept.name: Tourach's Gate
kept.why: The last line, 'Tap enchanted land: Attacking creatures you control get +2/-1', produced nothing: no pump for the +2 and no cost for tapping a permanent other than itself. I did NOT add eff:shrink for the -1 even though I added it to Minion of Tevesh Szat, because this hits YOUR OWN attackers and shrink would advertise it as removal.

kept.name: Shade's Breath
kept.why: 'EACH creature you control becomes a black Shade' is a mass effect on your whole board and was recorded as though it hit one creature. Steeling Stance in this batch carries scope:all for the same 'creatures you control' selector.

kept.name: Veldrane of Sengir
kept.why: Forestwalk is evasion and the reminder text says so outright. Zodiac Pig, whose only ability is swampwalk, carries eff:cant-be-blocked in this same batch, so this is the convention being applied inconsistently rather than a new reading.

kept.name: Shinen of Fear's Chill
kept.why: Two of the three things it does were missing. 'This creature can't block' is eff:cant-block-self, distinct from the eff:cant-block it already had for the channel ability aimed at someone else's creature, and channel's 'Discard this card' is the activation cost.

kept.name: Skulking Knight
kept.why: Flanking gives the blocking creature -1/-1, so the shrink was missing. Its second line, the sacrifice on becoming a target, has no word at all, hence the proposal.

kept.name: Searchlight Geist
kept.why: '{3}{B}: This creature gains deathtouch until end of turn' changes no power and no toughness. eff:pump glosses as 'pumps creatures' and drives the enhance role, so a keyword-only grant carrying it makes a deathtouch trick read as a combat pump. grants:deathtouch already says what the card does.

kept.name: Whalebone Glider
kept.why: 'Target creature with power 3 or less gains flying' has no P/T change either, the same fault as Searchlight Geist. I also declined to add cares:power for the 'power 3 or less' filter: that word means a card that scales WITH power and maps toward pt:big, and this card wants small creatures, so it would point the engine the wrong way.

kept.name: Skulking Fugitive
kept.why: List holds only printed type words. The whole card is a triggered ability - it is targeted, then it sacrifices itself - and neither the trigger nor the effect was written down.

kept.name: Steamclaw
kept.why: Both abilities read 'exile target card from a graveyard'. eff:exile-graveyard is present but nothing records that the card looks at graveyards at all.

kept.name: Scavenging Scarab
kept.why: 'This creature can't block' is the card's entire rules text and produced no word. eff:cant-block-self is exactly this.

kept.name: Gravel Slinger
kept.why: The activated ability is '{T}: deals 1 damage'. The tap symbol in the cost was not recorded, though eff:damage and acost:1 were.

kept.name: Martyrs of Korlis
kept.why: 'all damage that would be dealt to you by artifacts is dealt to this creature instead' redirects the damage - the damage is still dealt, to a different recipient. Nothing is prevented, and the vocabulary carries a precise word for redirection.

kept.name: Forethought Amulet
kept.why: Two clauses both unread. 'Sacrifice this artifact unless you pay {3}' is a sacrifice effect, and 'it deals 2 damage to you instead' of 3 or more is damage reduction. The list held only the upkeep timing.

kept.name: Flowstone Armor
kept.why: Only acost:3, col:none and type:artifact were recorded, so the ability itself is entirely unread. '{3}, {T}' includes a tap cost, and '+1/-1' raises power and lowers toughness - the same -1 toughness that gave Nim Replica and Rank and File eff:shrink.

kept.name: Putrid Cyclops
kept.why: The scry half was read and the second sentence was not: 'This creature gets -X/-X until end of turn' shrinks a creature, which is the clause that actually matters for what the card does.

kept.name: Whipstitched Zombie
kept.why: 'Sacrifice this creature unless you pay {B}' produced only the upkeep trigger words. The sacrifice, which is the card's whole drawback, was not written down.

kept.name: Stonewise Fortifier
kept.why: The card's only ability is 'Prevent all damage that would be dealt to this creature by target creature this turn' and the list records nothing but its cost, so the card currently reads as doing nothing.

kept.name: Teroh's Vanguard
kept.why: Under threshold the card gains 'When this creature enters, creatures you control gain protection from black'. The granted effect was read (eff:protect, grants:protection) but the enters trigger that delivers it was not.

kept.name: Zealots en-Dal
kept.why: 'if all nonland permanents you control are white' is a genuine colour condition on the board, not incidental wording, and it is the only thing gating the lifegain.

kept.name: Hate Weaver
kept.why: The ability reads 'Target blue or red creature'. The card can only ever be pointed at those two colours, so both colour words belong.

kept.name: Ivory Guardians
kept.why: 'Creatures named Ivory Guardians get +1/+1 as long as an opponent controls a nontoken red permanent' is a pump the list never recorded - only the protection keyword and the red condition were read.

kept.name: Safeguard
kept.why: Its only ability prevents all combat damage a creature would deal, and no effect word was recorded at all.

kept.name: Stabilizer
kept.why: Cycling is an activated ability, so "players can't cycle cards" stops an ability being activated. The card carried the cycling reference but nothing saying it stops anything.

kept.name: Shadow Rider
kept.why: Flanking gives the blocking creature -1/-1. The two triggers were read and the effect they produce was not.

kept.name: Soldevi Simulacrum
kept.why: Cumulative upkeep triggers at the beginning of your upkeep. Only the activated pump was read.

kept.name: Reign of Terror
kept.why: "You lose 2 life for each creature that died this way" happens on resolution as part of the effect. It is not a cost of casting or activating anything, and cost:life would tell the engine this is a card you pay life to use.

kept.name: Rejuvenation Chamber
kept.why: Fading removes a fade counter at the beginning of your upkeep. Only the tap-for-life ability was read.

kept.name: Sunfire Balm
kept.why: The spell's main effect is preventing the next 4 damage, and the cycling trigger prevents 1 more. Only the cycling draw was recorded, so the card read as a cantrip that does nothing.

kept.name: Drekavac
kept.why: "Sacrifice it unless you discard a noncreature card" makes you discard. The trigger was read and its effect was not, leaving a card whose entire text is unrecorded.

kept.name: Krovikan Plague
kept.why: The ability's cost is tapping the enchanted creature, and it also puts a -0/-1 counter on it. The enters trigger draws at the beginning of the NEXT turn's upkeep, which is a delayed upkeep trigger. Deliberately not adding eff:shrink: the counter goes on your own enchanted creature, and eff:shrink would file this as removal.

kept.name: Telim'Tor's Darts
kept.why: The activation cost is {2}, {T}. The tap was not recorded.

kept.name: Celestial Sword
kept.why: The pumped creature is sacrificed at the beginning of the next end step. Half the ability, and the half that matters most, was unread.

kept.name: Feast of Flesh
kept.why: It deals X damage to a target creature. Only the lifegain half of "deals X damage and you gain X life" was recorded.

kept.name: Serra Bestiary
kept.why: The enchanted creature can't attack, can't block, and can't use tap abilities. Only the last of the three was read, so a Pacifism variant looked like a narrow ability-shutoff rather than the removal-style effect it is.

kept.name: Villainous Ogre
kept.why: "This creature can't block" was not recorded at all, and the granted "{B}: Regenerate this creature" keeps it alive, which is what eff:protect says (the same reading Defiling Tears already gets for granting regenerate).

kept.name: Phyrexian Prowler
kept.why: Fading removes a fade counter at the beginning of your upkeep. Only the activated pump was read.

kept.name: Woeleecher
kept.why: Both halves of its only ability were missing: it removes a -1/-1 counter and gains you 2 life. The card carried the tap cost and nothing that happens.

kept.name: Unyielding Krumar
kept.why: The ability grants first strike and changes no power or toughness. grants:first strike already says what it does; eff:pump claims a stat buff the card does not give.

kept.name: Rotting Giant
kept.why: The alternative to sacrificing is exiling a card from your graveyard, so it both cares about the graveyard and has an exile cost. Neither was recorded. Not adding eff:exile-graveyard: it eats your own graveyard, and that word means graveyard hate aimed at opponents.

kept.name: Defiling Tears
kept.why: +1/-1 is both a pump and a shrink. Only the shrink half was recorded.

kept.name: Wayfaring Giant
kept.why: "gets +1/+1 for each basic land type among lands you control" is a power and toughness boost and produced no effect word at all - the whole card was unread apart from its type line.

kept.name: Descendant of Kiyomaro
kept.why: The conditional bonus "gets +1/+2" was dropped; only the granted lifegain trigger was read.

kept.name: Blind Creeper
kept.why: The only effect is -1/-1 on itself. scope:all came from the breadth of the trigger ("whenever a player casts a spell"), not from the effect, which touches nothing but this creature.

kept.name: Serra Paladin
kept.why: The first ability, "{T}: Prevent the next 1 damage that would be dealt to any target", produced nothing; only the vigilance ability was read.

kept.name: Militant Monk
kept.why: Its one activated ability prevents damage and costs {T}, and neither was recorded - the card read as a vanilla vigilance creature.

kept.name: Moonlight Geist
kept.why: "{3}{W}: Prevent all combat damage that would be dealt to and dealt by this creature" produced no effect word.

kept.name: Cloistered Youth // Unholy Fiend
kept.why: Only the front face's upkeep trigger was read. It actually transforms (eff:transform), and the back face has a beginning-of-end-step trigger (trig:step:end) that makes you lose life (eff:lose-life). kw:transform is the printed keyword and says nothing about the card doing it.

kept.name: Sorcerer of the Fang
kept.why: The activated ability includes {T} in its cost and that was not recorded.

kept.name: Goblin Dirigible
kept.why: "you may pay {4}. If you do, untap this creature" is an optional-payment upkeep trigger - the same shape as Skyline Scout, which does carry the word.

kept.name: Royal Herbalist
kept.why: Exiling the top card of your library is part of the activation cost and was not recorded.

kept.name: Matopi Golem
kept.why: "put a -1/-1 counter on it" is printed rules text, not reminder text, and the card genuinely puts a counter on itself when it regenerates. Nothing recorded any counter effect.

kept.name: Phobian Phantasm
kept.why: Cumulative upkeep triggers at the beginning of your upkeep. trig:step was recorded without the specific step, so the card reads as having some unspecified phase trigger.

kept.name: Kjeldoran Guard
kept.why: "When that creature leaves the battlefield this turn, sacrifice this creature" is a leaves-the-battlefield trigger and produced nothing; only the pump half of the ability was read.

kept.name: Unerring Sling
kept.why: Three gaps in one ability: {T} is in the cost (cost:tap sits alongside the already-present cost:tap-others), the damage is "equal to the tapped creature's power" (cares:power), and it can only target a creature with flying (cares:kw:flying), which is what makes it a flyer answer rather than general removal.

kept.name: Kry Shield
kept.why: The card had no effect words at all. Its single ability costs {T}, prevents all damage a creature would deal, and gives it +0/+X.

kept.name: Seasoned Tactician
kept.why: Exiling the top four cards of your library is the activation cost and was not recorded.

kept.name: Shrieking Grotesque
kept.why: The enters trigger only happens "if {B} was spent to cast it", which is exactly what cares:mana-spent records and which nothing captured.

kept.name: Slumbering Tora
kept.why: It turns itself into a creature, which is eff:animate and was missing entirely (only eff:set-pt was there, which says the size but not that it becomes a creature). Discarding a card is the activation cost.

kept.name: Loyal Gyrfalcon
kept.why: The trigger is specifically "whenever you cast a white spell", so it cares about the colour white and that was unrecorded. scope:all is wrong: losing defender affects only this creature, and the word came from the trigger's breadth rather than from any effect.

kept.name: Sand Golem
kept.why: Its whole point is returning itself from the graveyard to the battlefield when an opponent makes you discard it. Only the +1/+1 counter was recorded, so the recursion - the reason anyone plays it - was invisible.

kept.name: Trustworthy Scout
kept.why: Searches your library; the library zone is what the ability operates on and only eff:search-library was recorded.

kept.name: Possessed Nomad
kept.why: Threshold gives it +1/+1, which is a pump nothing recorded, and the granted ability costs {2}{B} and a tap. cares:color:w is a word scan on 'destroy target WHITE creature' - this is a white HOSER, and telling the engine it is a white-matters card is exactly backwards.

kept.name: Custodi Peacekeeper
kept.why: The activated ability costs {W} and a tap; only acost:2 was recorded. Deliberately NOT adding cares:power - the card restricts by power, it does not scale with it, and cares:power means the latter.

kept.name: Spirit Weaver
kept.why: It buffs green or blue creatures, which is a positive colour-matters statement rather than a hoser, so the blue half is real. The green half cannot be said at all.

kept.name: Noble Banneret
kept.why: 'This creature and those creatures get +1/+1' - the lifelink half was recorded and the pump half was not.

kept.name: Hall of Mirrors
kept.why: It creates NO tokens - existing creatures you control become copies. It affects each other creature you control, which is the mass effect scope:all describes.

kept.name: Concession Stand
kept.why: The Food token it creates reads '{2}, {T}, Sacrifice this artifact: You gain 3 life' on the card itself, so making a Food is making life.

kept.name: Haunted House
kept.why: 'It gains haste' was not recorded. Deliberately NOT adding eff:exile for the end-step clause: that exiles the creature you just reanimated, so filing it as removal would be wrong, and it is not a flicker either since nothing returns.

kept.name: Pick-a-Beeble
kept.why: It creates a Treasure token on visit and two more on the prize, and nothing recorded that it makes tokens at all. It also puts luck counters on itself, which is the -self convention.

kept.name: Balloon Stand
kept.why: The first mode creates a 1/1 red Balloon token and no token word was recorded. It is also a 'Choose one' modal.

kept.name: Swinging Ship
kept.why: 'At the beginning of that combat' is a begin-combat trigger, and it untaps ALL creatures that attacked. There is no 'whenever this attacks' trigger anywhere on the card, so trig:attacks is a word scan on 'attacked'; eff:extra-combat already places it correctly.

kept.name: Tunnel of Love
kept.why: One of the two chosen creatures is YOURS and they are exiled and returned at the next end step, which is a blink. The other branch is a fight, and a fight is each creature dealing damage equal to its power.

kept.name: Storybook Ride
kept.why: 'Exile the top X cards of your library... You may play those cards this turn' is precisely impulse draw, and the card carried no effect word for it.

kept.name: Merry-Go-Round
kept.why: It literally grants horsemanship, which was not recorded, and it affects your whole board. eff:cant-be-blocked is the consequence and was kept. Deliberately NOT adding cares:power - a 'power 2 or less' restriction is not scaling with power.

kept.name: Valorous Charge
kept.why: It pumps WHITE creatures only, so it is a white-matters card. The colour restriction was not recorded anywhere.

kept.name: Treacherous Vampire
kept.why: Only the attack/block trigger was read. That trigger sacrifices it unless you exile a card from your graveyard, and threshold both gives it +2/+2 and grants it a death trigger that costs you 6 life. Five separate things unwritten.

kept.name: Selfless Exorcist
kept.why: It exiles a creature card from a graveyard, which is graveyard hate and the only reason to play it. Neither the exile nor the zone was written down.

kept.name: Vindictive Mob
kept.why: Nothing here affects everything. It sacrifices one creature when it enters and cannot be blocked by Saprolings; the class noun looks like a mass selector and is not one.

kept.name: Lesser Werewolf
kept.why: The list held only the activation cost. The ability checks its own power, shrinks itself, and puts a -0/-1 counter on a creature blocking or blocked by it.

kept.name: Revered Elder
kept.why: Its entire ability prevents damage and the list recorded none of it.

kept.name: Tombfire
kept.why: It exiles ALL flashback cards from a player's graveyard. The mass selector and the graveyard zone were both missing, though the flashback reference was caught.

kept.name: Young Wei Recruits
kept.why: 'This creature can't block' produced nothing at all, while Belbe's Percher carries this word for a weaker version of the same restriction.

kept.name: Mind Burst
kept.why: X is one plus the number of copies in ALL graveyards, so it genuinely reads graveyards.

kept.name: Daru Cavalier
kept.why: It searches your library on entry; the search was recorded but not the zone.

kept.name: Smuggler Captain
kept.why: Same as Daru Cavalier: eff:search-library without the library zone.

kept.name: Surging Sentinels
kept.why: Ripple reveals the top four cards of your library and casts matching spells without paying their mana costs. Only a bare trig:cast was recorded, so the free casts and the library look were both lost.

kept.name: Craven Knight
kept.why: 'This creature can't block' was not written down at all.

kept.name: Cursed Monstrosity
kept.why: Being targeted sacrifices it unless you discard a land. The discard cost was caught and the sacrifice was not.

kept.name: Battlefield Percher
kept.why: It can block only creatures with flying, the identical clause Belbe's Percher carries this word for.

kept.name: Tar Pit Warrior
kept.why: The card's whole text is a trigger that sacrifices it, and the facet list held nothing but the subtypes.

kept.name: Tethered Skirge
kept.why: Being targeted costs you 1 life; the list held only flying. Nim Abomination carries eff:lose-life for the same 'you lose N life' shape, so this is the established convention.

kept.name: Marsh Lurker
kept.why: The ability gives fear to itself and nothing else. The mass scope is almost certainly read out of the reminder text's 'artifact creatures and/or black creatures'.

kept.name: Jeweled Spirit
kept.why: It gains protection itself and affects no other permanent. 'from the color of your choice' is a choice, not a mass selector.

proposals.means: YOU lose life, as a drawback or a cost of the card's own effect, rather than an opponent being drained.
cards: Ob Nixilis of the Black Oath
proposals.why: eff:lose-life is glossed as 'drains life' and is what a Vito or Marchesa drain payoff wants; using it for self-inflicted loss files Reanimate, Phyrexian Arena, The One Ring, Necropotence and Ancient Tomb's black cousins as drain cards. The vocabulary already draws exactly this distinction for the damage version with eff:damage-self (144 cards, on Ancient Tomb and City of Brass in this very batch), and for exile, discard, tap, destroy and bounce with -self/-own. Life loss is the one drawback verb with no direction, so a self-loss card is either silently misfiled as a drain or, as here, left unread altogether. Three cards in this batch of fifty want it.

proposals.means: Triggers when a player discards a card.
proposals.why: The vocabulary has trig:draws-card for the mirror event and nothing at all for discarding. Necropotence's second line ("Whenever you discard a card, exile that card from your graveyard") cannot be expressed, and neither can Bone Miser, Waste Not or Containment Construct. eff:discard / cost:discard describe causing or paying a discard, never reacting to one.

proposals.means: The card cares about green cards or green spells specifically, the way cares:color:b/w/u/r/c already work.
proposals.why: Green is the only colour missing from cares:color:*. Emerald Medallion's whole text is "Green spells you cast cost {1} less" and there is no way to record which colour it discounts, so it reads identically to a colourless cost reducer. Same gap on the rest of the Medallion and Monument cycles.

proposals.means: Gives creatures ward N, a tax an opponent must pay to target them.
proposals.why: Nothing in the vocabulary can say a card grants ward. grants:hexproof and grants:shroud are prohibitions, and grants:protection is a different, stronger shield; ward is a tax that still allows targeting if paid, so mapping it onto any of those would overstate the protection. Ward appears on a large and growing number of modern cards.

proposals.means: triggers when a permanent you control is turned face up
proposals.why: Roshan's only card-advantage engine fires on turning permanents face up, and there is no word for it. trig:enters and trig:cast are both wrong - a morph or disguise creature is already on the battlefield when this triggers. Without it a morph/disguise deck cannot find its payoffs.

proposals.means: forces creatures you control (or a named group) to attack each combat if able
proposals.why: eff:goad is about forcing an OPPONENT'S creatures to attack somebody else, eff:cant-attack is the opposite prohibition, and eff:force-block is about blocking. Nothing expresses a self-imposed "attacks each combat if able", which is the first line of this card and of Hellraiser Goblin, Bloodthirsty Blade's target and the whole Juggernaut shell.

proposals.means: The Ring tempts you: you get or advance the Ring emblem and choose a Ring-bearer.
cards: One Ring to Rule Them All
proposals.why: A real printed mechanic with about forty cards and its own deck-building payoffs, and the vocabulary has no word for it at all. Not a synonym for anything: it is neither a counter, a token, nor a grant, and the emblem's abilities change as it advances.

proposals.means: A permanent doesn't untap during its controller's next untap step.
proposals.why: eff:tap is false here — the Monument never taps anything, it keeps something already tapped down. The Monument cycle, Frost Titan, Dungeon Geists and Sleep are the same effect, and with no word for it the whole trigger half of this card is silent.

proposals.means: Removes permanents from the game temporarily. They cannot be targeted, damaged, destroyed or sacrificed while phased out, and return under their owner's control with counters, attachments and tapped state intact.
proposals.why: eff:exile-own is a blink: the permanent leaves and comes back as a new object, re-triggering enters abilities and losing counters. Phasing does the opposite - nothing re-enters, so it dodges a wipe without resetting the board. grants:phasing (3 cards) is the printed keyword on a permanent, not a card doing this to your board. Teferi's Protection, Out of Time, Slip Out the Back and Teferi's Realm all do it and the vocabulary cannot say so.

proposals.means: Makes a permanent become a card type in addition to its other types, without turning it into a creature.
proposals.why: eff:animate is creature-specific by its gloss, so turning a land or an enchantment into an artifact has no word at all. This is the whole point of Liquimetal Torque, Liquimetal Coating and March of the Machines-style effects, and it is a real deck-building interaction (make it an artifact, then use artifact removal or an artifact payoff on it).

proposals.means: the card stops you losing the game or stops opponents winning it, rather than causing a win or loss
proposals.why: eff:win-game and eff:lose-game both describe CAUSING a result. Platinum Angel does the opposite and currently carries no effect word at all, so its entire text is invisible. Angel's Grace, Phyrexian Unlife, Gideon of the Trials and Lich's Mirror are the same shape.

proposals.means: Permanents do not untap during their controller's untap step, or untap fewer of them.
proposals.why: Meekstone carries no verb at all — the engine knows it looks at creatures and not what it does to them. eff:tap is a one-shot tap-down and is a different card; there is no word for the standing untap lock. Covers Meekstone, Winter Moon, Kismet-shaped effects and Stasis.

proposals.means: You take the initiative (the Undercity dungeon and its ongoing turn-order contest).
proposals.why: eff:set-monarch already exists for the parallel mechanic, and the initiative behaves the same way in a deck: it is a repeating card-advantage engine you must defend. Right now this card's enters trigger records nothing at all, so half of what it does is invisible.

proposals.means: changes the colour of cards, spells or permanents rather than caring about a colour
proposals.why: The vocabulary has cares:color:w/u/b/r/g/c for a card that CHECKS a colour, and nothing for a card that CHANGES one. Painter's Servant, Prismatic Lace, Celestial Dawn and Mycosynth Lattice's colour clause all do this, and it is the entire reason Painter's Servant is played (Grindstone, colour hosers, protection-from-colour). Today the card compiles to eff:choose alone, which says only that a choice was made.

proposals.means: Removes a creature from combat, so it is no longer attacking or blocking and deals and receives no combat damage.
proposals.why: eff:protect is only an approximation and eff:untap misses the point entirely. Removing from combat is a distinct action with its own consequences: the attacker survives and stays untapped, and a blocked creature's blocker deals no damage. Maze of Ith and Reconnaissance are the well-known members and neither can currently be described.

proposals.means: Stops one or more players gaining life.
proposals.why: 'Your opponents can't gain life' is a whole ability with no representable word. eff:lose-life is the opposite effect and eff:prevent-damage is about damage, so this static hate clause currently reads as though the card does nothing but draw. It recurs on a real cluster of cards such as Archfiend of Despair, Rain of Gore and Sulfuric Vortex.

proposals.means: Forces creatures to attack a particular permanent or player, rather than attacking freely.
cards: Kytheon, Hero of Akros // Gideon, Battle-Forged
proposals.why: The +2 ("creatures that player controls attack Gideon Jura if able") is the whole reason Gideon planeswalkers are played as defensive cards and no word covers it. eff:force-block exists for the blocking half of the same idea, and eff:goad is the opposite claim (attack ANYWHERE ELSE, never me).

proposals.means: A permanent does not untap during its controller's untap step, so a tap effect on it is permanent rather than for one turn.
proposals.why: eff:tap says a permanent becomes tapped and says nothing about it staying tapped, which is the whole point of Dance of the Dead's drawback and of Sleep-style lockdown. Nothing in the vocabulary distinguishes tapping a blocker for a turn from turning a creature off for good.

proposals.means: The card creates a token for a player other than you, as compensation for what it just did to them.
proposals.why: eff:create-token means the card makes tokens FOR YOU, and adding it here would file a removal spell as a token card and put it in Krenko's deck. eff:give-control is about handing over an existing permanent, not minting a new one. The cluster is real and well played - Stroke of Midnight, Generous Gift, Beast Within - and it is a genuine downside the ranker cannot currently see.

proposals.means: The card checks poison counters on a player rather than giving them.
proposals.why: 'Activate only if an opponent has three or more poison counters' is a poison payoff, and eff:poison means the opposite — giving poison. Nothing expresses caring about a poison total, so every Corrupted card and every toxic payoff is invisible to a poison deck.

proposals.means: triggers when one or more counters are put on this creature
proposals.why: 'Whenever one or more +1/+1 counters are put on this creature, draw a card' is the card's entire ability and there is no trigger word for it, so the draw floats with nothing causing it. ctr:+1/+1 says the card involves that counter kind, not that receiving one is an event, and this is the payoff half of every counters deck (Duelist, Sanguine Evangelist, Toski-style draw).

proposals.means: You control another player during a turn, choosing their plays for them.
proposals.why: eff:gain-control is for stealing a permanent. Taking a player's whole turn is a different effect and is not covered by anything in the list. Around a dozen cards do it, Mindslaver and Emrakul among them, and their most powerful ability currently produces no word.

proposals.means: Triggers when a permanent becomes the target of a spell or ability.
proposals.why: trig:cast:targeting is the caster's side - it fires when YOU cast a spell that targets. Shay fires when a creature an OPPONENT controls is targeted, by a spell or an ability, which is a different event and not expressible today.

proposals.means: puts a permanent or card into its owner's library, usually shuffled in
proposals.why: eff:move-zone is the closest word and is generic enough to mean anything; eff:exile and eff:destroy are both false here, and eff:bounce-own is about your own permanents. Tucking is a distinct removal answer (Condemn, Chaos Warp, Time Ebb, this land) that gets around indestructible and regeneration, and no existing word confers the removal role for it.

proposals.means: Removes your maximum hand size.
proposals.why: cares:zone:hand only says the card looks at hands. There is no word for lifting the discard-to-seven rule, which is the entire reason Reliquary Tower, Thought Vessel, Venser's Journal and this card go into draw-heavy decks.

proposals.means: checks how much life you have, rather than the act of gaining it
proposals.why: cares:lifegain covers 'whenever you gain life' triggers only. Serra Ascendant, Test of Endurance, Angel of Vitality and Righteous Valkyrie check a life THRESHOLD, which is a different condition and is currently unsayable, so a top-tier lifegain payoff reaches lifegain decks only through kw:lifelink.

proposals.means: You may look at and play or cast cards from the top of your library.
proposals.why: eff:impulse requires exiling the cards first, which this does not do, and eff:look-and-pick is a one-shot dig rather than a standing permission. Gwenom's attack trigger currently produces no effect word at all. Covers Future Sight, Bolas's Citadel, Vizier of the Menagerie and Etali-style top-of-library engines.

proposals.means: stops players drawing beyond a limit, or at all
proposals.why: eff:cant-cast and eff:cant-activate cover spells and abilities; trig:draws-card is a trigger, not a restriction. Spirit of the Labyrinth and Narset, Parter of Veils currently carry no effect word.

proposals.means: the card counts or is paid for creatures that are modified, that is creatures with a counter on them, or equipped, or enchanted by an Aura you control
proposals.why: Modified is a printed, rules-defined term (Kamigawa: Neon Dynasty) and nothing in the vocabulary reaches it. It is not eff:add-counters, not cares:sub:aura and not cares:type:artifact: it is the union of all three, and cards like Towashi Guide-Bot, Kappa Tech-Wrecker and Michiko's Reign of Truth are only good in a deck that supplies that union. Without the word these cards can be placed in no archetype at all.

proposals.means: venture into the dungeon, or take the initiative
proposals.why: Its attack trigger produces no facet at all today. Nothing in the vocabulary describes entering or advancing a dungeon, and it is not a token, a counter or a keyword grant, so no existing word can stand in for it.

proposals.means: the card cares whether OTHER permanents already have counters on them, rather than putting counters on things itself
proposals.why: eff:add-counters, eff:remove-counters and cost:remove-counters all describe moving counters. Nothing says "looks for a permanent that has a counter". Yathan Tombguard triggers on a creature with a counter on it dealing damage, and Leader's Talent level 2 checks "if it had a counter on it". Both are +1/+1 counter payoffs invisible to the vocabulary.

proposals.means: permanents arrive on the battlefield tapped
proposals.why: eff:tap is an action pointed at something already in play (tap down a blocker, tap a creature to lock it). A static replacement that makes every permanent arrive tapped is a symmetric slowdown, and reading it as tapping things down offers this to decks looking for a tapper. Nothing else in the vocabulary covers entering tapped.

proposals.means: triggers whenever you (or a player) discard a card
proposals.why: The vocabulary has trig:draws-card for the mirror event and nothing for discarding. Monument to Endurance, Bone Miser, Archfiend of Ifnir and Containment Construct all key off discarding and the trigger is currently invisible; cares:zone:hand only says the card looks at hands.

proposals.means: triggers when one or more cards leave your graveyard
proposals.why: trig:leaves is the battlefield-leave trigger the blink plan rules read, so putting it on a graveyard payoff would file this card as a blink enabler. There is no word for a graveyard-departure trigger, and this card currently carries no trigger word at all. Underworld-recursion payoffs share the shape.

proposals.means: gives the spells you cast convoke
cards: Eirdu, Carrier of Dawn // Isilu, Carrier of Twilight
proposals.why: Convoke changes how a spell is PAID FOR, not what it costs, so eff:reduce-cost would be a false claim; and there is no grants: entry for convoke although the grants: family covers keywords systematically. The front half's entire text is currently unread.

proposals.means: Triggers whenever you commit a crime (target an opponent, anything they control, or cards in their graveyard).
proposals.why: Nothing in the trig: vocabulary can express it, so this card's only trigger is currently silent - the tokens appear to come from nowhere. Crime is a named mechanic with its own payoffs and its own deckbuilding demand (cheap ways to target opponents), which is exactly what a trigger word is for.

proposals.means: Stops abilities from triggering, usually enters-the-battlefield triggers.
proposals.why: eff:cant-activate covers activated abilities and eff:cant-cast covers spells; neither covers triggers. Torpor Orb currently carries no effect word at all — the engine knows it affects everything and not what it does. It names a small but sharply defined stax family (Torpor Orb, Hushwing Gryff, Hushbringer, Tocatli Honor Guard) that a blink or ETB deck must be able to identify as hostile.

proposals.means: the card singles out creatures that have defender
proposals.why: cares:kw: exists for flying, reach, deathtouch, lifelink, haste and a dozen more, but not defender, so the walls archetype cannot be expressed. Perimeter Captain, Arcades the Strategist, Doran, High Alert, Assault Formation and Wall of Kelp payoffs all lose their defining clause.

proposals.means: A player cannot lose the game, or cannot win it - the game-ending rules are altered rather than a win or loss being caused.
proposals.why: eff:win-game and eff:lose-game both mean CAUSING a win or a loss. Nothing says a win or loss is PREVENTED, which is the entire text of Abyssal Persecutor, Platinum Angel, Angel's Grace and Gideon of the Trials. Persecutor currently carries no eff: word at all.

proposals.means: The card gives an OPPONENT life, either as a drawback (cumulative upkeep here) or deliberately, as group hug does.
proposals.why: eff:gain-life reads as a lifegain payoff, so tagging this card with it would put a drawback wall into lifegain decks. The vocabulary already splits by who for damage (eff:damage-self), discard (eff:discard-self) and draw (eff:draw-each); life has no such split, so an opponent gaining life cannot be said at all.

proposals.means: This creature can block more than one attacker at a time.
proposals.why: The card's only ability, and it has no effect word at all as a result. Nothing existing covers it: eff:force-block is about compelling a creature to block, grants:defender is about being unable to attack, and eff:cant-be-blocked is the attacker's side. About fifteen cards say it (Palace Guard, Hundred-Handed One, Guardian of the Gateless, Rekindled Flame-era walls), and it is the defining card of a defensive board.

proposals.means: checks or is paid for life you have lost
proposals.why: "If you lost life last turn" is the condition that makes the whole card work and there is no way to say it. cares:lifegain exists for the mirror case; trig:loses-life is a trigger on the event and this is an intervening-if check on a different trigger, so neither fits. Without it this reads as a plain upkeep counter with no condition, which is a much better card than it is.

proposals.means: Changes what basic land types a land has
proposals.why: eff:animate covers turning a permanent into a creature and nothing covers changing a land's type. It is a distinct and real effect - it is fixing on Navigator's Compass and Unstable Frontier, and denial on Blood Moon - and today those cards carry no verb for their main ability at all.

proposals.means: This creature can block more than one attacker each combat.
proposals.why: Nothing existing covers it. eff:cant-block and eff:cant-attack are restrictions on others, eff:force-block makes a creature block THIS one. A defensive multi-blocker is a distinct, recurring printed shape (Kraken Hatchling-style walls, Guardian of the Gateless) that a defensive or go-tall deck genuinely wants, and today those cards carry no word for their only ability.

proposals.means: This permanent gains the activated abilities of other permanents you control.
proposals.why: Marvin's whole card is this and it currently carries no effect word at all. eff:copy is about copying spells or making token copies of permanents, not about acquiring another permanent's activated abilities while both remain on the battlefield. Also covers Mirrorworks-style ability sharing and Arcane Adaptation-adjacent grants.

proposals.means: Changes what land types lands have, and so what colours they tap for - either adding a type to every land or replacing their types outright.
proposals.why: Nothing existing reaches it. eff:add-mana is wrong because the card produces no mana itself; eff:animate is specifically turning a permanent into a creature; eff:neutralise is turning a permanent harmless. Yet this is a real and load-bearing effect in two opposite directions: Urborg and Yavimaya in this batch are five-colour fixing that a mana base should reach for, and the same wording on Blood Moon, Magus of the Moon and Back to Basics is a stax piece that attacks a greedy mana base. Both are currently invisible - Urborg's list says only that it mentions lands and affects all of them, which is equally true of Armageddon.

proposals.means: You may cast or play cards from the top of your library.
proposals.why: Nothing covers it. eff:impulse requires exiling the cards first and this does not exile them; eff:cast-from-graveyard and eff:play-from-graveyard are the wrong zone; eff:cast-free is about not paying a cost, and here you pay normally. Mystic Forge's main ability currently produces no word at all, so the card reads as a do-nothing artifact that exiles your own top card. Bolas's Citadel, Future Sight, Vizier of the Menagerie and the Etali/Kykar style "play the top card" permanents are the same shape.

proposals.means: Exiles cards from your OWN library, as a cost or a side effect, rather than exiling a permanent or a graveyard.
proposals.why: eff:exile would misfile this as removal; eff:impulse is wrong because the cards go to hand and are never played from exile. Same split that already justifies eff:exile-graveyard and eff:exile-self. Tainted Pact and Demonic Consultation are the archetypal pair and both currently record nothing about it.

proposals.means: Triggers when a player commits a crime - targets an opponent, something an opponent controls, or a card in an opponent's graveyard.
proposals.why: Crime is a printed mechanic on dozens of Outlaws of Thunder Junction cards and there is no trigger word for it, so every crime payoff is left with its effects listed and no trigger. It is not any existing trigger: it fires on targeting, which no trig: word covers, and trig:cast:targeting is about a spell being cast rather than any targeting at all.

proposals.means: Stops counters being placed on permanents or players at all.
proposals.why: The card's entire text is this and it carries only scope:all, so the engine knows nothing about what it does. eff:remove-counters takes counters off after the fact and cost:remove-counters is a cost; neither says counters can never arrive. This is a real archetype piece (Solemnity plus Phyrexian Unlife) and a hard anti-synergy against every counters deck, which nothing can currently express.

proposals.means: the card gives a protective keyword to ITSELF rather than to your other creatures
proposals.why: Etched Champion has protection from each color; it protects nothing else. Carrying plain grants:protection makes it read as a card that keeps your creatures alive, the Swiftfoot Boots job, which it cannot do. Same shape as the existing cost:sacrifice-self and eff:exile-self splits, and it also covers Paradise Druid, Shimmer Dragon and Syr Ginger.

proposals.means: The card makes ONLY ITSELF cheaper — "this spell costs {1} less to cast if..." — as opposed to eff:reduce-cost, which makes other spells cheaper.
proposals.why: eff:reduce-cost means "makes spells cost less", which is a deck-level engine (Urza's Filter, Goblin Warchief) and reads as something the deck is built around. A discount on one card is a stat about that card and tells a deck nothing. Tagging this card eff:reduce-cost would say a Villain deck wants expensive spells; leaving it bare says the second line of the card does not exist. Same -self precedent as cost:sacrifice-self and eff:exile-self. Ghalta, Primal Hunger and Kicker/affinity-style self-discounts are the same population.

proposals.means: This permanent does not untap during its controller's untap step, so it stays tapped until something else untaps it.
proposals.why: Nothing in the vocabulary can say this. eff:untap and eff:tap-own describe actions the card takes; cost:untap is a cost paid. There is no word for the standing drawback, and it is a real deck-building signal in both directions: the drawback wants untappers alongside it, and the same wording is how a stax piece punishes opponents. Colossus of Sardia's second line is currently invisible to the engine.

proposals.means: strips hexproof, shroud or protection from opponents' permanents so they can be targeted
proposals.why: eff:neutralise is for turning a permanent harmless (Darksteel Mutation) and no other word covers making an untargetable permanent targetable. Arcane Lighthouse, Detection Tower, Glaring Spotlight and Shadowspear are removal ENABLERS and currently carry nothing at all for their defining ability, so the whole cycle reads as a plain mana land.

proposals.means: takes counters off one permanent and puts them on another, rather than creating or destroying them
proposals.why: add-counters plus remove-counters is the closest available and it says the wrong thing: it reads as a card that both grows things and shrinks things, when this card conserves counters and relocates them. That is a distinct job a counters deck specifically wants (rescuing counters from a permanent about to die, or piling them onto one body), and Nesting Grounds, Fain and the counter-shuffling cards share the shape.

proposals.means: Triggers when you create one or more tokens.
proposals.why: "Whenever you create a token" is the engine of the card and no trigger word covers it - trig:enters/trig:enters-other is about permanents entering, which a token does, but the printed trigger is on the CREATION and fires for tokens that enter tapped, attacking, or in other zones. The card currently records the counter and the Food but nothing about what causes them. Cluster: Rosie Cotton, Cadira Caller of the Small-style payoffs, Wand of the Worldsoul, Neyali, Bello token-matters commanders.

proposals.means: Shuts graveyards off for everyone without exiling anything - cards cannot be cast, played or returned from a graveyard.
proposals.why: eff:exile-graveyard is the only hate word and it means literally exiling cards, so Grafdigger's Cage, Rest in Peace's static cousins, Silent Gravestone and Dauthi Voidwalker-style locks either get a word that is factually false or no word at all. Nothing existing can say 'the graveyard is turned off'.

proposals.means: This creature attacks each combat if able (the -self form; a separate eff:must-attack would cover a card forcing other creatures to attack).
proposals.why: Nothing in the vocabulary says a creature is compelled to attack. eff:goad is the closest and is the opposite direction — it forces OTHER players' creatures to attack elsewhere. "Attacks each combat if able" is a real drawback a deck builder weighs (it cannot be held back as a blocker) and appears on a large family of big red and Eldrazi beaters.

proposals.means: Triggers when you scry or surveil.
proposals.why: The card's main ability is 'whenever you scry or surveil'. There is no trigger word for it - eff:scry and eff:surveil say the card DOES it, not that it is paid when you do. Scry/surveil-matters is a real archetype with a growing card pool and nothing in the vocabulary can express the payoff side.

proposals.means: the Ring tempts you, making a creature your Ring-bearer and advancing the Ring's abilities
cards: Now for Wrath, Now for Ruin!
proposals.why: The Ring tempting is a distinct mechanic with its own payoffs and enablers, and no existing word touches it. eff:add-counters and eff:player-counter are both wrong because the Ring is an emblem-like state, not a counter.

proposals.means: triggers when a player activates an activated ability
proposals.why: There is a trigger word for casting (trig:cast, trig:cast-own, trig:cast-opponent) and an effect word for stopping activation (eff:cant-activate), but nothing for an ability being activated. Wizened Mentor's whole card is that trigger and it currently produces no trigger facet at all, so the card reads as a vanilla token maker.

proposals.means: a triggered ability that fires when this creature mutates
proposals.why: Its only triggered ability is "whenever this creature mutates", and the vocabulary has no trigger word for it, so both mutate cards in this batch carry no trig: facet at all despite having a trigger. kw:mutate is the printed keyword, not the trigger.

proposals.means: the card cares about creatures' toughness rather than their power — assigning combat damage by toughness, pumping toughness as the payoff, or scaling off it
proposals.why: cares:power exists and covers the power side. The toughness side is a real, distinct Commander archetype (Doran the Siege Tower, Assault Formation, High Alert, Arcades) and nothing in the vocabulary can express it, so a deck built on it cannot be recognised or supplied.

proposals.means: Lets creatures attack that otherwise could not, chiefly by ignoring defender.
proposals.why: eff:cant-attack is the opposite and there is no word for granting permission. This is the whole card, and it is the enabler a Doran or Arcades wall deck is built on. Without it the card carries no effect word and can never be offered to the deck that wants it.

proposals.means: triggers when this permanent becomes the target of a spell or ability
proposals.why: This is the heroic and valiant archetype. trig:cast:targeting is about a spell being cast, not about a permanent being targeted, so nothing expresses the trigger these cards are built on.

proposals.means: lets a creature block when it otherwise could not, or block additional attackers: blocking while tapped, blocking any number of creatures, blocking an extra creature
proposals.why: Masako's only real line is that tapped creatures you control can still block, and her list is nothing but printed facts. grants:vigilance is a different ability, eff:force-block is the attacker forcing a block, and eff:cant-block is the opposite. Nothing expresses a widened blocking permission, which is the whole of several defensive cards.

proposals.means: the card changes a maximum hand size, either removing your own limit or shrinking an opponent's
proposals.why: Locust Miser's entire card is this, and so is half of Price of Knowledge in the same batch, plus every Reliquary Tower / Thought Vessel / Venser's Journal. It is not a discard effect - nobody discards on resolution - and today those cards carry only cares:zone:hand, which cannot tell a hand-size hoser from a card that looks at your hand.

proposals.means: The creature assigns its combat damage equal to its toughness instead of its power (Doran, Assault Formation, High Alert, Arcades, this card).
proposals.why: "Assigns combat damage equal to its toughness rather than its power" is the defining clause of a real Commander archetype and no word can say it. cares:power is the opposite claim, eff:set-pt does not apply because power and toughness are untouched, and eff:pump only says the numbers moved. Without it a toughness-matters commander can find none of its payoffs.

proposals.means: A creature can block an additional creature (or any number of creatures) each combat.
proposals.why: eff:force-block makes a creature block this one, and eff:cant-block stops blocking. Nothing says a blocker can cover more than one attacker, which is this card's entire text and the basis of a real defensive archetype (High Ground, Brave the Sands, Dueling Grounds).

proposals.means: the card is paid off by, or checks whether, you are the monarch
proposals.why: eff:set-monarch (41 cards) says a card MAKES you the monarch. Nothing says a card is PAID for being it. This card's entire ability is gated on "if you're the monarch" and that condition is currently unrecorded, so a monarch deck cannot find its own payoffs.

proposals.means: the card makes YOU sacrifice your own permanents, as an effect rather than as a cost
proposals.why: eff:sacrifice is used for edicts (Baleful Beholder in this same batch, 'each opponent sacrifices'), and cost:sacrifice is for activation costs. A repeating forced sacrifice of your own creatures is an aristocrats ENGINE, the opposite of an edict, and neither existing word says so. The -own split already exists for eff:destroy-own, eff:exile-own, eff:tap-own and eff:bounce-own.

proposals.means: Choose or name a card, then hose it - taxing it, stopping it being cast, or shutting off its abilities.
proposals.why: Nothing in the vocabulary covers naming a card. eff:choose is modal choice, eff:increase-cost and eff:cant-cast say what happens afterwards but not that the card is a targeted hate piece keyed on one named card. It is a real recurring shape (Pithing Needle, Sorcerous Spyglass, Meddling Mage, Nevermore, Runed Halo, Slaughter Games, this card) and it identifies a stax/hate cluster the engine currently cannot name.

proposals.means: Switches a creature's power and toughness rather than setting them to a stated number.
proposals.why: eff:set-pt is a fixed assignment. A switch is a distinct build-around (it pays off high-toughness creatures like Wall of Wonder and Merfolk Thaumaturgist) and reads the creature's own numbers, which set-pt never does. Roughly 40 cards. Filed as an add on set-pt only because the vocabulary has nothing closer today.

proposals.means: Opponents' spells and abilities must choose this permanent as a target if able, drawing targeted removal and other targeted effects away from your other permanents.
