proposals.why: The card's entire text is this and it carries no effect word at all. eff:redirect-spell is about pointing a spell that has already been cast somewhere else or taking it (Misdirection, Commandeer); this is a standing targeting requirement that applies while the opponent is choosing targets. eff:protect is about keeping creatures alive by granting resilience, which this does not do. eff:force-block is the same shape for combat and exists, so the vocabulary already draws this distinction on the combat side and not on the targeting side.

proposals.means: An effect (not a cost) that sacrifices the card itself.
proposals.why: cost:sacrifice-self covers paying itself as a cost. Nothing covers 'when this blocks, sacrifice it at end of combat' or Thought Dissector's 'sacrifice this artifact'. eff:sacrifice would be read as a sac outlet, which is the opposite of true - the card is the fodder, not the mouth.

proposals.means: changes the colour of a permanent or spell ("target permanent becomes white until end of turn", "creatures you control are green")
proposals.why: Aurora Griffin's whole activated ability is a colour change and the list can say nothing at all about it. eff:animate changes a permanent's TYPE, eff:set-pt changes its stats, and cares:color:* records that a card cares about a colour rather than that it alters one. Colour changing is a real cluster (Painter's Servant, Prismatic Lace, Sunlance-proofing, turning a creature a colour to dodge protection or to switch off fear/intimidate) and no existing word reaches it.

proposals.means: A static effect that lets creatures be blocked as though they did not have a named evasion ability (landwalk, swampwalk, fear, shadow, unblockability).
proposals.why: Nothing existing covers it. eff:cant-be-blocked is the opposite claim and would file this as evasion rather than as an answer to evasion. eff:neutralise is about turning one permanent into something harmless, not about a rules-level blocking permission across the board. Without a word, this card and Quagmire in this same batch both compile to nothing, so the engine can never offer either as an answer to an evasive deck.

proposals.means: A player who would begin an extra turn skips it instead, or extra turns cannot be taken.
proposals.why: Half of Trouble in Pairs is a stax effect nothing can express: eff:extra-turn means TAKING one, and eff:skip-phase is about phases within a turn. Cards like this, Stranglehold-adjacent lock pieces and Angel of Destiny-style denial belong in a control or stax plan, and today they read as pure draw engines.

proposals.means: Triggers when a player, usually an opponent, searches their library.
proposals.why: cares:zone:library says the card looks at libraries but not that it is PAID when an opponent tutors. Archivist of Oghma, Opposition Agent, Ashiok Dream Render and the other search-punishers are a real cluster and they currently read as generic lifegain-and-draw creatures, so no plan can ask for them.

proposals.means: Looks at the top N cards of your library and puts them back in any order.
proposals.why: eff:scry is look-and-bottom and eff:look-and-pick takes a card into a zone. Neither describes rearranging the top without removing anything, which is the whole of Top's first ability and of Scroll Rack, Index and Soothsaying.

proposals.means: Triggers when you create a token, as opposed to when a permanent enters.
proposals.why: trig:enters covers a permanent arriving, but this fires on creating any token including Treasure, Clue and Food, and does not fire for a nontoken creature entering. It is the token-payoff trigger and nothing in the vocabulary can say it.

proposals.means: Lets you play lands or cast spells from the top of your library.
proposals.why: eff:impulse exiles cards first and eff:play-from-graveyard is the graveyard. Neither covers the top-of-library cluster: Bolas's Citadel, Future Sight, Oracle of Mul Daya, Vizier of the Menagerie, Experimental Frenzy.

proposals.means: Strips protective or evasive keywords from permanents, usually opponents', so they can be targeted or destroyed.
proposals.why: eff:neutralise turns a permanent harmless, which is the opposite direction. Nothing says 'makes the untouchable touchable', which is what Shadowspear, Arcane Lighthouse and Glaring Spotlight do and the only reason they are played.

proposals.means: Triggers when you cast THIS spell, so the value happens even if the spell is countered.
proposals.why: trig:cast-own means "whenever you cast a [kind of] spell" and marks a spellslinger commander. Tagging Kozilek with it would misfile him. There is no word for a self-cast trigger, which is precisely what makes the Eldrazi titans, Ulamog and similar cards resilient, and that is a distinct deck-building property.

proposals.means: gives your spells improvise, so tapping artifacts pays part of their cost
proposals.why: eff:add-mana is the nearest existing word and it is not accurate: nothing adds mana, artifacts are tapped as an alternative payment. eff:reduce-cost is also wrong because the printed cost does not change. grants:convoke/grants:improvise is the same shape as the existing grants:cascade and grants:flashback.

proposals.means: Copies an activated or triggered ability rather than a spell or permanent.
proposals.why: eff:copy is spell and permanent copying, and eff:multiply-triggers is a card that automatically doubles YOUR triggers (Panharmonicon). Neither says "copy an ability on demand", which is what Rings of Brighthearth, Lithoform Engine, Strionic Resonator and Illusionist's Bracers do, and it is a distinct deck the engine cannot currently name.

proposals.means: Returns permanents to their owners' control, undoing theft, rather than taking anything.
proposals.why: eff:gain-control glosses as "steals permanents", which is the opposite claim: Homeward Path is played as an ANSWER to theft, and filing it as a theft card would put it in Gonti/Xanathar decks and out of the decks that want it. eff:give-control is also wrong - nobody hands a permanent away. The second ability currently produces no facet whatsoever.

proposals.means: Limits or stops an opponent searching their library, e.g. "searches the top four cards instead" or "players can't search libraries".
proposals.why: Aven Mindcensor's only ability produces no effect facet - it holds cares:zone:library and two printed keywords, so the engine knows it looks at libraries and not that it attacks them. Nothing existing fits: eff:cant-cast is about spells, eff:unless-pays is a tax, eff:counter is the stack. It is a real recurring cluster (Aven Mindcensor, Leonin Arbiter, Stranglehold, Ashiok Dream Render, Opposition Agent, Shadow of Doubt) and a genuine stax signal.

proposals.means: exiles a card from another player's library, hand or graveyard and lets you play or cast it
proposals.why: eff:impulse is exiling off the top of YOUR library. eff:gain-control is stealing a permanent already on the battlefield. eff:exile would file a library-theft tutor as removal, which is the exact misfiling eff:exile-graveyard was split off to avoid. Gonti, Thief of Sanity, Opposition Agent and Hostage Taker are the same shape and share no word today.

proposals.means: The card cares about cards sharing a name, whether by casting copies of the same name, counting them, or letting you run any number of them.
proposals.why: Ripple only does anything in a deck built on repeated names (Relentless Rats, Shadowborn Apostle, Persistent Petitioners), and nothing in the vocabulary can say a card is about card names. cares:sub:* names a creature type, not a name, and eff:copy is copying an object rather than matching a name.

proposals.means: Triggers when this Equipment or Aura becomes unattached from the permanent it was on.
proposals.why: trig:leaves is about leaving the battlefield and trig:zone-change about changing zones; becoming unattached is neither, and here it carries a real drawback (you sacrifice the creature). Nothing existing can say it.

proposals.means: the card's effect keys off another card's mana value being high or low
proposals.why: cares:power exists for the power axis and nothing covers the mana-value axis. mv:big and mv:cheap describe the card itself, not what it looks at. This card discounts colourless spells of mana value 7 or greater and Conduit of Ruin in the same batch tutors for one; that is the big-mana Eldrazi archetype and no word states it.

proposals.means: lets you cast spells for a payment other than their mana cost - life, an exile, a discard - rather than for free
proposals.why: eff:cast-free is glossed "without paying for it" and these cards do require payment, so it is not the same claim. This is a real recurring engine shape (this Demon, Bolas's Citadel, K'rrik, Fist of Suns, Omniscience-adjacent cards) and today the whole clause produces nothing, so a deck built around casting enchantments cheaply cannot find it.

proposals.means: Triggers whenever one or more counters are put on a permanent (or on a creature you control).
proposals.why: The vocabulary has ctr:* for what kind of counter a card uses and trig:* for events, but no trigger for counters being placed. Nest of Scarabs' only trigger is "whenever you put one or more -1/-1 counters on a creature" and it currently carries no trig: word at all, so the engine cannot tell it apart from a card that simply makes tokens. It names the whole counters-payoff family on both the +1/+1 and -1/-1 sides.

proposals.means: A continuous replacement: cards that would be put into a graveyard are exiled instead (Rest in Peace, Leyline of the Void, Planar Void, Anafenza, Necrodominance).
proposals.why: eff:exile-graveyard is a one-shot or repeated exiling of cards ALREADY in a graveyard. This stops the graveyard ever filling, which is a different card in both directions: it is the strongest graveyard hate, and it is severe anti-synergy with any deck that recurs its own cards - including, on Necrodominance, its own controller.

proposals.means: Lets creatures that have defender attack anyway, or lets a creature assign combat damage equal to its toughness instead of its power.
proposals.why: grants:defender is the opposite (it gives defender). eff:pump does not fit because no power or toughness changes. Defenders-matter is a real Commander archetype - Assault Formation, Huatli, Rolling Stones, High Alert - and no existing word can say a card turns walls into attackers, so every card in that archetype is invisible to the builder.

proposals.means: triggers when a permanent you control is destroyed by an opponent's spell or ability
proposals.why: trig:dies covers creatures dying and trig:leaves is any departure from the battlefield, including your own blinks and sacrifices. This card's whole condition is a punisher clause on an opponent DESTROYING a noncreature permanent, and no word distinguishes being destroyed by an opponent from leaving for any other reason.

proposals.means: Triggers when one or more cards are put into a graveyard from a library (milled), whether by you or anyone.
proposals.why: The vocabulary has trig:draws-card, trig:gains-life and trig:loses-life for event triggers of this shape, and eff:mill for doing it, but nothing for BEING PAID when milling happens. This card's second ability is entirely that, and it is the payoff half of every mill deck (Bruvac-style self-mill payoffs, Zombie makers off mill). cares:zone:graveyard is the closest existing word and it only says the card looks at graveyards, not that it triggers.

proposals.means: Strips hexproof, shroud, protection and ward from permanents an opponent controls so they can be targeted.
proposals.why: The first ability's entire purpose and there is no word for it. eff:neutralise turns a permanent harmless, which is the opposite direction; grants:* only adds keywords. This is the Arcane Lighthouse / Glaring Spotlight effect that makes an otherwise dead removal spell live, and a deck holding hexproof commanders genuinely wants it.

proposals.means: Triggers when a player discards a card.
proposals.why: Direct parallel to the existing trig:draws-card, and nothing covers it. Bag of Holding, Containment Construct, Archfiend of Ifnir and the rummaging payoffs all key off the discard event, which is a real archetype and currently unsayable.

proposals.means: Gives cards foretell that do not have it.
proposals.why: grants: already covers granted non-evergreen keywords (grants:flashback, grants:escape, grants:retrace, grants:embalm). Nothing records that a card hands foretell out, and cares:kw:foretell is the payoff side, not the granting side - Dream Devourer is the card that makes a foretell deck possible at all.

proposals.means: Triggers whenever you roll one or more dice.
proposals.why: The card's first ability produces no trigger word. Dice-rolling is a real Commander archetype (Wyll, Farideh, Vrondiss and the AFR/Baldur's Gate cards) and eff:random only records the act of rolling, never a payoff that watches for it.

proposals.means: Makes a permanent an artifact in addition to its other types.
proposals.why: eff:animate covers turning a permanent into a CREATURE, which is a different claim, and no word covers changing a permanent's type to artifact. It is the enabler for artifact removal aimed at lands and for artifact-count payoffs (Liquimetal Coating, Liquimetal Torque, Karn, March of the Machines), and without it this card compiles to nothing.

proposals.means: You take the initiative (the Undercity mechanic), the way eff:set-monarch records becoming the monarch.
proposals.why: eff:set-monarch already exists for the parallel mechanic and initiative has none, so the entire first ability of every initiative card reads as blank. It is not a counter, a token or a trigger, so nothing else can express it.

proposals.means: Forces each opponent (or each player) to sacrifice a permanent of their own choice.
proposals.why: eff:sacrifice covers both a sacrifice outlet you use on your own board (Ruthless Lawbringer, Ashnod's Altar) and an edict aimed at opponents, which are opposite cards for deck building - one is an aristocrats engine, the other is removal that beats hexproof. eff:destroy does not fit either, because the opponent chooses. Both Braids and Barrensteppe Siege in this batch need it.

proposals.means: Players cannot sacrifice permanents, or pay life, to cast spells or activate abilities.
proposals.why: eff:cant-cast stops spells outright and eff:cant-activate stops activated abilities outright; neither is true here. This is a cost restriction that shuts off sacrifice outlets and fetch lands while leaving everything else legal. It is the defining half of the card and nothing in the vocabulary can say it, so the engine currently reads Angel of Jubilation as a plain anthem.

proposals.means: the card takes the initiative
proposals.why: eff:set-monarch exists for the monarch, which is the same shape of shared-designation mechanic; initiative has no word, so these cards carry nothing for their headline ability.

proposals.means: triggers when you commit a crime (target an opponent, something they control, or a card in their graveyard)
proposals.why: Crime is a named, printed triggering condition on a whole cycle of cards and no word covers it. trig:cast:targeting is about a spell you cast targeting something, which is narrower and misses activated abilities and attack triggers that commit crimes.

proposals.means: the restriction on casting applies to this permanent's own controller, not to opponents
proposals.why: eff:cant-cast is a stax word - it means you are stopping THEM. Steel Golem stops YOU casting creature spells, which is a drawback on a cheap beater and the opposite kind of card. A deck builder reading the shared word will offer Steel Golem as an opponent-hoser. This is the same controller split the vocabulary already draws with eff:exile-own, eff:tap-own and eff:damage-self.

proposals.means: the card triggers whenever you proliferate
proposals.why: There is no way to say a card is a PROLIFERATE PAYOFF. eff:proliferate would be actively wrong here - this card never proliferates, it is paid when you do. The drain and the lifegain are recorded but nothing says what sets them off, so a proliferate deck cannot find it. Atraxa-style decks are the whole audience for the card.

proposals.means: gives creatures the afterlife keyword, so they leave a Spirit token behind when they die
proposals.why: grants:* already spans the keyword space, and there is no entry for afterlife. Without it this card reads as a one-mana cantrip: the reason a player casts it in response to a wrath is entirely unrecorded.

proposals.means: stops players searching their libraries
proposals.why: The card carried no effect word of any kind. Nothing in the vocabulary covers library denial: eff:cant-cast is spells and eff:cant-activate is activated abilities. It is a real and recognised stax axis (Aven Mindcensor, Stranglehold, Opposition Agent, Ashiok Dream Render) and every one of those cards is currently silent about its main ability.

proposals.means: Triggers when a creature attacks YOU or a planeswalker you control, rather than when this card attacks.
proposals.why: trig:attacks is used throughout this batch only for 'whenever this creature/Vehicle attacks' (TARDIS, Witch-king, Steel-Plume Marshal), so applying it here would file a defensive pillowfort card as an aggro attack payoff. This card currently carries NO trigger word at all because the vocabulary cannot express the direction. Same shape as the existing trig:cast-own / trig:cast-opponent split.

proposals.means: Exiles or takes a CARD an opponent owns (from hand, library or graveyard) and lets you cast or play it.
proposals.why: eff:gain-control is for permanents already on the battlefield, and eff:impulse is specifically your own cards off the top of your own library. Neither covers taking an opponent's cards and casting them, which is the whole of Intellect Devourer, Gonti, Thief of Sanity, Xanathar and Etali. The card currently says only that it exiles something, not that the exiled cards are yours to cast.

proposals.means: Changes or restricts what mana permanents produce, rather than adding mana itself.
proposals.why: eff:add-mana is for producing mana, eff:cant-cast is about spells and eff:increase-cost is taxing. Nothing covers Contamination, Blood Moon, Infernal Darkness or Harbinger of the Seas, which are a real mana-denial archetype and currently read as cards that do nothing.

proposals.means: Makes permanents lose hexproof, shroud, protection or indestructible so they can be targeted or destroyed.
proposals.why: The vocabulary has grants:hexproof, grants:shroud, grants:protection and grants:indestructible but nothing for taking them away. Arcane Lighthouse, Detection Tower, Glaring Spotlight and this card exist purely to make an untouchable board answerable, and they currently record nothing at all for that clause.

proposals.means: Changes a player's maximum hand size, in either direction.
proposals.why: The card's entire text is 'each opponent's maximum hand size is reduced by one' and it currently carries no effect word whatsoever. Nothing existing fits: it does not make anyone discard on resolution, and eff:discard would be wrong. The same word covers the other side, Reliquary Tower and Thought Vessel, which are real payoffs for wheel and mass-draw decks and are equally unreadable today.

proposals.means: triggers when you roll a die, or on a particular result
cards: Night Shift of the Living Dead
proposals.why: eff:random says the card makes a roll happen; nothing says a card is PAID when a roll happens. "Whenever you roll a 6" is the payoff half of the dice archetype (this card, and the AFR and Wilds of Eldraine dice commanders), and without it a dice deck cannot find its own payoffs.

proposals.means: Cards in graveyards cannot be put onto the battlefield - a static prohibition on reanimation, not a removal of the cards themselves.
proposals.why: Kunoros exiles nothing, so eff:exile-graveyard is factually false, and eff:cant-cast covers only the second half ("Players can't cast spells from graveyards"). The first half, "Creature cards in graveyards can't enter the battlefield", has no word at all. This is the Kunoros / Rest in Peace-adjacent lock effect: real graveyard hate that works by prohibition rather than by exile. Ground Seal, Silent Gravestone and Leyline of the Void's non-exile cousins are the same shape.

proposals.means: the outcome of the effect is decided by an opponent's choice, guess or vote (punisher effects, Fact or Fiction, 'an opponent guesses/chooses')
proposals.why: eff:choose is YOU picking a mode. Nothing says the opposite: that the card hands the decision to an opponent, which changes how the card plays entirely. Browbeat, Vexing Devil, Fact or Fiction and this card share that shape.

proposals.means: a triggered ability that fires when you unlock this door
proposals.why: Both halves of every Room card trigger on "When you unlock this door". Unlocking is not entering: the second door is unlocked later while the permanent is already on the battlefield, so trig:enters cannot stand in for it. Room cards currently have their triggers compile to nothing, which is why this card carried only two words for two whole abilities.

proposals.means: lets you pay life in place of a spell's mana cost
proposals.why: The card's entire ability produced no effect word. cost:life is a cost on this card's own ability, not permission to pay life for OTHER spells, and eff:reduce-cost is a different claim - paying life equal to mana value is not cheaper mana, it is a different currency. K'rrik, Son of Yawgmoth and Bolas's Citadel are the same shape and are built around; nothing in the vocabulary can say it.

proposals.means: Exiles cards from YOUR OWN graveyard, as a cost or as an effect, rather than from an opponent's.
cards: Egon, God of Death // Throne of Death
proposals.why: eff:exile-graveyard is defined as graveyard hate and is used to keep hate out of graveyard decks. Egon exiles two cards from his own graveyard every upkeep and exiles a creature card from it to draw; Ashnod, Flesh Mechanist in this same batch does the same as an activation cost. These are graveyard PAYOFFS and tagging them with the hate word would score them against the very decks that want them, so the effect currently has to be left unrecorded entirely.

proposals.means: stops triggered abilities from triggering
proposals.why: The card's entire text is unrepresented: it has only kw:flash, kw:flying and scope:all. eff:cant-activate covers activated abilities and eff:cant-cast covers spells, neither of which is a triggered ability, and eff:multiply-triggers already exists as the exact inverse.

proposals.means: the card looks for, or pays off, creatures that have toxic
proposals.why: cares:kw:* exists for flying, deathtouch, lifelink, reach and a dozen more, but not toxic. The Raptor's whole trigger reads "another target creature you control with toxic", which nothing in the list can say, so a toxic deck cannot find it.

proposals.means: the card counts, or is bounded by, how much life a player lost this turn
proposals.why: cares:lifegain exists for the other direction and trig:loses-life covers the trigger, but nothing says a card SCALES with life already lost. Mortarion's X can never exceed the life you lost this turn, so half his text is unsayable.

proposals.means: Triggers when one or more counters are put on this permanent.
proposals.why: There is no trigger word for a counter being placed. This is a common shape in +1/+1 counter decks (adapt, evolve and proliferate payoffs) and the closest existing words are eff:add-counters / cost:add-counters, which describe PUTTING a counter rather than being PAID when one arrives - the opposite direction.

proposals.means: Replaces losing the game so that you do not lose - Angel's Grace, Lich's Mirror and similar.
proposals.why: The reason this card exists ("the next time you would lose the game this turn, instead...") is unrecorded and unrecordable. eff:lose-game and eff:win-game already exist at 15 and 25 cards, so a word for the third state at a comparable count is consistent rather than a synonym for either.

proposals.means: A triggered ability that fires when this permanent turns to its other face ("When this creature transforms into ~, ...").
proposals.why: The back face's edict is gated on a transform trigger and there is no trigger word for it. trig:enters is wrong (transforming is not entering), and cares:kw:transform / kw:transform are printed markers that say the card CAN transform, not that something happens when it does. Roughly 60+ double-faced cards carry a transform trigger and every one of them currently loses its trigger entirely.

proposals.means: You may activate loyalty (or other) abilities more times each turn than the rules allow.
proposals.why: Chapter III is the whole payoff of the card and nothing expresses it. eff:multiply doubles an effect and eff:multiply-triggers doubles triggers; neither is a permission to activate again. This is the Oath of Teferi / The Chain Veil superfriends effect.

proposals.means: Triggers when this Vehicle becomes crewed.
proposals.why: Not an attack, an enters, or a tap of this permanent - the event is other creatures being tapped to crew it, and it can happen at instant speed outside combat. Vehicles are a supported archetype and 'becomes crewed' payoffs are its whole reward structure; kw:crew only says the card HAS crew, not that it is paid for crewing.

proposals.means: Triggers when you give a gift (the Gift mechanic on a spell or permanent).
proposals.why: The card's ONLY trigger condition is "whenever you give a gift" and no trig: word covers it. Gift is not a cast, an enter, a dies or a step trigger, so nothing existing can say when this card draws.

proposals.means: the card cares about a die roll or coin flip made elsewhere, rather than making one itself (Xenosquirrels, Barbarian Class, Wyll Blade of Frontiers, Farideh)
proposals.why: eff:random means the card itself flips or rolls; there is no word for a card that is a payoff for rolling, so the whole dice-matters archetype is invisible

proposals.means: Triggers when this creature crews a Vehicle or saddles a Mount.
proposals.why: Canyon Vaulter's only ability is this trigger and no facet expresses it, so the card reads as having no trigger at all. trig:tapped is a different event (crewing taps the creature but the trigger is on the crewing, and a Vehicle crewed by other creatures does not fire it).

proposals.means: Life you would gain becomes something else instead (cards, counters, damage), rather than being gained.
proposals.why: cares:lifegain says the card watches lifegain and eff:draw says it draws, but neither says the two are the SAME event replaced. Alhammarret's Archive doubles gain, Nefarious Lich and Rhox Faithmender-style replacers convert it, and Sulfuric Vortex stops it entirely - the vocabulary cannot tell a lifegain deck's payoff from a lifegain deck's off-switch.

proposals.means: Lifts a restriction on attacking - creatures with defender may attack, or creatures that could not attack may.
proposals.why: grants:defender is the opposite claim, eff:cant-attack stops a creature attacking, and eff:pump does not apply because no stats change. There is no word in the vocabulary for REMOVING an attack restriction, so Rolling Stones, Assault Formation, Warmonger's Chariot and the Huatli-style "walls can attack" cards carry no effect word at all and can be chosen for nothing.

proposals.means: makes ACTIVATED ability costs cheaper - equip, ninjutsu, unearth, level up, activated abilities generally - as opposed to eff:reduce-cost, which is about casting spells.
proposals.why: "Equip costs you pay cost {1} less" is a real, deck-defining effect for Equipment decks (Auriok Steelshaper, Puresteel Paladin's cousins, Brass Squire-style enablers) and the vocabulary cannot say it. eff:reduce-cost is not a synonym: it is about SPELLS and is consumed as a ramp-ish signal, so applying it here would say this card accelerates your mana, which it does not - it never makes a spell cheaper.

proposals.means: the card checks whether a permanent left the battlefield under your control this turn, or cares that one did
proposals.why: trig:leaves is a trigger, and this is a condition checked on resolution. Nothing in the vocabulary can say 'this is better in a deck that sacrifices or blinks its own permanents' for a non-triggered check like 'if a creature left the battlefield under your control this turn'.

proposals.means: Returns a permanent to its owner's hand, whoever controls it (Boomerang, Cyclonic Rift, this card).
proposals.why: The vocabulary only has eff:bounce-own, which is a blink-adjacent value effect on YOUR side. A generic return-to-hand is one of the format's main answers and currently has to hide inside eff:move-zone, which also covers milling, exiling and graveyard shuffling.

proposals.means: Lets you cast cards from exile that this card or another effect put there, rather than from your hand.
proposals.why: eff:impulse is specifically exiling off the top of your library to play it, and eff:cast-from-graveyard is the graveyard. An exile-and-recast engine like this, Prosper-style repeatable exile casting, or a card that stores creatures under itself has no word, so it currently reads as a card that does nothing.

proposals.means: the card checks for, counts or uses tokens you control as a resource or a condition
proposals.why: tok:* says what a card MAKES; nothing says a card cares about tokens it did not make. "Tap two untapped tokens you control" is a token-matters payoff and is currently invisible, so a token deck cannot be pointed at it. It is not a synonym for eff:create-token, which is the opposite direction.

proposals.means: gives permanents an additional creature type
proposals.why: Hivestone, Xenograft, Arcane Adaptation, Conspiracy and Maskwood Nexus all do one thing and the vocabulary cannot say it. eff:animate is a different claim (a noncreature BECOMING a creature); this changes what type a creature already is, and it is the enabler card of every tribal deck whose commander names a tribe.

proposals.means: Gives permanents a creature type they were not printed with, e.g. "each creature you control is a Vampire in addition to its other creature types".
proposals.why: This is the enabler a tribal deck reaches for when it does not have enough real members (Arcane Adaptation, Xenograft, Conspiracy, Mephidross Vampire). Nothing covers it: every grants: word is a keyword ability, grants:changeling is a specific printed keyword, and eff:animate is turning a noncreature into a creature, not changing a creature's tribe.

proposals.means: lets you target permanents or players that have hexproof or shroud as though they did not have it
proposals.why: Kaya's static ability is the whole reason to play her and no word touches it. eff:neutralise is about changing a permanent, eff:protect is about shielding your own, and cares:kw:hexproof would say the deck WANTS hexproof, which is backwards. Arcane Lighthouse, Detection Tower, Glaring Spotlight and Shadowspear are the same shape and all currently read as answering nothing.

proposals.means: Changes what colour or type of mana a permanent produces when it is tapped, instead of producing mana itself.
proposals.why: eff:add-mana says a card is a mana source, which this is not - it produces nothing and taxes you every upkeep. Its whole function is that every land in the game produces {B} instead, which is mana denial and a stax effect, the opposite of ramp. Nothing in the vocabulary distinguishes altering someone else's mana production from making mana, so Contamination-shaped cards currently read as either blank or as accelerants.

proposals.means: triggers when one or more counters are put on this permanent
proposals.why: The whole third line is "whenever one or more +1/+1 counters are put on this creature" and no trigger word covers a counter being placed. trig:tapped, trig:untapped and trig:dealt-damage all exist for comparable event shapes; this one is the counters-matters payoff shape (Fathom Mage, Simic Ascendancy) and is currently invisible.

proposals.means: the card gives a protective keyword to ITSELF only, not to your other creatures
proposals.why: There is no way to separate Swiftfoot Boots, which keeps your commander alive, from Veteran Survivor, Paradise Druid and Syr Ginger, which say "this creature has hexproof" about themselves and protect nothing else. Using grants:hexproof for both makes every self-hexproof creature look like an equipment-grade protection card. The -self convention already exists for exactly this distinction on cost:sacrifice-self, eff:exile-self and trig:enters-self.

proposals.means: the card is paid off by, or triggers on, you surveilling
proposals.why: "Whenever you surveil" is a trigger on a mechanic, and there is no word for it. cares:kw:cycling, cares:kw:foretell and cares:kw:vote already exist at this scale, so the shape is established; surveil-matters is a real Dimir archetype and nothing in the list can currently express it.

proposals.means: the creature may block more than one attacker each combat
proposals.why: "Can block an additional creature each combat" is a real granted ability with no word available. eff:force-block and eff:cant-block cover being made to block and being stopped from blocking, but neither says a blocker covers two attackers, which is what makes cards like this and Sunweb defensive pieces.

proposals.means: Puts a card onto the battlefield face down as a 2/2 creature that can be turned face up later. Covers manifest, manifest dread, cloak and disguise.
proposals.why: eff:create-token is factually wrong here - a manifested card is a real card, not a token, and it can be turned face up for value. Nothing in the vocabulary distinguishes making a body from your library out of a real card from stamping out a token, and roughly sixty printed cards do it.

proposals.means: Puts -1/-1 counters on, or otherwise shrinks, your OWN creatures.
proposals.why: Blight 2 puts two -1/-1 counters on a creature you control. Plain eff:shrink would file this as removal, which is the opposite of what it does; the -own convention already exists for eff:tap-own, eff:destroy-own, eff:exile-own and eff:bounce-own, and this is the same distinction.

proposals.means: Triggers when this permanent is turned face up from being face down, the morph and megamorph payoff trigger.
proposals.why: Nothing in the vocabulary can say it. trig:enters is wrong because the permanent is already on the battlefield; eff:transform is an effect that flips something else, not a trigger on being flipped; kw:morph is a printed fact saying the card HAS morph, not that anything happens when it turns up. Master of Pearls' entire payoff, a mass +2/+2 on being unmorphed, currently hangs off no trigger at all, so the engine cannot tell it apart from a card that pumps on cast.

proposals.means: the card is paid off, or discounted, by how many cards you have drawn this turn
proposals.why: trig:draws-card is a trigger that fires on each draw; this is a threshold CONDITION ("if you've drawn three or more cards this turn") checked when the ability is activated. Nothing expresses the draw-two-matters payoff shape, which is a real blue-black archetype, so the whole reason this card is played is unsayable.

proposals.means: counters can no longer be put on a permanent or a player, ongoing while this is around
proposals.why: eff:remove-counters says the counters go away once; the lasting prohibition is a separate, load-bearing effect (Solemnity, Melira, Vizier of Remedies, this card) and it is what makes these cards hate pieces rather than a one-shot. eff:cant-cast / eff:cant-activate / eff:cant-block are the existing prohibitions for other actions, so this fits the pattern rather than duplicating anything.

proposals.means: The card counts, rewards or cleans up creatures that are goaded, rather than goading them itself.
proposals.why: "investigate for each goaded creature you control. Then each creature you control is no longer goaded" - the payoff scales off how many of your creatures are goaded. eff:goad is the opposite direction (forcing creatures to attack elsewhere) and would be wrong here. Goad is a real Commander archetype and nothing in the vocabulary can express its payoff side.

proposals.means: Gives a permanent an additional creature type it did not print with.
proposals.why: 'is an Angel in addition to its other types' is unsayable today. eff:animate is turning a noncreature into a creature, which is a different thing. This is a real and useful cluster for tribal decks: Call to Serve, Xenograft, Arcane Adaptation, Conspiracy, Maskwood Nexus, Kindred Discovery's cousins. A tribal deck genuinely wants these cards and nothing can currently find them.

proposals.means: The card checks whether a creature died this turn (or earlier in the turn) as a condition on a trigger or effect, without itself being the trigger for the death.
proposals.why: trig:dies is wrong - nothing here triggers on a creature dying, it triggers on entering and then LOOKS BACK at whether a death happened. cares:zone:graveyard is also wrong, because the card never touches a graveyard. This is the morbid/'if a creature died this turn' condition, a real aristocrats payoff shape with no word in the vocabulary.

proposals.means: strips a card out of a player's hand to exile rather than to the graveyard
proposals.why: eff:discard is the graveyard version and is rules-wrong here; eff:exile reads as battlefield removal. Hand attack that dodges the graveyard is a distinct thing a deck wants.

proposals.means: Triggers when this creature attacks and is not blocked
proposals.why: "Attacks and isn't blocked" is a different event from trig:attacks: it only pays off when evasion works, so these cards want unblockable-matters support rather than go-wide attack support. trig:attacks fires on a creature that gets chumped, trig:deals-damage fires on a blocked creature that tramples through, and neither says this.

proposals.means: Replaces the amount of damage a source would deal with a fixed amount, in either direction.
proposals.why: eff:prevent-damage stops damage, eff:redirect-damage moves it to another recipient, and eff:multiply doubles or triples it. This card sets any nonzero damage to exactly 2, so it raises small hits and shrinks large ones at once. No existing word can say that, and calling it eff:multiply would be false for every source dealing 3 or more.

proposals.means: Names a card and removes every copy of it from a player's hand, graveyard and library at once.
proposals.why: Two cards in this batch alone (Lost Legacy, Eradicate) plus Cranial Extraction, Praetor's Grasp and Memoricide do this. eff:exile plus eff:exile-graveyard describes the mechanics but not the effect, which is stripping a named card from a whole deck — a distinct answer that nothing existing names.

proposals.means: triggers when this Equipment or Aura becomes attached to a permanent
proposals.why: eff:attach records the act of attaching, but there is no trigger word for a card that is PAID when it becomes attached. Real and recurring: Hammer of Nazahn, Kaldra Compleat, Sword of Forge and Frontier, this card. Nothing in trig:* covers it.

proposals.means: the card checks whether it is itself enchanted or equipped
proposals.why: cares:sub:aura and cares:sub:equipment say a card cares about those card types in general. Nothing says a CREATURE is paid for being suited up, which is exactly what a Voltron deck is shopping for (Novice Knight, Kor Duelist, Ardenvale Tactician-style bodies). As it stands this card carries no judgement word at all and can be chosen by nothing.

proposals.means: The card can regenerate a creature, giving it a repeatable shield against destruction.
proposals.why: kw:regenerate is only the printed keyword. No effect word says the card KEEPS something alive this way: grants:indestructible is a different, permanent thing, and eff:protect is used for protection tricks. A recurring regeneration engine is a real resilience effect the facet vocabulary cannot state.

proposals.means: You may spend mana as though it were mana of any color (for some or all spells). Colour-requirement relaxation, not mana production.
proposals.why: The card's entire second ability is unrepresented. eff:add-mana is about producing mana and is false here - this makes existing mana castable. cares:color:* says a colour matters. Celestial Dawn, Cascading Cataracts, Sunglasses of Urza, Fist of Suns and every 'spend mana as though' card is silent on this.

proposals.means: an opponent, and only an opponent, draws cards; you do not
proposals.why: eff:draw reads as card advantage for you, so a group-hug gift like this is filed in the draw role and offered to a deck wanting card draw - the exact fault the effect.who split fixed for Temple Bell. eff:draw-each is symmetric and does not fit either: here you draw nothing. There is no word for a one-sided gift to somebody else, which is a real Commander archetype (political and pillowfort cards).

proposals.means: The card checks whether a creature died this turn as a condition, rather than triggering on the death itself.
proposals.why: Morbid and the 'if a creature died this turn' clause are a condition, not a trigger, so trig:dies is wrong for them, and cares:zone:graveyard is about the zone rather than the event. This is a real aristocrats payoff signal across morbid cards and the wider 'if a creature died this turn' wording, and it is the exact sibling of cares:lifegain, which already exists for the same shape on the life side.

proposals.means: Lets mana already in your pool be spent as though it were a different colour or type. Changes what mana can pay for, without producing any mana.
proposals.why: The card's entire text is unrecorded - it has only col:none and type:artifact. eff:add-mana is the only mana word and it is wrong here: Sunglasses produces no mana at all. Celestial Dawn, Sunglasses of Urza and the fixing cycle all do this and none of them can currently say anything.

proposals.means: This creature is required to block each combat if able, or must be blocked - a compulsion on itself rather than on other creatures.
proposals.why: eff:force-block is the opposite direction: its gloss is "forces a creature to block IT", which is lure (Provoke, "all creatures able to block this do so"). Nothing in the vocabulary says a creature must itself block every combat, which is a real defensive drawback-or-asset on Watchdog, Wall of Nets-style blockers and the Guard/Defender family, and matters to pillow-fort and defender decks.

proposals.means: Names a card and removes every copy of it from a player's hand, library and graveyard, usually by exiling them.
proposals.why: eff:discard puts cards in the graveyard where they can be recurred, and eff:exile-graveyard is graveyard hate only. Neither says "this card takes a specific card out of an opponent's deck permanently", which is what Necromentia, Lost Legacy, Unmoored Ego, Memoricide, Sadistic Sacrament and Praetor's Grasp all do. It is a distinct job (combo hate) that no existing word can express.

proposals.means: the card gives ITSELF negative power/toughness, as a cost or drawback, rather than shrinking something else
proposals.why: eff:shrink is the removal word - it confers the removal role. This card shrinks only itself to gain flying, so reading it as removal is a false positive of exactly the kind cost:sacrifice-self, eff:exile-self and eff:damage-self already exist to prevent. Nothing in the vocabulary distinguishes the two directions.

proposals.means: the card gives a protective keyword to ITSELF only, not to your other creatures - the -self counterpart of the grants: family (also grants:hexproof-self, grants:indestructible-self)
proposals.why: A bare grants: word makes a card read as a protection PIECE for the deck. A Thopter that gives only itself shroud protects nothing else, and the same shape misreads Paradise Druid, Shimmer Dragon and Syr Ginger, which say 'this creature has hexproof' about themselves. cost:sacrifice-self and eff:exile-self set the precedent for splitting direction into its own word.

proposals.means: Exiles a card an opponent owns (from hand, library or graveyard) and lets you play or cast it.
proposals.why: eff:impulse is specifically your own library's top cards, and eff:gain-control is a permanent already on the battlefield. Neither covers taking a card out of someone else's hand or library and casting it yourself, which is a real recurring effect (Gonti, Thief of Sanity, Hostage Taker, Muse Vessel) and a genuine theft archetype. Today those cards carry only cares:zone:exile, which says what they look at and not what they do.

proposals.means: changes the colour of mana a source produces, or lets mana be spent as though it were another colour
proposals.why: eff:add-mana says a card PRODUCES mana. Nothing in the vocabulary says a card converts or unlocks colours already being produced, which is a real and distinct deck-building job: False Dawn, Celestial Dawn, Chromatic Lantern, Sunglasses of Urza, Mycosynth Lattice. These are the cards a five-colour or off-colour deck is built on and today they carry only eff:draw or nothing.

proposals.means: deals damage to a creature YOU control
proposals.why: eff:damage would file this as removal, which is wrong - it can only hit "another creature you control". eff:damage-self is damage to YOU the player, not to your board. The -own convention already exists for eff:exile-own, eff:destroy-own, eff:bounce-own and eff:tap-own, and this is the same distinction for damage: Wicked Guardian, Vampire Aristocrat-style ping-your-own effects, and the cards that damage your own creature to trigger something.

proposals.means: the card is switched on by you having discarded a card this turn, or cares that a discard happened
proposals.why: "Activate only if you've discarded a card this turn" is the entire reason this card is played, and the vocabulary has only eff:discard, eff:discard-self, cost:discard and cost:discard-self - four words for MAKING a discard happen and none for being PAID when one has. That is a genuine archetype (madness, hellbent, Containment Construct, Bone Miser, Anje's payoffs) which currently cannot be asked for by any plan. Everything else on this card is correct.

proposals.means: Returns a land you control to your hand.
proposals.why: eff:bounce-own is documented as narrowed to creatures returning to hand, so it must not be widened back to lands. Landfall and land-ETB decks specifically want this effect (Tazeem Raptor, Meloku, Trade Routes, Storm Cauldron) and nothing in the vocabulary can say it.

proposals.means: The card's size or effect scales with your party (up to one each of Cleric, Rogue, Warrior and Wizard).
proposals.why: Party is a real deckbuilding constraint - it wants four specific creature classes rather than one tribe - and no existing word expresses it. cares:sub:* names one subtype at a time and would need four of them to approximate a mechanic that is really about holding one of each; cares:power and the type words say nothing about it.

proposals.means: Triggers at end of combat.
proposals.why: trig:step has begin-combat, upkeep, draw, both mains and end step, and no end of combat. This card's only ability triggers there and carries no trig: word at all; Stoic Ephemera in the same batch is the same gap.

proposals.means: The card only works on, or is paid for by, permanents that are already tapped or untapped - a targeting restriction or condition on tap state rather than an effect that taps.
proposals.why: The Wasp can only shoot a TAPPED creature an opponent controls, which makes her a payoff in a deck full of tappers and a blank in one without. trig:tapped covers a trigger fired BY something tapping, and eff:tap covers doing the tapping; neither says a card cares that a permanent is already in that state.

proposals.means: players cannot play lands, or lands cannot enter the battlefield
proposals.why: eff:cant-cast is about spells and a land is played, not cast; eff:cant-activate and eff:extra-land-drop cover neither direction of this. Land denial is the whole of this card's first two lines and nothing in the vocabulary can say it.

proposals.means: The permanent demands a recurring payment every upkeep and is destroyed, sacrificed or lost if you decline. Covers cumulative upkeep, echo, and "at the beginning of your upkeep, destroy/sacrifice this unless you pay X".
proposals.why: Nothing existing says a card taxes you every turn to stay on the battlefield. cost:* words are all one-off activation or casting costs, eff:unless-pays taxes an OPPONENT, and eff:do-if-cost-paid describes an optional bonus rather than a maintenance fee. This is a real recurring liability a deck builder should be able to see, and it is what makes cards like this and the echo cycle play far worse than their stats suggest.

proposals.means: Makes a player reveal their hand or play with their hand revealed for a duration.
proposals.why: cares:zone:hand only says the card looks at the hand zone; nothing records that it EXPOSES an opponent's hand as an ongoing effect. Telepathy, Glasses of Urza and this card share that shape and currently carry no verb.

proposals.means: Taps a permanent and keeps it from untapping during its controller's untap step, rather than tapping it for a single turn.
proposals.why: eff:tap covers a one-turn tap. A permanent that never untaps is a different card entirely (a stax/lockdown piece rather than a combat trick), and Mole Worms, Dungeon Geists, Sleep and Frost Breath cannot be told apart from Icy Manipulator today.

proposals.means: Triggers when day becomes night or night becomes day.
proposals.why: No trig: word covers the day//night cycle. trig:step is about phases within a turn; this fires on a game-state flip that can happen on any player's turn, and the whole daybound/nightbound archetype hangs on it.

proposals.means: Fetches a card from outside the game (sideboard or collection) rather than from a zone in the game.
proposals.why: eff:search-library is wrong (no library is searched) and eff:move-zone understates it. A wish is a tutor with no deck-building cost, which is a distinct thing for the engine to reason about.

proposals.means: Keeps a permanent from untapping during its controller's untap step, so a tap becomes a lasting lock rather than a one-turn effect.
proposals.why: eff:tap only says it turns something sideways; it cannot distinguish a Sleep or a Dungeon Geists, which takes a blocker out of the game for good, from a one-shot tapper. Nothing in the vocabulary expresses the permanence.

proposals.means: The card's effect keys on a creature being face down, or on it being turned face up.
proposals.why: 'When enchanted creature is turned face up, destroy it' is the entire trigger of this Aura and nothing expresses it, so the card reads as an unconditional destroy Aura, which it is not. Aven Soulgazer in the same batch ('Look at target face-down creature') has the same gap. The cares:kw:* family already exists for keywords the card looks at (cares:kw:flying, cares:kw:cycling, cares:kw:transform), and cares:kw:transform is a different mechanic - transforming a double-faced permanent is not turning a morph face up.

proposals.means: lets a creature block more creatures than usual this combat or each combat
proposals.why: The second sentence, "That creature can block up to two additional creatures this turn", is a real defensive mechanic with no word. eff:force-block is the opposite direction (compelling a block), eff:cant-block forbids blocking, and grants:* only carries printed keywords. Brave the Sands and the several creatures reading "can block an additional creature each combat" are the same shape and are currently silent about it.
